forensics.lens: Data-platform Architect — provenance, the ADR-077 reset contract, and the honesty of served numbers (ADR-104/105)
forensics.the_70_question: From this lens the answer is arithmetic before it is process. The reset is not a rare event: CYCLE_GENESES (lambdas/web/site_api_data.py:104-124) records 12 resets in the 55 days from 2026-07-12 to 2026-09-05 — the platform's single most frequent state transition — while docs/PROPORTIONALITY.md row 86 sizes the reset machinery for something that "runs once per RESET, which is a few times a quarter". Every piece of reset verification was therefore built for an exceptional day and then exercised weekly, and it is one-sided. ADR-077 is a READ contract: with_phase_filter is imported by 76 files, singleton_visible by 34, and three generations of ratchets (#946/#1085/#1200 singletons; #2109/#2150/#3444 readers) guard the reader set. The WRITER side has no contract with the reset at all: 112 files in lambdas/ call put_item/update_item, 26 of them stamp provenance (experiment_stamp/tag_record); the only set guard (test_coach_ensemble_writer_phase_stamp_guard_2119) covers COACH#/ENSEMBLE# put_item only; phase_taxonomy.py:41-43 states that every other scoped writer "still rel[ies] on the wipe/tagger for provenance"; and 31 writer-direction seams on EXPERIMENT_SCOPED partitions sit in tests/pair_seam_residue.py as dated exemptions — charter rule 3 converted the missing contract into accepted debt with no countdown. The reset's own verification then asserts only what the READ side serves, once, at T0: rendered 96 URLs, semantic 8 API checks plus ONE DDB check that sweeps taxonomy.RAW_TIMESERIES_SOURCES (restart_verify_semantic.py:350) and never the scoped partitions the wipe just tombstoned, and an AI truth pass — all before the first scheduled writer runs (the chronicle sweep at 18:00Z, ~10h later). The only writer-side check, restart_verify check 14 (the countdown sweep), is attended: it is referenced by no workflow, no CDK schedule and no operating-calendar ritual; #3390's cycle-15 runlist "was never executed and now cannot be"; and until #3488 its sanctioned_reason() exempted every live write carrying the current cycle stamp — 56 of 73 rows on Day 0 — so the one instrument built for the class reported zero by construction, and its own unit test (the since-replaced test_current_cycle_stamp… case) asserted the blind rule. So the review found, on Day 0 at ~17:00Z, exactly what the reset structurally cannot see: what writers do after the snapshot. Six of the seven P1s (CPO-1, NARR-1, NARR-2, R1, G-1, QS-1) are one mechanism — a point-in-time wipe followed by scheduled writers with no provenance obligation, verified once, at the wrong instant, from the read side — and the seventh (DV-1/R3, '47% odds of day 30') is the reset FREQUENCY itself leaking into a statistic: seven re-anchored cycles of 1-7 days counted as day-30 survivors because `cd is None` has no horizon check (site_api_rollups.py:712) and the caption's 'n=2' is a hand-typed string beside a computed len(priors) (:736, :741). The reason a one-time review found 70 is that the review is the only consumer that looks at the WRITE side and the DERIVED side (S3 pages, share kits, RECAP#, static catalogs) after a reset — nothing scheduled does, and the instruments that claimed to had vacuous controls (archive_one reported html_files_archived=0 / already_archived=29 as success, docs/restart/_chronicle_report.txt; assert_registry_coverage derives from OPERATIONAL_COACH_IDS, the same hand list the wipe uses). It is not that 70 things broke on 09-04; it is that every reset since cycle 4 left the same residue (week-NN pages live since 2026-07-10, ~370 escapees in cycle 11 per INCIDENT_LOG 2026-08-02, five recurring reds on main at both resets in the window) and this was the first time someone graded the residue instead of the rendering.

root_cause_classes.name: C1 — Scheduled writers select by status/timestamp and never by the wipe's stamp (the reset→writer contract does not exist)
root_cause_classes.thesis: The wipe (deploy/restart_intelligence_wipe.py) writes tombstone=True, tombstoned_at, phase=pilot, cycle=N via UpdateItem and leaves every other attribute — including status='draft' — intact (Interpretation B). Readers honour that through singleton_visible/with_phase_filter, but writers were added one at a time with their own selectors: the chronicle 48h sweep keyed on status+age (a 10-day bound a 3-day-old draft sails through), the recap committed RECAP#latest with no phase, coach_state_updater stamps every row it touches including CROSS_PHASE RELATIONSHIP#state, and the commitment evaluator's inputs bind at birth to a source the registry already knows is dark. Because the wipe is a point-in-time snapshot and the writers run on EventBridge 10-14h later, every reset re-populates a surface the wipe honestly emptied — structurally, whenever a reset lands within CHRONICLE_AUTOPUBLISH_MAX_DAYS of a Wednesday draft. #3485 fixed ONE writer (the sweep) and stamped ONE derived record (the recap); the class — 31 writer seams on EXPERIMENT_SCOPED partitions carried as dated residue in tests/pair_seam_residue.py, and a set guard (#2119) whose scan set is COACH#/ENSEMBLE# put_item only — is untouched. Recurs every reset.
root_cause_classes.why_existing_gates_missed: The #2109 phase-filter ratchet and its three waves guard READERS (with_phase_filter call sites) and cannot see a writer's raw table.query (CPO verdict). #2119's writer set guard is scoped to COACH#/ENSEMBLE# put_item, not to classify()==EXPERIMENT_SCOPED, so SOURCE#chronicle / SOURCE#insights writers are outside it by construction. Charter rule 3's seam guard (#2847) enumerated the writer seams at seed date and froze them as residue with no countdown — the exemption ledger became the place the missing contract went to be forgotten. The pair-contract registry has 8 producer→consumer pairs and zero writer↔wipe or writer↔writer pairs (tests/pair_contract_registry.py). restart_verify_semantic check 5 proved posts.json at T0 and stopped; the sweep ran at 18:00Z.

prevention.what: One taxonomy-derived writer set guard: AST-sweep lambdas/ mcp/ deploy/ for every put_item/update_item whose pk resolves (via phase_taxonomy.classify) to EXPERIMENT_SCOPED, and require the write path to pass through experiment_stamp()/tag_record() — generalising test_coach_ensemble_writer_phase_stamp_guard_2119 from a hand-scoped prefix pair to the registry's class, update_item included. Seed the 31 residue write seams as its shrink-only baseline so enrolling a writer removes a row (the ratchet's downward gear already exists). Pair it with the wipe flipping status→'voided' on any draft it tombstones (deploy/restart_intelligence_wipe.py build_update) so a status-keyed selector cannot re-select a tombstoned row even before the guard reaches it, and enrol chronicle DATE# (status vs tombstone) + habit_scores DATE# + RELATIONSHIP#state as CoOwned entries in tests/pair_contract_registry.py (replay writer B after writer A, assert A's tombstone/phase fields survive).
prevention.where: tests/test_coach_ensemble_writer_phase_stamp_guard_2119.py → tests/test_scoped_writer_provenance_guard.py (derived from lambdas/experiment/phase_taxonomy.py::classify + _PK_RULES); deploy/restart_intelligence_wipe.py::build_update; tests/pair_contract_registry.py (new CoOwned entry class); tests/pair_seam_residue.py as the baseline; docs/CONVENTIONS.md §9 row 'a scheduled writer that selects by status/timestamp cannot see a reset'
prevention.negative_control: Plant a synthetic module with `table.put_item(Item={'pk':'USER#matthew#SOURCE#insights',...})` and no stamp → the guard must red (positive control: the same module wrapped in tag_record must pass). For the wipe: run build_update on a fixture draft and assert status=='voided' and that chronicle_approve_lambda._find_stale_drafts returns nothing for it while the identical un-tombstoned record IS returned (the #3485 test already has the second half). For CoOwned: replay the recap writer after the wipe on a fixture row and assert phase/tombstone survive — must fail against the pre-#3485 _commit_recap.
prevention.missing_primitive: Contract test — specifically the writer↔wipe / writer↔writer form of primitive 4; the platform only had producer→consumer pairs

detection.what: A nightly data census inside the already-scheduled qa_smoke_lambda: for every pk family classify() calls EXPERIMENT_SCOPED (derived from _PK_RULES + SOURCE_CLASS, never OPERATIONAL_COACH_IDS), key-bounded query for rows dated < EXPERIMENT_START_DATE that are neither tombstoned nor phase=pilot, plus the inverse (any CROSS_PHASE row carrying tombstone/phase). Emit the count on the existing FailCount metric. This is the derived generalisation of check_coach_ensemble_phase_stamp_coverage (#1970), which today enumerates a hand list.
detection.rent_estimate: ≈$0 marginal: no new Lambda, alarm or metric — ~40 key-bounded DDB queries/night inside the existing qa-smoke run and its existing FailCount alarm; well inside free-tier RCU noise. Attention cost: one digest line when red.
detection.demote_trigger: Two consecutive resets AND 60 consecutive nights with zero census findings while the writer set guard's residue baseline is at zero — the guard has then absorbed the class at PR time and the census is measuring a table that cannot drift; fold it into restart_verify_semantic check 6 and retire the nightly leg.

root_cause_classes.name: C2 — The reset verifies the READ side once, at T0, and defers the WRITE side to an attended runlist nobody is obliged to run
root_cause_classes.thesis: restart_pipeline.py's three hard gates (rendered 96 URLs, semantic 8 checks, AI truth) prove what the site SERVES at the instant the pipeline finishes. Its DDB check sweeps only taxonomy.RAW_TIMESERIES_SOURCES for phase=experiment rows (restart_verify_semantic.py:350) — the partitions the TAGGER touches — and never the EXPERIMENT_SCOPED partitions the WIPE touches, nor the countdown window the wipe cannot see. The writer-side instrument (restart_verify.py check 14) is a POST-genesis, owner-run script referenced by no schedule, no workflow and no operating-calendar ritual; #3390's runlist for cycle 15 was never executed and the cycle-16 box is still open. Sub-steps report success with no work contract: the chronicle archive step reported html_files_total=29, archived=0, already_archived=29 and passed (NARR-5 CRC), the frozen-artifact sweep does not run after a re-anchor/override (CTO-3, the #1985 class on its third reset), and the pipeline's pre-push sweep runs Docs-CI's python gates and node --test but zero pytest, so the regenerated prereg artifact reds main at every reset (principal-02, both resets in the window). The pipeline's own proportionality row believes it runs 'a few times a quarter'; it ran 12 times in 55 days.
root_cause_classes.why_existing_gates_missed: Point-in-time: every gate ran ~16:50Z; the sweep that resurrected the draft ran 18:00Z, og-image 19:30Z, the recap after that. Read-side: check 6 enumerates RAW_TIMESERIES_SOURCES, so a scoped partition with an un-tombstoned pre-genesis row is invisible to the reset's only data assertion. Attended: check 14 is the one writer-side sweep and it lives behind a human running a script on Day 1; the 09:30 PT cloud routine has no AWS access by design. Vacuous: archive_one returns (dest, False) on dest-key collision and the report counts that as success; restart_verify's composite-alarm leg had never once run (#3390, describe_alarms without AlarmTypes). The PROPORTIONALITY row for the sweep (#3477) states a false cadence, so nobody priced the reset as a weekly event.

prevention.what: Three edits to the reset's own contract. (1) A work contract per step: every restart_* sub-script reports {input_count, acted_count, skipped_count} and the pipeline reds when input_count>0 and acted_count==0 without a named reason (archive_one 0/29 becomes red, not 'already archived'). (2) Semantic check 6 sweeps the classify()-derived scoped set for un-tombstoned rows dated < genesis, in addition to the raw set. (3) The pre-push sweep (restart_verify_gates.py) derives — by grep/AST — the set of tests/*.py that open deploy/generated/** or the prereg stamp and runs exactly that set (the #3477 sweep's own principle, python leg). Plus a re-verify at T+24h: the #3390 cloud routine re-curls posts.json, /api/recap, /api/predictions and asserts no entry predates genesis while day_n≥0 — it already exists and needs no AWS.
prevention.where: deploy/restart_pipeline.py (step report contract) + deploy/restart_chronicle_handler.py::archive_one; deploy/restart_verify_semantic.py check 6 (derive from phase_taxonomy.classify); deploy/restart_verify_gates.py + tests/test_restart_verify_gates_3477.py (derived pytest leg); the #3390 cloud routine prompt; docs/PROPORTIONALITY.md row 86 corrected to the measured cadence (12 resets / 55 days)
prevention.negative_control: Fixture bucket with generated/journal/posts/week-04/index.html older than the reset and absent from the rebuilt posts.json → restart_verify must red (positive control: the same page listed in posts.json passes). Fixture table with one un-tombstoned SOURCE#insights DATE#<genesis−1> row → semantic check 6 reds. A test that the derived pytest set is non-empty and contains test_plan_literal_reconciliation.py / test_prereg_hash_stamp.py / test_prereg_seal_1980.py — an empty derivation RAISES (the #3477 dead-man shape).
prevention.missing_primitive: Dead-man — the reset has no detector for 'a step ran and did nothing' or 'the writers ran after me'; secondarily the derivation guard (check 6 and the pytest leg enumerate hand-chosen subsets)

detection.what: Move check 14's sweep core (deploy/countdown_gap_sweep.py is already importable and registry-derived) into the nightly qa_smoke_lambda for the 10 nights after any genesis — the sweep runs unattended on Day 1 instead of waiting for a session — and have the #3390 cloud routine post its T+24h re-curl verdict. Both ride existing schedules.
detection.rent_estimate: ≈$0 marginal: the sweep is a scan of the wipe's partitions (~15 partitions, key-bounded) once per night for 10 nights per reset inside the existing qa-smoke Lambda; no new alarm (FailCount already routes). Attention: one digest line.
detection.demote_trigger: Two consecutive resets where the nightly sweep finds zero escapees AND the C1 writer guard's residue baseline is zero — at that point every writer stamps at birth and the sweep is a check on a window that no longer exists; retire the nightly leg and keep check 14 as the attended fallback.

root_cause_classes.name: C3 — Write-time provenance and rendered tense come from a constant/SSM, not from the event's own date: the pre-start window is not a phase the registry knows
root_cause_classes.thesis: A sanctioned future genesis (#931/#939) creates a window [wipe, genesis) in which the platform is 'between cycles', but the taxonomy has two phase values (pilot/experiment) and no pre-start value. experiment_stamp() returns EXPERIMENT_PHASE_CURRENT unconditionally and the cycle from SSM, which the reset bumps BEFORE genesis; PHASE_FILTER_EXPRESSION admits attribute_not_exists(phase) forever; and the tagger ran at 16:37Z, 32 minutes before the INSIGHT# rows existed (DA-7). So every countdown-window write — 10 of 24 served 'cycle 16' predictions, 2 of them gradeable bets with windows starting on Day 0, none in the frozen artifact (QS-1) — is stamped as the experiment it precedes, and every renderer that hand-rolls preStart() one span short narrates the genesis in the past tense ('since the September 5th reset' on September 4; 'Experiment day 0 (restarted 2026-09-05)'; 'DAY 1 · day to go'; a Day-0 analyzer prompt clamping days_in_experiment to 1). The countdown-gap sweep exists to catch the residue; until #3488 it sanctioned the residue. Recurs on every future-genesis reset — which is every reset since cycle 11.
root_cause_classes.why_existing_gates_missed: There is no registry value to derive from: the 'pre-start' state lives in /api/journey.pre_start and in each page's preStart() rather than in phase_taxonomy, so every consumer re-derives it and the derivation guard has nothing to check against (AIQ verdict: 'grounding classes cover numbers/dates/freshness/behavioral/night, none cover tense'). The sweep's own test pinned the sanctioning rule that blinded it (the replaced test_current_cycle_stamp… case), a vacuous negative control. The pre-start contract sweep (tests/test_pre_start_contract_sweep) covers a hand-chosen subset of endpoints, not qa_manifest's registry. No contract compares served PREDICTION# rows against the sealed artifact's ids (QS verdict); the #3480 fix served pre_registered_at but does not assert season rows ⊆ frozen ids.

prevention.what: Make provenance a function of the date, once: experiment_stamp(as_of=...)/tag_record derive phase from `as_of >= EXPERIMENT_START_DATE` (pre-genesis writes stamp pilot, or a new PRESTART value that PHASE_FILTER_EXPRESSION hides) — then the countdown window needs no sweep because nothing written in it is ever visible. Have the coach emission chain refuse gradeable PREDICTION#/COMMITMENT# writes while pre_start is true, and add the season⊆frozen contract: every non-voided season PREDICTION# row with created_date ≤ genesis must have an id in the sealed artifact, run in restart_verify and CI against the committed prereg. Retire per-surface preStart() re-derivation by routing every phase line through build_experiment_phase_context (#1086) and enrolling every qa_manifest API endpoint in the pre-start contract sweep with a genesis+1 fixture asserting no numeric 0 on a pre-genesis date and no past-tense genesis.
prevention.where: lambdas/experiment/phase_taxonomy.py::experiment_stamp + lambdas/common/compute_metadata.py::tag_record; lambdas/coach/coach_state_updater.py (emission refusal); tests/test_countdown_gap_sweep.py (season⊆frozen contract against deploy/generated/genesis_preregistration.json); tests/test_pre_start_contract_sweep.py derived from tests/qa_manifest.py; lambdas/intelligence/intelligence_common.py::build_experiment_phase_context as the single phase line; tests/grounding_wiring.py (register the temporal rule in the freshness class so it is in the census)
prevention.negative_control: A write with as_of = genesis−1 that lands phase=experiment must fail the stamp test (positive control: as_of = genesis stamps experiment). A fixture PREDICTION# row created_date ≤ genesis whose id is absent from the frozen artifact must red the season⊆frozen contract; the 14 frozen ids must pass. The grounding rule: today's live sentence ('since the September 5th reset', gen_date 09-04) is the positive control and 'the reset lands tomorrow' the negative.
prevention.missing_primitive: Registry — the pre-start state is a vocabulary value that exists in no registry, so primitive 2 (derivation guard) had nothing to derive from

detection.what: The C1 nightly census already covers this class's residue (an un-tombstoned scoped row dated < genesis). Add one deterministic rule to the existing reader-truth judge's deterministic layer (baseline_freshness): gen_date < EXPERIMENT_START_DATE and text matches since|after|following + genesis/reset → finding. Both ride existing nightly runs.
detection.rent_estimate: $0 — a regex rule in an existing deterministic pass and a census the C1 row already pays for
detection.demote_trigger: n/a (FREE); retire the temporal rule if experiment_stamp derives from date AND the pre-start contract sweep covers qa_manifest, since the rule is then a check on a state that can no longer be written

root_cause_classes.name: C4 — Served statistics whose caption/method/label is a second, hand-typed writer beside the computation (ADR-105 is a rule with no owning gate)
root_cause_classes.thesis: A public number and its stated method are produced by two writers that nothing binds: the computation (survivors/(n+2), pooled Brier, a directional EWMA grade, projected_prod_only, fat÷(lean+fat)) and a prose string or label typed beside it ('n=2 is narrative, not statistics' at site_api_rollups.py:736/:741 beside len(priors)=15; 'well-calibrated / skilled=true' over two unskilled strata; 'directional' on a point claim; 'projected month-end' with its class scope discarded by every consumer; '42.7% body fat' under a 44% bar). The survival case is the reset machinery leaking into statistics: `cd is None` (:712) has no horizon check, so seven re-anchored cycles of 1-7 days count as day-30 survivors — the more the platform resets, the more confident the odds become. ADR-105 demands 'uncertainty + n on every statistical claim' but docs/CONVENTIONS.md §9 has no row naming a gate that owns it, and tests/api_schemas/*.json pin field PRESENCE, never that a method describes its own arithmetic. Mostly latent one-offs that the reset frequency and the Day-0 empty state made visible; DV-1 will worsen every reset until fixed (#3549 open).
root_cause_classes.why_existing_gates_missed: The visual sweep and the reader-truth judge see rendering and prose, not encoding arithmetic (DV verdict); the API schema contract checks shape; test_calibration_core_parity has no two-strata control (QS verdict); the receipts test pins a false sentence rather than the condition it claims (COST verdict) — the phrase-pinned-prose class the principal row grades. No gate in §9 owns 'a statistical claim whose method cannot produce it from its own inputs', so no gate could have been asked what would make it red.

prevention.what: An ADR-105 emission contract: every public endpoint that serves a probability, skill, calibration verdict, projection or composition percentage returns a `method` OBJECT built by the same function as the number — {n, denominator/censoring rule, strata, derived_from, scope} — and the api_schemas contract requires it; captions render from the object, never from a literal. Register the defect class in CONVENTIONS §9 with that test as owner. Each endpoint gets one adversarial fixture chosen to make the current arithmetic lie: all-censored 1-7-day priors (p30 must not exceed the Laplace prior), two strata at 0.5/22% and 0.8/79% (pooled card may never read well-calibrated while every stratum is unskilled), a level claim 'X will be approximately N on <date>' (may never receive type=directional), a payload whose projected_scope ≠ 'all classes' (the label must carry the scope).
prevention.where: tests/api_schemas/api_survival.json, api_calibration.json, api_receipts.json, api_predictions.json (required `method` object); new tests/test_served_statistic_method_contract.py; lambdas/web/site_api_rollups.py::survival, lambdas/experiment/calibration_core.py::score_pairs + stats_core.py:822 (stratified reference Brier), lambdas/coach/coach_state_updater.py::build_predic… (claim-shape classifier), lambdas/web/site_api_budget.py::receipts; docs/CONVENTIONS.md §9 new row
prevention.negative_control: Mutate priors from 2 to 3 → the served n must move (fails today: 'n=2' is a literal). Feed the all-censored fixture to the current survival() → p30=47 must be rejected (positive control: a fixture with one cycle that reached day 30 must raise p30 above the prior). The two-strata fixture must red the current pooled skill and pass once stratified. 'Recovery score will be approximately 53.5% on September 5th' must not receive type=directional (positive control: 'HRV will rise over the next two weeks' must).
prevention.missing_primitive: Derivation guard — the caption must derive from the computation; secondarily the contract test with a fixture that makes the arithmetic fail (fixture must be the wire)

detection.what: The DV verdict's rule, run against LIVE payloads in the existing nightly qa-smoke: any 'n=<int>' / '<int> prior cycles' literal inside a served string must equal a numeric field in the same payload; any served p/skill field must carry its method object. Reds the day a caption goes stale, without a review.
detection.rent_estimate: $0 — one regex pass over payloads the nightly qa-smoke already fetches (check_hero_weight_arithmetic is the precedent)
detection.demote_trigger: n/a (FREE); retire the live rule when every enrolled endpoint's caption is generator-derived from the method object — the contract test then makes the live check redundant

root_cause_classes.name: C5 — The reset tools enumerate from hand-typed lists where the registry rules per row/prefix (guard-the-instance inside the machinery that is supposed to be the set guard)
root_cause_classes.thesis: phase_taxonomy classifies by prefix rule (`COACH#` → EXPERIMENT_SCOPED first-match), but the wipe's coverage assertion derives its required COACH#* set from OPERATIONAL_COACH_IDS, the nightly stamp audit enumerates the same hand list plus a four-tuple of ENSEMBLE# pks, coach_state_updater stamps per PARTITION where the registry rules per ROW (RELATIONSHIP#state is CROSS_PHASE by sk), and a reclassification (ADR-153, CHAT# → cross_phase, ~5h after a wipe) shipped with no reconcile step, so 26 CROSS_PHASE rows still carry tombstone=True/cycle=12 and the registry's 'NEVER tagged, NEVER wiped' is false in live data. Result: COACH#nudge_ledger and COACH#outbound_ledger are wipeable on paper, outside COACH_PARTITIONS, outside the audit, and 13 rows from three cycles back survived every reset untouched. The wipe's own gate (assert_registry_coverage) and its CI twin (test_restart_wipe_coverage) pass because they compare two copies of the same hand list. Latent rather than per-reset: it fires when a pk family or classification is added, and stays wrong silently.
root_cause_classes.why_existing_gates_missed: assert_registry_coverage() derives covered_pks from FULL_PK_PARTITIONS ∪ COACH_PARTITIONS and its required set from OPERATIONAL_COACH_IDS — both sides hand-typed, so a blanket-rule family the registry classifies scoped but nobody listed is invisible to both (DA verdict: 'instruments that enumerate from a hand-typed list … cannot fail on the case they were written for'). The #2844 conformance guard keys on registry vocabularies (sources, personas, lambdas, alarms) — pk families are not one of its vocabularies. The stamp audit uses should_phase_stamp() per row (correct) but the writer does not (DA-6): the derivation exists on the read side and was never applied to the write side. No test asserts the registry's claims against live data (DA-9).

prevention.what: Make the live census the required set: restart_pipeline step-0 already enumerates every pk family in the table — write that list to deploy/generated/pk_family_census.json and have assert_registry_coverage (wipe), the countdown sweep, the nightly stamp audit and the SCHEMA.md doc-facts rule all assert `{family : classify(family)==EXPERIMENT_SCOPED} ⊆ covered_pks` from it, never from OPERATIONAL_COACH_IDS. Gate the write-side stamp on should_phase_stamp(pk, sk) in coach_state_updater/coach_history_summarizer/ensemble_digest (`stamp = experiment_stamp() if should_phase_stamp(pk, sk) else {}`). Require any _PK_RULES / SOURCE_CLASS reclassification PR to ship a reconcile script (the DA-9 one-off: strip tombstone/phase/cycle from the 26 rows, dry-run listed) — a test that the taxonomy's git blame date for a rule is not newer than the last reconcile record for that family.
prevention.where: deploy/restart_pipeline.py step 0 (census artifact); deploy/restart_intelligence_wipe.py::assert_registry_coverage; deploy/countdown_gap_sweep.py; lambdas/operational/qa_smoke_lambda.py::check_coach_ensemble_phase_stamp_coverage; lambdas/coach/coach_state_updater.py; tests/test_restart_wipe_coverage.py (fixture family classified scoped but uncovered → SystemExit); scripts/check_doc_facts.py (SCHEMA.md families from the census)
prevention.negative_control: Add a fixture family 'COACH#phantom_ledger' to the census fixture with no PARTITIONS entry → assert_registry_coverage must SystemExit (positive control: today's real census must pass once nudge_ledger/outbound_ledger get their SYSTEM_STATE rules). A coach_state_updater put on RELATIONSHIP#state must carry no `phase` key (fails against the current writer). The nightly inverse check: a CROSS_PHASE row WITH a phase stamp → WARN, proven on the 26 live rows before the reconcile runs.
prevention.missing_primitive: Derivation guard — applied to the reset tools themselves (the wipe, audit and sweep were exempted from the rule they enforce)

detection.what: The inverse leg of the C1 nightly census (a CROSS_PHASE row carrying tombstone or phase; an EXPERIMENT_SCOPED family absent from the wipe's covered set) — the same qa-smoke check, derived from classify() over the census artifact.
detection.rent_estimate: ≈$0 marginal — shares the C1 census run (one scan of the census families, key-bounded); no new alarm
detection.demote_trigger: Two consecutive quarters with zero families added to the census and zero reconcile findings — the taxonomy is then stable and the CI-time coverage test alone suffices; fold the nightly inverse leg into test_restart_wipe_coverage

root_cause_classes.name: C6 — Derived artifacts (S3 pages, share kits, moments, OG cards, static catalogs, proof stamps) sit outside the taxonomy, so the wipe cannot reach them and each has its own slug-keyed, once-only archive
root_cause_classes.thesis: ADR-077 governs DynamoDB rows. Everything derived from a scoped row and written to S3 or config — generated/journal/posts/week-NN/index.html, moments/share-kits/week-NN/kit.json, moments/index.json, chronicle-*.png, the /data and /protocols proof blocks, config/challenges_catalog.json's coach 'evidence' — has no class, no `derived_from` pointer and no cycle in its key. restart_chronicle_handler.archive_one is idempotent on the SLUG: it returns 'already archived' when archive/pilot/posts/week-NN/index.html exists, and every week-NN has existed since the cycle-4 reset on 2026-07-10, so no reset since has archived, tombstoned or 301'd a page (html_files_archived=0 on 2026-09-04); the #3485 live repair 'restored the pre-sweep S3 version' of week-04 — which was the cycle-14 article, the same slug blind spot inherited by the repair. Share kits and per-post PNGs have no removal path when a post leaves the manifest (G-2 CRC). Recurs every reset since cycle 4; #3512 landed the archive notice (a reader-facing mitigation) but the archive is still slug-keyed and no assertion ties live artifacts to the visible record set.
root_cause_classes.why_existing_gates_missed: The taxonomy's coverage assertion has nothing to say about S3 — the class registry is a DDB registry, so 'every scoped thing is wiped' was true of rows and false of the pages built from them. restart_verify_rendered checks 96 REGISTERED URLs 200 and never asks what ELSE 200s (growth verdict); the archive step's success condition is 'destination exists', which is exactly the failure. og_moments rebuilds the index daily as a pure function of posts.json (so the index self-heals) but kit.json and chronicle-*.png are written once by chronicle_approve with no purge. The challenges catalog is static config: no reset, tombstone or phase filter reaches it, and the undated-statistic rule (#1226/#2343) had no static-config variant.

prevention.what: Extend phase_taxonomy with a DERIVED_ARTIFACTS registry: {S3 prefix or config path → source partition, key scheme MUST include the cycle, purge rule}. Key archive_one on (slug, cycle) — archive to generated/journal/archive/cycle-<N>/posts/ — and ALWAYS tombstone-overwrite + 301-register a live week-NN absent from the new posts.json. Add to restart_verify: every generated/journal/posts/week-NN/ that returns 200 is in the live posts.json; moments/index.json ⊆ posts.json; every share-kit canonical_url ∈ posts.json. Require `evidence_as_of` + `evidence_cycle` on any catalog entry whose evidence_summary contains a digit (test over config/challenges_catalog.json) and have the renderer label or strip pre-genesis. Put scripts/v4_build_evidence.py in sync_site_to_s3.sh's builder list so the /data and /protocols proof stamps rebake with the others.
prevention.where: lambdas/experiment/phase_taxonomy.py (DERIVED_ARTIFACTS); deploy/restart_chronicle_handler.py::archive_one + register_permalink_redirect; deploy/restart_verify.py (live-page ⊆ manifest assertion, with a planted-stale-page fixture in tests/test_restart_site_sweep.py); lambdas/content/og_moments.py::_sweep_chronicles (purge); tests/test_challenges_catalog_evidence_stamp.py; deploy/sync_site_to_s3.sh builder list + restart_verify baked-proof check
prevention.negative_control: Fixture bucket with generated/journal/posts/week-05/index.html (mtime older than the reset) absent from posts.json → restart_verify reds; the same page listed → passes. archive_one on a slug whose cycle-4 archive exists must archive again under cycle-16 and report acted_count=1 (fails against current code: returns (dest, False)). A catalog entry with 'HRV 29.56' and no evidence_cycle → red. A kit.json whose canonical_url left the manifest must be purged by _sweep_chronicles (negative control in tests).
prevention.missing_primitive: Registry — derived artifacts have no entry in the taxonomy, so neither the wipe nor its coverage assertion can reach them

detection.what: Extend the #3485 nightly chronicle_manifest_qa (already in qa_smoke) from 'every posts.json entry maps to a visible DDB row' to the derived set: every 200 under /journal/posts/week-NN/ ∈ posts.json (HEAD over the registry of slugs), moments/index.json ⊆ posts.json, newest posts.json/moments entry does not predate genesis while day_n ≥ 0.
detection.rent_estimate: ≈$0 marginal — ~10 HTTPS HEADs and one JSON compare per night inside the existing qa-smoke run; no new alarm
detection.demote_trigger: Two consecutive resets with zero derived-artifact findings after archive_one is cycle-keyed and the purge path exists — the reset then owns the derived set by construction and the nightly compare is redundant with restart_verify's assertion

forensics.evidence_quality: Established from the repo and the forensic input, read-only: reset frequency (12 resets in 55 days, CYCLE_GENESES literals); the reader/writer asymmetry (with_phase_filter in 76 files, singleton_visible in 34, experiment_stamp in 14, tag_record in 15; 112 files with put/update and 26 of them stamping); the #2119 guard's scope (COACH#/ENSEMBLE# put_item only, by its own docstring); the semantic verify's DDB check iterating taxonomy.RAW_TIMESERIES_SOURCES only (restart_verify_semantic.py:350); check 14 unreferenced by any workflow, CDK schedule or operating-calendar ritual; the residue ledger (285 rows, 69 write-direction, 31 on EXPERIMENT_SCOPED partitions by my parse); the wipe's coverage assertion deriving from OPERATIONAL_COACH_IDS; survival()'s `cd is None` and literal 'n=2' still on main; PROPORTIONALITY row 86's 'a few times a quarter'; #3485/#3488/#3512 diffs and what they left. NOT established: (1) I ran no tests and no live AWS or DDB queries — every live count (56/73 sanctioned rows, 66 escapees, html_files_archived=0, 26 tombstoned CROSS_PHASE rows, 13 ledger rows) is taken from the findings' CRCs and the commit messages, not re-measured; (2) the 'UNSTAMPED writer' census is a crude grep — several hits are SOURCE#<scoped> writers that rely on the tagger by documented design, so the true unstamped-scoped-writer count lies between the #2119-guarded set and ~25 files; (3) the 31 residue write seams were classified by a best-effort classify() over partition names, ±a few; (4) whether restart_verify has been run on Day 1 for cycle 16 — the #3390 box read as unchecked, but the issue body may be stale; (5) I did not read the 520KB review artifact, only the input's summaries/CRCs; (6) the rent estimates for the nightly census/sweep legs are inferred from query shape (key-bounded, inside an existing Lambda), not measured; (7) the claim that C1 'recurs every reset within 10 days of a Wednesday draft' is the CPO-1 CRC's structural argument, which I checked against CHRONICLE_AUTOPUBLISH_MAX_DAYS=10 in the handler but did not verify against the draft history; (8) the class boundaries (C1 vs C3, C1 vs C6) are my judgement — a reviewer could defensibly merge C1/C3/C6 into one 'the reset contract is read-side only' class; I kept them apart because each has a different missing primitive (contract / registry value / registry entry) and therefore a different fix location.

forensics.lens: Engineering Manager / SDLC lead — defects as consequences of how the work is organised: many short fresh-context AI sessions, one owner, a board that turns over ~300 issues in 14 days, and rituals (wrap / land / prove-it / new-machinery / issue-filer / review) that are read at the author's discretion rather than enforced at a stage.
forensics.the_70_question:
The review found ~70 things the platform had not because the workflow's own instruments measure MERGE, CLOSURE and GATE-COUNT, while the review measured LIVE EFFECT on a Day-0 surface — the one axis (time after a reset) and the one moment the workflow never measures. Five measured facts, in order of weight:

(1) Half of main lands with no test gate at all. Since 2026-08-22 main took 613 commits: 311 PR merges and 302 direct pushes (156 reconcile-bot, 146 by the agent session account); 179 of the direct pushes touch lambdas/cdk/mcp/deploy/scripts. The installed hooks are `commit-msg` + `pre-commit` (black/ruff + sync_doc_metadata) only — no pre-push hook exists, `deploy/agent_commit.sh` contains zero `pytest`, and ADR-117 makes the Unit Tests job non-gating for deploy. The principal verdict measured 26 of 29 red Unit-Test runs on main in 14 days as direct pushes; HANDOVER_LATEST.md records the session breaking main twice 'by running targeted tests instead of the full suite'. The reset pipeline itself is a direct push (principal-02). So a red main is measured after the fact, never prevented, and a red main still ships.

(2) Closure is decoupled from live effect. `scripts/closure_contract.py` DEFAULT_MODE = "warn"; `Fixes #N` closes at merge, before deploy. Of 289 issues closed since 08-22: 25 have zero comments, 173 carry `**Shipped:**`, only ~122 carry anything resembling live evidence; median open→close is 9.0h and 186/229 close inside 24h. That is exactly how INT-1 (#1480, sentinel write IAM-denied every run for 49 days), G-3 (#2254, status write denied since 08-08), OBS-1 (#1956, never once produced its measurement) and CPO-2 (#532, 21 consecutive 'kept=0 broken=0' runs) all read CLOSED while non-functional. The prove-it rule 'fail-closed paths need a LIVE proof' is a memory entry and a skill paragraph, not a closure requirement.

(3) The review cadence carried grades forward across a reset-heavy month and then measured a surface it had never seen. `fullreview_grades_2026-08-16_delta.json` names cpo/designer/dataviz/qs/a11y/cost/devex/growth as 'grades stand' from the 07-28 partial / 08-02 delta, reader and data-architect from 08-09; the 08-27 delta was held (instrument rewrite, recorded in operating_calendar.py) so no review of any breadth ran 08-16→09-05. Every prior review ran on Day 1–6 of a cycle (07-16 = cycle 6 Day 3; 08-02/09/16 = Day 6); 09-05 is the first ever on Day 0 / pre-start, hours after a reset and BETWEEN the reset and its first scheduled writers (17:09Z insight writes, 18:00Z chronicle sweep, 19:30Z og_moments). 39 of the 99 confirmed findings are reset/phase/genesis defects and 6 of the 7 P1s (CPO-1, NARR-1, NARR-2, R1, G-1, QS-1) are that window. Every one of the 17 grade entries also carries an anchor EXTENSION written on the day, most naming the Day-0 surface — so a material share of the 13 drops is a bar that was legitimately raised onto a surface no gate or review had ever observed, not decay of previously-A areas.

(4) Recurrence is the norm, not the exception: 33 of 99 findings' own class strings cite the prior issue number whose class they re-instantiate (#2109 4th wave, #2643→#2877 one specimen, #747 partial reach, #3390 pinned to one file, #1989/#3350 instances fixed / class never swept, #3477 shape in a third pipeline). CONVENTIONS §10 'file into the class' is 13 days old and lives in the issue-filer (review-time only); `worktree-implementer.md` has no 'enumerate the set' step; ADR-099 puts Effort in the denominator, so a 9-hour instance fix outranks a class sweep (memory: 'score inverts priority').

(5) Green is a count of gates, not of proofs. `scripts/gate_census.py` today: 597 gates, 50 'can-fail (proven)', 538 unproven, 49 flagged vacuous-empty, 33 swallowed-exit. The principal verdict: 35 of 101 recent source-scanning guards skipped a positive control. The session through-line 'instruments unable to fail' is recorded for Sessions F, G, P, Q, R and U in memory — six times — and is still a memory topic, not a CI ratchet.

Net: the 70 were 'silent' because silence is the workflow's default output: a direct push meets no test, a merge closes the issue, a fail-soft write logs 'non-fatal', a citation is matched by name, a guard is counted whether or not it can fail, and a delta review carries the grade forward. The review was the first instrument in 20 days that asked 'does it work live, today, after the reset' — and that question has no owner in the workflow.

root_cause_classes.name: The ungated landing path — agent sessions and the reset pipeline push straight to main with no test leg
root_cause_classes.thesis: Every gate the platform owns is PR-side or CI-side, but the path most commits take is a direct push authenticated as the owner's account (the ADR-148 bypass actor, principal-01's corrected cause). Between an agent's terminal and main there is only the pre-commit format hook: `deploy/agent_commit.sh` runs no pytest, `scripts/install_hooks.sh` installs no pre-push hook (verified: `.git/hooks/` holds commit-msg + pre-commit only), the reset pipeline pushes its regenerated artifacts direct (principal-02), and the wrap commits docs/CLAUDE.md/.claude direct while its local battery hand-lists 4 of Docs CI's 12 gates (DEVEX-3). Since Unit Tests is non-gating for deploy (ADR-117), a red main also ships. The consequence is measured: 302 of 613 commits on main since 08-22 are direct pushes (179 code-touching), 26 of 29 red Unit-Test runs were direct pushes, and the session that wrote the handover broke main twice the same way in one night. The reconcile bot's follow-up push 48s after each merge then cancels the human commit's Docs CI verdict (DEVEX-2), so even the after-the-fact signal is erased.
root_cause_classes.why_existing_gates_missed: The gates are sound in construction and simply not on the path: branch protection's bypass actor is the account every agent session pushes as; pre-commit runs formatters only; `wait_pr_green.sh` and `assert_pr_green.py` only see PRs; the reset's own sweep ran one doc gate and zero pytest until #3477/#3479; `check_main_green.py` read a `cancelled` rollup as 'no signal' (fixed #3530) so the reds that did surface were discarded.

prevention.what: A pre-push test leg on the direct-push path: `scripts/install_hooks.sh` installs a `pre-push` hook (pinned-formatter shape, fail-closed, `--no-verify` is the only bypass) that, when the push target is main, runs the premerge lane (`pytest -m 'premerge and not integration'`, ~155s per the principal path-to-A) PLUS the derived artifact-reader set (tests that read deploy/generated/** or the prereg stamp — derived by grep over tests/, never hand-listed); `agent_commit.sh` gains `--push` which routes through it; `deploy/restart_verify_gates.py` and `scripts/wrap_gates.py` both build their doc leg from `restart_verify_gates.docs_ci_gate_commands()` (already exists, DEVEX-3's corrected cause) with a ⊇ contract test against docs-ci.yml. A structural test asserts the hook is installed and names the lane (the #2570 shape). The reconcile bot's push keys Docs CI concurrency on `github.sha` so no main verdict is ever cancelled by a sibling push.
prevention.where: scripts/install_hooks.sh (new pre-push), deploy/agent_commit.sh (--push), scripts/wrap_gates.py + deploy/restart_verify_gates.py (import docs_ci_gate_commands), .github/workflows/docs-ci.yml + v4-gate.yml (concurrency group on sha), tests/test_docs_ci_owns_doc_gates.py sibling for the mirror-derivation contract
prevention.negative_control: Commit a one-line break to a `premerge`-marked test on a scratch branch, `git push origin HEAD:main` (dry, to a throwaway remote) → hook refuses with the failing test name; a docs-only commit passes in seconds; delete `docs_ci_gate_commands()`'s import from wrap_gates.py → the ⊇ contract test reds; push two commits to main 30s apart → both Docs CI runs complete with their own verdicts.
prevention.missing_primitive: Contract test (the landing path vs the pre-merge lane) and derivation guard (local check step-set derived from the workflow YAML) — the charter's primitives 2 and 4 were applied to PRs and never to the direct-push path.
prevention.rent_estimate: $0 AWS; ~2.5 min of local wall-clock per direct push to main, zero on branch pushes

detection.what: A wrap-battery line (scripts/wrap_gates.py, the (e2) green-main gate) that counts, from `gh api actions/runs?branch=main&event=push`, direct-push runs whose `test / Unit Tests` job concluded failure in the trailing 7 days and prints the number; the handover marker line carries it, and the closure sweep treats a non-zero count as an incident-row obligation. This is FREE because it is a `gh` read inside a battery that already runs every session.
detection.demote_trigger: n/a (no rent); retire the line if 8 consecutive wraps report 0 AND the pre-push hook's install test has been green throughout
detection.rent_estimate: $0 — one gh API read per wrap

root_cause_classes.name: Closure on merge, not on live effect — fail-soft instruments ship dead and read CLOSED
root_cause_classes.thesis: `Fixes #N` closes the issue at merge; the closure contract (`scripts/closure_contract.py`) is armed `warn`; its `outcome-verdict` requirement checks the SHAPE of the closing comment, not that the instrument ever produced a non-degraded output. Fail-soft code — a `put_item` in a try/except that logs 'non-fatal', a check that tags itself `chronic=True`, a grader with no output metric — is indistinguishable from working code in every test (a FakeDdbTable never denies a write) and in every alarm (an Errors alarm sees no error), so the only thing that could have caught it is a live observation at closure, which nothing requires. The board's velocity makes this structural: median open→close 9.0h, 186/229 under 24h, so the 'first real run' that would reveal the dead path is always after the close. Four of this review's most expensive findings are exactly this shape and were closed 21–49 days before the review: INT-1 (#1480), G-3 (#2254), OBS-1 (#1956/#2378), CPO-2 (#532); NARR-5/G-1 is the same shape on the reset's archive step (silent no-op every reset since cycle 4), and INT-3/a11y-3/DEVEX-8 are fast-follows or 'step 4' items that were never ticketed once the parent closed.
root_cause_classes.why_existing_gates_missed: The closure contract's detectors A/B check comment shape, residual homes and the PR closing set — none asks for a first live output; `wrap (e8)` asks the session to write `realized` only with live evidence in hand, but that is a sentence in a skill; `/prove-it`'s 'fail-closed paths need a LIVE proof' and `/land`'s 'merged is not deployed' are discretionary reads; the IAM-parity pattern (`tests/test_freshness_checker_iam_parity.py`) existed and was not applied to the new sender (G-3) because nothing at PR time asks 'did this Lambda gain a verb'.

prevention.what: Two additions to the existing closure registry, both structural: (1) a `first-live-output` requirement in `CLOSURE_CONTRACT` — when the closing PR's diff adds or edits a fail-soft site (AST-detectable: a boto3 write/put/query inside `try` whose `except` logs and continues; a check returning a `chronic`/`skip`/warn-class result; a new EMF metric emitter or alarm), the closing comment must carry `first non-degraded output observed at <ISO timestamp> — <where>` or the verdict must be `partial` and the issue stays open (detector A emits `no-live-proof`); (2) an IAM-parity contract generalised from the freshness-checker test: for every Lambda whose role carries `dynamodb:LeadingKeys`/action allowlists, AST-derive the module's boto3 verbs and pk literals and assert containment (the integrations + growth verdicts, same test family), enrolled in the premerge conftest list so a new verb without a grant reds the PR. Flip detector A to `block` for the `no-live-proof` code only (not the whole contract) — it is the one code whose false-positive cost is a reopened issue, never a lost fix.
prevention.where: scripts/closure_contract.py (new Requirement + finding code), scripts/closure_sweep.py (detector A), scripts/check_pr_closing_set.py (advisory PR-side hit when the diff has a fail-soft site and carries `Fixes`), tests/test_site_api_write_scope.py generalised into tests/test_role_family_write_scope.py, .claude/skills/land/SKILL.md §5 and .claude/agents/worktree-implementer.md (state the live-proof line in the PR body's post-merge ops steps)
prevention.negative_control: Replay PR #2254's diff through detector A with a closing comment lacking the timestamp line → `no-live-proof` hit; the same comment with the line → clean. Add a `put_item` on a pk outside the role's LeadingKeys allowlist in a scratch branch → the role-family test reds naming the Lambda and the pk; move it inside → green. A docs-only PR with `Fixes` → no hit.
prevention.missing_primitive: Contract test (writer ↔ role scope) and dead-man (a fail-soft path's own silence) — primitives 4 and 5 were absent at the writer; the closure registry (primitive 1) exists but has no requirement that touches live effect.
prevention.rent_estimate: $0 — CI seconds and one extra line per closing comment

detection.what: A logged-ERROR/WARN MetricFilter dead-man on the operational checkers (freshness-checker, chronicle-email-sender, coach-nudge, qa-smoke) using the existing `monitoring_stack.py:993` pattern, routed to the daily digest (never the pager). A 'non-fatal' line logged every run becomes visible within a day instead of never. Also the qa-smoke nightly gains a ledger-stuck check (nudge rows at `attempting` > 24h; DA-1) — that half is free, it is one Query in an already-running Lambda.
detection.demote_trigger: Remove a filter+alarm after 60 days with zero non-zero datapoints ONCE the role-family write-scope contract test is enrolled in premerge (the CI-side primitive makes the runtime one redundant for the IAM-denial sub-class); re-evaluate the row at the quarterly PROPORTIONALITY re-read.
detection.rent_estimate: ~$0.10/mo per filter+alarm × 4 ≈ $0.40/mo (CloudWatch alarm pricing; metric filters on existing log groups are free within the first custom metrics tier)

root_cause_classes.name: Instance fixed, set never swept — the issue is scoped to the specimen and the implementer never enumerates the class
root_cause_classes.thesis: An issue arrives naming one file, one selector, one alarm, one page; the lane (fresh context, ~9h to close) fixes that member, the PR carries `Fixes #N`, and the class owner — if one exists — is judged by child count (memory: 'epic checklists are stale by construction'). The result is that the same class is 'fixed' repeatedly at the instance: #2643 landed on Eight Sleep only (#2877, INT-3), #747's placeholder fix reached four builders and not radarChart (DV-8), #3390's composite-alarm fix pinned one file while four callers stayed blind (OBS-4), #1989/#3350 fixed two opacity-recede instances while ~230 nodes stayed (a11y-1), the light-override class got its third specimen after two instance fixes (a11y-2), #3050 pinned one of the three ordering relations its own docstring states (AIQ-1), #2384's retired-cast guard scans a set that omits deploy/ and config/ (R2), the raw-hex gate sweeps stylesheets while JS templates carry hex (DES-4), the type floor is armed on 3 of 89 pages (DES-2). 33 of the 99 findings' class strings cite the prior issue whose class they re-instantiate. CONVENTIONS §10 'file into the class' is 13 days old and lives only in the issue-filer (a review-time actor); the worktree-implementer brief has no step that asks 'how many members does this set have'; ADR-099's Effort denominator makes the instance fix the higher-scoring pick.
root_cause_classes.why_existing_gates_missed: `/new-machinery` asks 'guard the SET' but is invoked at the author's discretion; `tests/test_source_enumeration_drift.py` covers the sets it was hand-taught (INT-3: DAILY_SOURCES is outside it); the gate census flags `exempt-by-incompleteness` (38) and `vacuous-empty` (49) but nothing ratchets them; the issue body's `## Acceptance` is 3–5 boxes on the instance and the closure contract grades those boxes, so a complete instance fix is a fully-realized close.

prevention.what: Make the set part of the issue and of the PR, structurally: (1) `issue-filer.md` contract — every `type:bug`/`type:story` filed from a review or an incident carries a `## Set` section: the enumeration query (grep/AST/registry expression) that defines the class and its member count today, plus one mandatory acceptance box 'the guard enumerates the set from source and covers N/N members (or the residual is folded onto class owner #M)'; `scripts/check_backlog_hygiene.py` lints the heading. (2) `worktree-implementer.md` step 6b — before opening the PR, run the `## Set` query, paste the member list into the PR body, and either cover all members or name the residual's carrier; the driver's `/land` step 5 reads it. (3) The principal path-to-A #4 rule as a structural test: any `tests/test_*.py` that AST-parses or regex-scans first-party source must contain a synthetic must-fail case for the same helper (shrink-only allowlist, dated) — this turns 'guard the set' from advice into a red.
prevention.where: .claude/agents/issue-filer.md (`## Set` section), scripts/check_backlog_hygiene.py (heading lint), .claude/agents/worktree-implementer.md (step 6b), .claude/skills/land/SKILL.md §5, tests/test_source_scanning_guards_have_controls.py (new structural test over tests/), docs/CONVENTIONS.md §10 (one-line pointer, not a restatement)
prevention.negative_control: File a bug body without `## Set` → hygiene lint reds at wrap (e7); open a PR whose body lists 3 of 5 members and folds nothing → `/land` §5 reads `partial`, issue stays open; add a scanner test with a hand-typed file list and no must-fail case → the structural test reds naming it; add the synthetic violator fixture → green.
prevention.missing_primitive: Derivation guard over the SET (primitive 2) — every member of this class has a guard that enumerates a hand-typed subset; the registry exists (source_registry, qa_manifest, persona_registry, the CDK alarm set) and the guard did not derive from it.
prevention.rent_estimate: $0 — a lint, a brief edit, one structural test

detection.what: The gate census's `unproven` count (today 538/597) and its `exempt-by-incompleteness`/`vacuous-empty` flag counts become shrink-only ratchet lines in the wrap battery and in `check_backlog_hygiene` — a new guard may not enter `unproven` without a dated exemption, and the three numbers may only go down. Free: `scripts/gate_census.py` already derives them every run.
detection.demote_trigger: n/a (no rent); the ratchet retires itself when `unproven` reaches the dated-exemption floor
detection.rent_estimate: $0 — CI seconds

root_cause_classes.name: Hand-typed mirrors of a fact the platform already owns — prose, comments, fixtures, and local restatements of CI's step set
root_cause_classes.thesis: Every session writes prose that the next session reads as fact: the CLAUDE.md status block, the handover, memory (403 files, 225 `reference_*`), PROPORTIONALITY rows, alarm citations, gate header comments, fixture literals, and registry prose. The doc-facts gates (#2003) exist but are phrase-keyed — `check_doc_facts.py` matches 'currently <date>', `check_memory_body_facts.py` matches 'always use <date>' and excludes MEMORY.md by design (DEVEX-5) — so the same false fact in different words passes, and comments/fixtures/skill prose are outside any net. The same mechanism produces the local mirrors of CI: `wrap_gates.py` hand-lists 4 of 12 doc gates (DEVEX-3), `wait_pr_green.sh` restates path filters as regexes that drifted (DEVEX-4), the reset sweep ran one gate vs twelve (#3477), the drift sentinel's cadence is encoded twice (OBS-3), the exemption ledger's reasons rot (OBS-7), the coverage header states three eras of numbers (principal-07), a caption hard-codes n=2 beside a computed n (DV-1), the subscribe promise hand-types a cadence three CDK schedules own (G-4), three surfaces state three source counts (G-6). 32 findings match the prose-vs-truth shape; 14 the subset/mirror shape. 83 direct docs commits landed on main in 14 days — the wrap is the platform's largest prose writer and its battery is the subset.
root_cause_classes.why_existing_gates_missed: The fact gates are phrase-keyed (the #2959/#3003/#3199 family the memory index itself says has failed in the field every time); comments and fixtures are not a doc surface any gate reads; the local CI mirrors have no ⊇ contract against the workflow YAML; and when the wrap commit does red Docs CI, the reconcile bot's follow-up push cancels the verdict (DEVEX-2).

prevention.what: (1) The mirror-derivation contract family (the DevEx verdict): for every local check that names a CI job as its target — wrap_gates, restart_verify_gates, wait_pr_green, the pre-commit hook — a test asserts its step/check set is a superset of the set parsed from the workflow YAML with PyYAML (`gate_census.py` already carries the parser); wait_pr_green derives expected checks from `pull_request.paths` via fnmatch, replacing the two regexes. (2) Fact-keyed rules, not phrase-keyed: genesis/cycle/ceiling/source-count rules in `check_doc_facts.py`/`check_memory_body_facts.py` match the VALUE (any ISO date within ±60 days of genesis in a genesis-context sentence; any integer adjacent to 'sources'/'lambdas'/'alarms') with the owner registry as oracle, scope extended to MEMORY.md, CLAUDE.md prose, `.claude/skills/**` and gate header comments; the #2376 wall-clock sweep extended to tests/js and to 'a hand literal duplicating a derived value in the same test' (principal-03). (3) Wrap rule: any number in the status block that a doc-facts rule owns is emitted by `sync_doc_metadata --render-status` and pasted, never typed — the wrap skill (b) step names it.
prevention.where: tests/test_ci_mirror_derivation.py (new family, sibling of tests/test_docs_ci_owns_doc_gates.py), deploy/wait_pr_green.sh (derive_expected_checks reads YAML), scripts/check_doc_facts.py + scripts/check_memory_body_facts.py (value-keyed rules, widened scope), scripts/check_wall_clock_fixtures.py (#2376) scope, .claude/skills/wrap/SKILL.md step (b)
prevention.negative_control: Remove one gate from wrap_gates.py's derived list → the ⊇ test reds; set EXPERIMENT_START_DATE to 2026-09-06 in a scratch tree → MEMORY.md 'genesis 2026-09-04' and CLAUDE.md prose red under the value rule, with a mutation proof that the old phrase-only rule stays green on the same input (the positive control that the fix is real); hand-type '1,500' beside a GOALS-derived assertion → the fixture sweep reds.
prevention.missing_primitive: Derivation guard (primitive 2) — the registries exist (workflow YAML, constants.py, source_registry, CDK schedules); the consumers restated them.

root_cause_classes.name: Reset-time verification is a snapshot; scheduled writers re-populate what the reset emptied and provenance is stamped from a constant
root_cause_classes.thesis: The reset is the platform's highest-frequency, highest-blast-radius operation — 15 cycles, 12 of them since 07-12, roughly one every five days — and it is verified once, at T+0 (handover: 'rendered 96/96 · semantic 8/8 · truth clean at ~16:5xZ'). Between that snapshot and Day 1, scheduled writers run on their own clocks with no knowledge of the reset: the chronicle 48h sweep selects by status+age and republished a tombstoned draft at 18:00:44Z (CPO-1/NARR-1/R1), the recap writer committed RECAP#latest with no phase stamp (NARR-2), og_moments rebuilt share kits from the resurrected manifest (G-2), insight writers wrote pre-genesis rows the tagger had already passed (DA-7), coach emission stamped phase=experiment from SSM's already-bumped cycle constant before genesis (QS-1), coach_state_updater stamped CROSS_PHASE rows (DA-6), the archive step no-op'd on a slug collision every reset since cycle 4 (G-1/NARR-5), frozen prologue artifacts carried the prior baseline for the third reset (CTO-3), and the reset regen + re-anchor regen tripped a Sum/day alarm (OBS-6). 39 of 99 findings and 6 of 7 P1s live in this window. No review had ever run in it (every prior review was Day 1–6), `restart_verify` has no time dimension, and the #3390 Day-1 runlist is owner-attended.
root_cause_classes.why_existing_gates_missed: restart_verify (23 checks) asserts lead-ins and rendered pages at reset time and stops; the #2109 phase-filter ratchet covers readers that use `with_phase_filter` and cannot see a writer's raw `table.query`; `assert_registry_coverage` enumerates from a hand-typed id list (DA-2); the tagger runs once, before the writers it was meant to cover (DA-7); the wipe stamps tombstone/phase but leaves `status=draft`, and the sweep's 10-day age guard reads a 3-day-old draft as live; the reset pipeline's own sweep runs against the working tree so history-keyed gates cannot see it (DEVEX-6).

prevention.what: (1) Writer-side set guard: an AST test over lambdas/ that every `put_item`/`update_item`/`query` on an EXPERIMENT_SCOPED partition (derived from `phase_taxonomy.classify()`, not a list) routes through `with_phase_filter`/`experiment_stamp` with phase derived from date-vs-genesis, not from the SSM cycle constant; the narrative verdict's set-guard and the QS verdict's derivation change, as one gate. (2) Reset totality from the live census: `assert_registry_coverage` and the pipeline's step-0 scan assert every `classify()==EXPERIMENT_SCOPED` pk family is in the wipe's covered set, and the inverse census (no CROSS_PHASE row tombstoned, no scoped row dated < genesis without phase=pilot, cycle stamps agree with `closing_cycle_for_genesis`) runs as a step-N gate. (3) The wipe voids the drafts it tombstones (status → superseded) and restart_verify asserts the sweep's candidate set is empty post-reset. (4) A T+writers re-verify: `restart_verify_rendered` + `restart_verify_truth` re-run automatically after the first scheduled-writer window (a `workflow_dispatch`/scheduled Actions job on public-repo minutes, or the #3390 runlist's re-curl) with the assertions 'every live week-NN permalink ∈ posts.json', 'moments/index.json ⊆ posts.json', 'newest posts.json entry does not predate genesis while day_n ≥ 0'.
prevention.where: tests/test_scoped_writers_route_through_phase.py (new AST set-guard), lambdas/experiment/phase_taxonomy.py (assert_registry_coverage derives from classify), deploy/restart_intelligence_wipe.py (void drafts), deploy/restart_verify.py (step-N census + candidate-set-empty), .github/workflows/restart-reverify.yml or the #3390 runlist (T+writers re-run), deploy/restart_pipeline.py post-override checklist (frozen-artifact sweep)
prevention.negative_control: Plant a chronicle row with tombstone=True, phase=pilot, status=draft, generated_at 3 days ago in the sweep's unit fixture → `_find_stale_drafts` must return empty (must-fail today); add a `table.query` on a COACH# partition without the phase filter in a scratch module → the AST guard reds; add a new `COACH#foo_ledger` pk family in a fixture → coverage assertion reds until the wipe covers it; run restart_verify at T+0 → green, run the T+writers pass with the planted resurrected post live → red on the permalink assertion.
prevention.missing_primitive: Derivation guard (writers derive 'publishable'/'phase' from the phase registry, not from status/constant) and dead-man (nothing re-asserts the reset's output after the writers run) — primitives 2 and 5.
prevention.rent_estimate: $0 AWS — tests, reset-script assertions, and one public-repo Actions re-run per reset

detection.what: Nightly `qa_smoke_lambda` (already paid for) gains three deterministic checks: served /journal/posts.json == the DDB visible chronicle set (the #3485 dead-man, extended), moments/index.json ⊆ posts.json, and a pre-genesis provenance census (no scoped row filter-visible with sk-date < genesis and no phase). Runs inside the existing nightly invocation — one more Query and one more S3 GetObject.
