root_cause_classes.name: Vocabulary copies outside the conformance guard's vocabularies and roots — a consumer hand-types a registry fact (genesis, phase, day, count, cadence, roster) and the charter's change bar is a sentence, not a check
root_cause_classes.thesis: CHARTER rule 1 is enforced by #2844's AST sweep of lambdas/mcp/cdk keyed on four vocabularies (sources, personas, lambda names, alarm names). Everything else the platform calls a registry fact is copied by hand where that sweep does not look: /api/explain builds its own phase line; coaching-dashboard hard-codes data_phase='established'; the brief collapses source_registry's paused/lag facets to a binary; the onboarding email labels 'Week {n}' ignoring the manifest's label; the confirmation email says '19 sources' while public_stats says 20 and og-home derives 22; /subscribe/ promises one Wednesday email against three CDK schedules; a supplement blurb says 117 lb against the hero's 140; the survival caption says n=2 beside a computed 15; receipts drop the projection's scope the SSM payload carries; coach_state_updater stamps phase onto CROSS_PHASE rows; insight writers never adopted tag_record. Each is the derivation-guard primitive skipped on a CONSUMER, and /new-machinery is invoked for 'durable machinery', not for a template or an endpoint that restates a fact.
root_cause_classes.why_existing_gates_missed: #2844's vocabulary set and root set are both narrower than the platform's registry facts; check_doc_facts.py owns docs prose only and its GENESIS_ANCHOR is phrase-keyed ('currently <date>'); the change bar says an off-charter PR 'needs to say so' — a self-declaration nothing reads; there is no Decimal-coercion derivation guard at all; the pre-start contract sweep covers the doors it was written for, per tab (#949 shape).

prevention.what: Extend tests/test_conformance_guard_2844.py: vocabularies += genesis/cycle/day literals (EXPERIMENT_START_DATE and CYCLE_GENESES values as strings), platform counts (platform_counts.DISCOVERED_COUNTS keys and values), subscriber send cadence (email_stack schedule literals), the operational coach roster (persona_registry), phase labels (the build_experiment_phase_context vocabulary); roots += config/, deploy/, site/assets/js/, lambdas/emails templates, tests/js. Every pre-existing hit lands in tests/conformance_residue.py with a date and reason (shrink-only). Add the Decimal derivation guard: every put_item(Item=…)/update_item argument must flow through floats_to_decimal/tag_record/parse_float=Decimal or an allowlisted literal-only dict (the mypy_clean_set idiom). The change bar becomes a CI finding, not a sentence.

forensics.evidence_quality: Established (reproduced read-only this session): gate census 597/50 proven/538 unproven with BASELINE_UNPROVEN_GATES=541 (tests/test_gate_census_lane_3000.py:499); 1,056 test files, 189 source-scanning, 114 with a control/mutation token (my grep proxy — cruder than the review's 101/35 heuristic, which I did NOT re-run); 465 guard files added since 2026-08-05, 461 via squash-merge; 771 PRs in 31 days; last-100 merged PRs open→merge p50 61 min / p90 290 min; no code-review workflow in .github/workflows; ruleset 21867590 requires one job + gitleaks with an always-bypass User actor; deploy/agent_commit.sh has 0 pytest references and the pre-commit hook is black+ruff; PR template checkbox text; #3477's closing comment ('realized', Docs-CI-scoped Outcome); #3473/#3474/#3390 acceptance boxes (only #3473 asks for a proof); the process verdicts read twice. Inferred, not established: (1) my 37/15/47 instrument-vs-product split of the 99 is judgment from summaries and class text, not machine-derived, and several members sit in two classes (OBS-1, OBS-4, CPO-2 appear in more than one list because their mechanism has two halves) — a different reader could move ~10 findings; (2) I did not read the 84 path-to-A actions in full (skimmed the first entries), so some prevention items above may duplicate an action already filed under #3489–#3498 — the class rules, not the instance fixes, are what I claim is new; (3) open→merge time is a proxy for review depth, not a measurement of it, and I could not establish which PRs were merged by their own authoring session; (4) the ~$0.80/mo rent for the class-6 dead-man is inferred from CloudWatch list pricing and CPO-2's own estimate, not measured on the account; (5) the incident log's 'silent' field — the /incident skill claims 51 of 184 rows were silent, but the table format I read has no such column, so I could not reproduce that number; (6) the 'why memory does not stop it' argument rests on the skills' own text and the recurrence counts the memory index records, plus DEVEX-5 — I did not measure how often /prove-it or /new-machinery are invoked per guard PR (no invocation log exists to read); (7) whether the four blocked PRs (#3580/81/83/88) already land part of class 4's stand-in derivation I could not tell without reading them, so class 4's prevention is stated as the class rule (enumerate every stand-in and every push site) rather than the instance.

redteam.persona: Cost engineer — owner of the $215/mo ceiling (ADR-063/133) and the PROPORTIONALITY ledger (ADR-103/144). I price every standing-rent proposal at list (alarm $0.10/mo, custom metric series $0.30/mo — this account is far past the 10-free tier, so a MetricFilter's output metric is NOT free; DDB on-demand reads ~$0.25/M; Logs Insights $0.005/GB scanned; public-repo Actions minutes $0), flag anything above ~2% of the bill ($3.50/mo on August's $175.85, $4.30 on the ceiling), and ask which existing rent this exercise retires. Anchor fact: CloudWatch went $4.84 (Mar) → $24.50 (Jul) → $31.45 (Aug), a 6.5x climb produced entirely by alarms and metric series that each individually cost 'nothing'.

class_verdicts.class_name: SDLC-A. The ungated landing path
class_verdicts.reason: Three analysts describe one class with the same numbers (145 direct pushes since 08-22 — I re-counted: 310 PR / 156 bot / 145 direct). Prevention is FREE in AWS terms but not in session terms: 155s x ~10 direct pushes/day ≈ 26 min/day of blocked session wall-clock, and the reset pipeline + wrap each pay it too. The premerge lane on a docs-only wrap commit is waste.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Split the hook by touched paths: docs-only pushes run docs_ci_gate_commands() (seconds); code-touching direct pushes are REFUSED by agent_commit.sh --push (route to a PR) rather than tested locally — the PR lane already exists and its minutes are free. Only the reset pipeline keeps the derived artifact-reader pytest set (#3477's python leg). Net: zero new local CPU on 83 of 145 direct pushes, and the 38 fix( direct pushes stop existing.

class_verdicts.class_name: SDLC-B. Point-in-time verification of a surface scheduled writers keep rewriting
class_verdicts.merge_with: K2 reset↔writer contract (SDLC-B + EM-5 + DA-C1 + DA-C2 + DA-C6)
class_verdicts.reason: Five analysts, one mechanism: the reset verifies the read side once at T0 and 104 schedules write afterwards. The nightly qa-smoke legs are priced right (~40 key-bounded queries + ~10 HEADs inside an already-paid Lambda ≈ $0.003/mo) — I accept STANDING_RENT ≈ $0. The one hidden cost: a 'T+writers re-verify' that re-runs restart_verify_truth pays the reader-truth judge again ($0.195/run x ~6 resets/mo ≈ $1.20/mo). Keep the re-verify deterministic (rendered + semantic), no AI pass.

class_verdicts.class_name: SDLC-C. Instruments that cannot fail, closed on the merge
class_verdicts.reason: Prevention (closure-contract rule 7, IAM-parity set test, never-fired ratchet, UNEVALUATED judge outcome) is FREE and right. The detection is mis-priced: '4 metric filters (free tier)' is wrong on this account — 4 filters emit 4 custom metrics = $1.20/mo, + 2 alarms $0.20, + the CommitmentsGraded pair $0.60 + $0.10 ≈ $2.10/mo. Under 2% alone, but Oracle-6 and EM-2 propose the same filters again with different function lists; if all three land the estate grows by 4–8 series and 3–5 alarms.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: (a) The AccessDenied sub-class (INT-1, G-3, OBS-1) is closed at PR time by the role-family IAM-parity test — no runtime detector needed for it. (b) For the residual 'logged ERROR every run' class: ONE Logs Insights query in the weekly drift sentinel (config-drift.yml, Actions minutes free) — `stats count() by @log where level=ERROR` over /aws/lambda/life-platform-* for 7d; the four checkers' logs are megabytes, so <$0.01/week, zero standing series, zero alarms. (c) CPO-2's dead-man is a DDB count (due>0 ∧ graded==0 for 14d) as a qa-smoke check riding FailCount — $0, not a metric pair + alarm.

One caution: four analysts each propose a slightly different structural test over tests/ (positive-control rule, scan-set rule, comparand-derivation rule, guard-entry-control). Land ONE file, not four; four overlapping AST sweeps over 1,056 test files is the same accretion pattern in CI seconds instead of dollars.

missing_classes.name: M1. An alarm or metric that cannot fire is pure rent — the alarm ESTATE has no ratchet
missing_classes.evidence: CloudWatch is the second-largest line on the bill and the fastest-growing: $4.84 (Mar) → $9.56 (Apr) → $24.50 (Jul) → $31.45 (Aug), +28% MoM, 18% of August's $175.85 (docs/COST_TRACKER.md rows 209–214). ~119 alarms (PROPORTIONALITY row 173: '11 of 119') ≈ $12/mo before metric series. The review found members of this estate that can never fire (CTO-2: site-api-ai-errors ≥3/hr on ~8 requests/week), that mute themselves (OBS-5: 14-day Maximum≥1), that trip on their own regen (OBS-6), that claim a cadence they don't have (CTO-4/OBS-7), and a qa-smoke check chronic for 30+ days (OBS-1) — every one ledgered as load-bearing. There is no derivation guard from the synthesized template to the ledger (alarm count / custom-metric-series count may only grow with a row and a reachability proof), and the monthly close (#3375) prints tier residence but never the CloudWatch line's composition. Missing primitive: RATCHET on the alarm/metric estate. FREE: tests/test_alarm_threshold_reachability.py (already proposed) + a synthesized-template census of Alarm and MetricFilter resources asserted against the ledger's row count, shrink-or-justify; monthly_close.py prints CloudWatch $ and the series/alarm counts so the growth is visible the month it happens.

missing_classes.name: M2. Rent whose demote trigger has no clock — the PROPORTIONALITY ledger is prose the calendar never probes
missing_classes.evidence: PROPORTIONALITY row 52 (the 2026-08-27 re-read): 'Two triggers had already fired unnoticed' — fresh-eyes' revisit trigger fired 07-26 and was noticed 08-27; the reader-truth ledger's demote clock runs to 09-26 with no probe. Row 133 calls it 'the cleanest instance on this ledger of a trigger with a bar but no clock'. The review's OBS-7, DEVEX-8, COST-01 ('a revisit clause that has no carrier'), a11y-3 (stale in the good direction), G-8 (a lifecycle with no terminal transition) are the same shape inside instruments. Every standing-rent proposal in this exercise carries a demote trigger — and every one of them will rot exactly this way unless the trigger is machine-readable. Missing primitive: DEAD-MAN on the ledger row. FREE: a `demote_by:` (ISO date) or `demote_when:` (a named metric + condition) token required on every Load-bearing row by check_doc_facts, and scripts/operating_calendar.py's daily probe reds any row past its date — the same mechanism that already dead-mans rituals, pointed at rent.

missing_classes.name: M3. The QA estate is the AI bill — detectors that call a model are the cost class the exercise must not grow
missing_classes.evidence: August: ci $14.38 + dev-session $0.20 = 63% of the $23.19 stamped window; the reader-truth judge alone is $0.195/fire (~$5.85/mo), vision QA $0.0475 x 6.7 deploys/day (~$9.50/mo) + $0.53/Sunday, the remediation agent ≈ $7/mo all triggers (PROPORTIONALITY rows 126, 132). Uncached input was 57% of Bedrock. AIQ-2 shows two of those judges returned 'ok' on a missing verdict — $15/mo of judges that could not fail. The analysts mostly propose deterministic rules (good), but the CTO path-to-A proposes doubling the public-AI probe cadence (3x/week → daily: 4 more full board_ask invocations/week, unpriced) and a T+writers re-run of the AI truth pass would add ~$1.20/mo. Missing primitive: the CONTRACT that a deterministic rule is tried before a model verdict (ADR-105's own ordering) applied to detectors. FREE: any new detector that calls bedrock_client must carry a CallerClass and a PROPORTIONALITY row before it is scheduled — a test over cdk schedules and workflow crons that every AI-calling detector is ledgered.

missing_classes.name: M4. Reset frequency is the platform's largest defect generator and its cost is not on any ledger
missing_classes.evidence: 12 resets in 55 days (CYCLE_GENESES); 39 of 99 findings and 6 of 7 P1s live in the reset window; DV-1/R3's 47% survival odds are the reset frequency leaking into a public statistic. Each reset burns a visual-qa full pass ($0.53), an AI truth pass ($0.195), three CDK deploys with per-deploy vision QA, a prereg freeze, and — per this review — ~40 defects. PROPORTIONALITY row 86 prices the reset machinery for 'a few times a quarter'. No row prices the reset EVENT. This is not machinery to build; it is an owner-facing number to print: the monthly close should carry 'resets this month: N, $ per reset, findings-per-reset from the last review' so the cheapest prevention on the platform — fewer resets — is a priced decision rather than a habit.

over_engineering_flags.proposal: Per-function logged-ERROR MetricFilters + digest alarms on the operational checkers (proposed independently by SDLC-C, Oracle-6, EM-2, and the integrations path-to-A)
over_engineering_flags.why: Every analyst wrote 'metric filters are free tier'. On this account they are not: the free tier is 10 custom metrics and this platform emits dozens of series across 10 LifePlatform/* namespaces plus ~119 alarms. Each filter's output metric is $0.30/mo. Four analysts x slightly different function lists = 4–8 series + 3–5 alarms if all land.
over_engineering_flags.rent_if_kept: $1.20–2.40/mo series + $0.30–0.50/mo alarms ≈ $1.50–2.90/mo (0.9–1.7% of August's bill), plus 4–8 more rows in an estate already growing 28% MoM
over_engineering_flags.alternative: The AccessDenied sub-class (INT-1, G-3, OBS-1) is closed at PR time by the role-family IAM-parity test — no runtime rent. For the residual, ONE Logs Insights query in the weekly drift sentinel over /aws/lambda/life-platform-* (`level=ERROR` count by @log, 7d): <$0.01/week, zero standing series, rides free Actions minutes. Weekly latency is acceptable for a class that sat 49 days.

over_engineering_flags.proposal: qa-smoke emits failing check ids as a CloudWatch dimension so check_alarm_citations can read the cause without log scraping (CTO path-to-A #4)
over_engineering_flags.why: A dimension per check id is a metric SERIES per check id: 11 checks today plus the ~6 new legs K2 proposes.

The review is priced in owner hours and Claude Code tokens, the scarcest resource here, and it is being pointed at a 5-day event cadence.

framing_critique.what_is_wrong: (1) 'What would have needed to happen to stop them going to production' names the wrong boundary. By the SDLC analyst's stage forensics ~58% of the 99 entered at implementation where NO gate existed to bypass, ~18% entered AFTER production — written by scheduled writers into a surface that was green at deploy time — and 13% were closed-on-merge instruments that were in production and non-functional for 21–49 days. The gate that was missing is not 'before prod'; it is 'before the next scheduled writer' (K2), 'before the issue closes' (K3), and 'before the guard is trusted' (K4). (2) 'Do another full review exactly the same and hit all A grades' is incoherent for at least five lenses on the rubric's own terms: three A anchors (cto, observability, and the $85 envelope wording) hand-type a ceiling that has been $215 since 09-01 — the rubric carries a DEVEX-5-class stale literal; narrative's A anchor says 'one coherent cycle-6 story' (the platform is on cycle 16); cpo/reader/growth anchors are testable only on Day ≥4 of a cycle and the baseline ran on Day 0; qs's 'every bet graded or voided across resets' needs bets that live 30 days on a platform that reset every 4.6 days. An identical re-run on an identical day would re-measure the same structural impossibilities. (3) The over-engineering exception is framed as a per-AREA scrutiny gate, but rent enters per-INSTRUMENT and by accretion: no single proposal here exceeds 2%, yet the four analysts' standing-rent items sum to ≈$7–9/mo (4–5% of the bill) if all land, and CloudWatch already grew 6.5x since March one 'free' alarm at a time. The ledger for this exists (ADR-144, PROPORTIONALITY) — the framing should invoke it, not restate it.
framing_critique.what_to_add: (a) TIME as a grading axis: every anchor states the day-of-cycle it can be observed on, and the review artifact records day-of-cycle at run; a grade is 'A on day N'. (b) The RETIREMENT question, explicitly: this exercise should name rent it removes — the two unreachable Errors alarms (CTO-2), the saturating interior-gap alarm (OBS-5), the chronic qa-smoke check (OBS-1), the remediation agent's demote clock (~$7/mo, OBS-3 shows its needs-human lines repeat verbatim), the fresh-eyes board (trigger due 11-27), and — once DA-C3 lands — the countdown-gap sweep and the nightly census it makes redundant. (c) A machine-readable demote clock on every PROPORTIONALITY row (M2), because every standing-rent proposal above carries a prose trigger that will rot the way row 52 documents. (d) The reset EVENT priced on the monthly close (M4): resets/month, $/reset, findings/reset — the cheapest prevention on the platform is an owner decision that currently has no number in front of it. (e) The rule that a deterministic check precedes any model-based detector (M3) — the AI bill is 63% QA/dev already.
framing_critique.what_to_drop: Drop 'exactly the same' and 'all A': replace with 'the executable half of each A anchor becomes a nightly or CI check ($0 where deterministic), the review grades the residual judgement, and anchors are re-derived from live constants before the next full run'. Drop 'why did we have silent issues' as a question about vigilance: silence is the workflow's default output (a direct push meets a formatter, a merge closes the issue, a fail-soft write logs non-fatal, a citation matches by name, a guard is counted whether or not it can fail) and no memory entry changes a default — only a gate on the path does. Drop 'stop them going to production' in favour of the three boundaries above. And drop the assumption that 13 grade drops are decay: every lens's A anchor was EXTENDED onto the Day-0 surface on the day it ran, so part of the drop is a legitimately raised bar on a surface no prior review had ever observed.

redteam.the_70_answer: One review found 70 because it was the first instrument in 20 days that asked 'does it work live, today, after the reset' — a question that has no owner in the workflow and costs nothing to ask nightly. Per-lens yield was flat (5.9 → 3.9 → 5.8 findings per lens across 08-09, 08-16, 09-05); what changed was that 17 lenses ran instead of 7, ten of them carried forward unmeasured since late July across ~600 main commits a fortnight and twelve resets, and the run landed on Day 0 of a reset — the one instant when every pre-start, phase and tombstone branch is exercised at once and the reset's own T0-green had already been rewritten by the 18:00Z writers. Underneath, silence is the default output of how work lands here: 145 of 455 human commits since 08-22 were direct pushes that meet a formatter and nothing else; an issue closes on merge nine hours after filing while its fail-soft write is IAM-denied for 49 days; 538 of 597 gates have never been shown to fail; a citation is matched by alarm name; a delta review assumes unchanged diff means unchanged grade on a platform whose defects come from schedules and resets, not diffs. The fix is not seventy repairs and it is not new machinery — every class above closes for $0 with a test, a ratchet, a template line or a nightly leg inside a Lambda you already pay for, and the two things that would actually reduce the count next month are owner decisions with no dollar sign on them today: stop landing code by direct push, and put a price on a reset before doing the next one. The only money in this whole exercise is the money to STOP spending — the alarms that cannot fire, the judges that return 'ok' on nothing, and the $7/mo triage email whose lines repeat verbatim — and the one number to watch is the CloudWatch line, which has grown 6.5x since March one free alarm at a time and would grow again if all four analysts' 'free tier' filters land together.
redteam.path_to_A_reality_check: FREE to A (tests, ratchets, derivations, skill edits; no rent): principal (pre-push/refuse-code-direct-push, derived fixtures, dead-def guard reach — all FREE; the $85 in no anchor here), devex (mirror-derivation family, value-keyed fact rules, wrap render-status — FREE; its A anchor 'incident classes encoded in gates rather than memory' is exactly K4), designer (registry-derived page sets for scroll/text-floor, JS hex sweep — FREE), dataviz (charts.js node contract, method object, coverage_hold — FREE), a11y (token pairs in both themes landed #3544/5; ledger `issue` rule + shrink-list read at wrap — FREE; the per-deploy light-context axe pass is free in dollars but ~3 min of deploy-lease per deploy at 6.7 deploys/day — put it on the daily standalone fire instead), reader (structural draft filter, cast scan set, survival bound — FREE), aiq (UNEVALUATED outcome, temporal rule as a deterministic freshness member, inventory derived from facets — FREE; its judge rent is already paid and should not grow), data-architect (writer set guard, live census as the required set, CoOwned entries — FREE; the 26-row reconcile is a one-off DDB write the owner approves), cost (COST-02/03/04 are field additions inside an existing GetMetricData batch — FREE; #3373's kill switch is L effort but $0; #2883 is an owner close). NEEDS RENT or an accepted rent decision: observability — A is reachable only if the 'every watchdog producer verified emitting' anchor is met by the IAM-parity test at CI ($0) rather than by runtime ERROR filters ($1.50–2.90/mo); the honest A here also REMOVES rent (CTO-2's two alarms re-thresholded, OBS-5 via marker) — and the anchor's own '$85 ceiling' literal must be re-derived to $215 before it can be graded; cto — same stale $85 literal in the anchor; ARCHITECTURE derived (#3509 done), DLQ parity from the synthesized template ($0), alarm reachability ($0); reachable FREE once the anchor is corrected. NEEDS AN OWNER ACT: integrations (the notion-sentinel grant or pk move + the chronicle-sender PutItem are cdk deploys of IAM — ask-first by the owner's own rule; Garmin 'a dead OAuth token pages within one cadence' is vendor-paused per ADR-074 and no code reaches A on it — the anchor should say 'or is disclosed as paused', which it partly does), security (SEC-4's remediation-role JSON is applied by the owner per #3336; SEC-1's prefix move touches the bucket policy), narrative and cpo (their A anchors are only observable on Day ≥4 with a cycle old enough to have seams — a Day-0 identical re-run cannot grade them A by construction; narrative's anchor also hand-types 'cycle-6'), qs ('every bet graded or voided across resets' requires bets that reach their windows, i.e. a cycle that survives longer than 4.6 days — the reset cadence, an owner act, is the blocker, not code), growth (C+ → A needs subscriber conversion in the weekly digest and a cadence that matches the promise — a product decision on send days — plus 'commercial option value real and measured', which is market outcome, not engineering; growth cannot reach A by any PR). WHAT 'AN IDENTICAL RE-RUN HITS ALL A' WOULD ACTUALLY REQUIRE: (1) re-derive the anchors first — three carry a stale ceiling literal and one a stale cycle number, so an identical run would grade against false bars; (2) run it on the same day-of-cycle it was run, which for cpo/reader/narrative/growth means grading anchors that state 'Day 4' on Day 0 — incoherent; the honest form is 'A on day N' with N recorded; (3) accept that qs, narrative and cpo cannot hold A across a reset cadence faster than their evidence windows — either the cadence changes (owner) or those anchors carry an explicit 'per cycle ≥ 30 days' precondition; (4) make the executable half of every anchor a $0 nightly/CI check so the grade is the checks' verdict on any day rather than a panel's verdict on one day; (5) fund nothing: the sum of all standing rent above, taken with the cheaper alternatives, is ≈$0.50/mo, and the exercise should net NEGATIVE on the CloudWatch line by retiring the alarms that cannot fire and demoting the instruments whose clocks have already run out.

redteam.persona: Distinguished Engineer, hiring-panel cold read. I infer the process from the defects: 597 gates with 50 proven (12:1), 465 guard files in 30 days, 771 PRs in 31 days at p50 61 min open→merge, 16 geneses with 12 resets in 55 days, 403 memory files with 85 review-discipline entries, no second reader on any PR, and half of main landing by a path with no test between the terminal and main. The individual work is careful; the SYSTEM is one where instrument creation runs ~10x ahead of instrument verification, every defect is answered by minting another instrument, nothing ever retires one, and closure happens at merge rather than at first live output. The four analysts diagnosed this correctly and then — in aggregate — proposed ~50 more instruments, most of them gates-over-gates. That reflex is the pathology, not the cure.

class_verdicts.class_name: A1-A / A2-4 / A3-1: The ungated landing path (direct push, reset pipeline, wrap commit meet only black+ruff)
class_verdicts.reason: The one class all four analysts converge on and the one I re-verified end to end: .git/hooks/ has commit-msg + pre-commit only; deploy/agent_commit.sh contains no pytest; PR template line 19 literally instructs the behaviour that redded main twice on 09-04 (HANDOVER_LATEST.md). principal-01 (26/29 red Unit-Test runs were direct pushes), principal-02 (both resets in the window redded main), DEVEX-1/2/3. This is structural change #1: ONE landing path. A pre-push hook running `pytest -m 'premerge and not integration'` plus the AST-derived deploy/generated/** reader set, the same derived doc-gate list for wrap and reset via the existing docs_ci_gate_commands(), docs-ci/v4-gate concurrency keyed on sha, and the PR template line replaced. FREE. Negative control: a planted premerge red on a branch whose upstream is main → push refused with the test named. Merge A2-4 and A3-1 into this; they are the same class stated three ways. Drop the separate weekly 'red direct-push count' detectors — after the hook lands they read 0 by construction; fold into the existing wrap (e2) main-green gate.

class_verdicts.class_name: A1-B / A3-5 / A4-C1 / A4-C2 / A4-C5: Point-in-time reset verification while scheduled writers rewrite the surface (the reset↔writer seam)
class_verdicts.reason: The class is real and owns 6 of 7 P1s (CPO-1, NARR-1, NARR-2, R1, G-1, QS-1) plus DA-6/7/9, NARR-5, CTO-3, OBS-6. But the analysts' primary prevention — an AST set-guard over the 69–112 raw put/query callers with a 31–69-entry shrink-only residue ledger — is the biggest FREE-but-expensive item in the whole panel. The P1s close with three edits that touch no writer: (1) the wipe flips status→voided on every draft it tombstones (restart_intelligence_wipe.build_update) so a status-keyed selector cannot re-select it; (2) experiment_stamp()/tag_record derive phase from as_of vs EXPERIMENT_START_DATE, never from the SSM cycle constant (A4-C3); (3) the existing #3485 nightly served⊆visible contract extended to moments/index.json and 'newest entry ≥ genesis while day_n ≥ 0'. Keep A4-C2's per-step work contract ({input, acted, skipped}; acted==0 with input>0 is red) — it is the cheapest dead-man for NARR-5/G-1 and the actual archive_one fix. Keep A4-C5's 'step-0 census artifact is the required set' — a derivation fix, not a new instrument. Correct PROPORTIONALITY.md:86 ('a few times a quarter' vs 12 resets/55 days) as an ADR-104 honesty fix. Defer the writer-side AST guard until those three have survived two resets; if the nightly contract reads zero across them, the guard is measuring a seam that no longer exists.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: voided-at-wipe + date-derived stamp + extend the existing #3485 nightly check (~$0 marginal, already scheduled). No writer AST sweep, no residue ledger, no new Actions workflow (A3-5's restart-reverify.yml is a new mirror to derive — the #3390 cloud routine and qa_smoke already exist).

class_verdicts.class_name: A4-C3: Pre-start is not a phase the registry knows (provenance from a constant/SSM, tense from per-surface preStart())
class_verdicts.reason: The one genuinely MISSING REGISTRY VALUE in the whole panel, and the highest leverage per line of code proposed anywhere: QS-1, DA-7, AIQ-3/6/8, NARR-3, CPO-3/4, DV-4/5 all derive from 'phase = constant' and 'pre-start re-derived on every surface'. Primitive 2 had nothing to derive from. Fix: experiment_stamp(as_of) derives from date; the coach emission chain refuses gradeable PREDICTION#/COMMITMENT# writes while pre_start; season⊆frozen contract against the committed prereg; every phase line through build_experiment_phase_context (#1086). FREE. Negative control: a write with as_of = genesis−1 that lands phase=experiment fails; the live 'since the September 5th reset' sentence with gen_date 09-04 is the positive control. Do not fold this into the reset class — its fix location and missing primitive are different.

class_verdicts.class_name: A1-C / A2-6 / A3-2: Instruments that cannot fail, closed on the merge (fail-soft paths, mocked transport, closure by comment shape)
class_verdicts.reason: The class is real and expensive: INT-1 (49 days), G-3 (28 days), OBS-1, CPO-2 (21 runs of kept=0 broken=0), DA-1, AIQ-2, all closed with green tests over a fake wire; closure_contract.py:89 is 'warn' with no live-output requirement; #3477 closed 'realized' and recurred the same day. But three analysts proposed three different closure rules (A1 'first-live-observation', A2 'set-named' + 'first-output-observed', A3 'first-live-output') for one idea. Structural change #4: ONE closure rule — when the closing PR's diff touches a fail-soft site, an alarm, a scheduled instrument, or a new AWS verb (AST-detectable), the close must carry 'first non-degraded output observed at <UTC> — <where>' or the verdict is partial and the issue stays open. Take A3's scoping: flip THAT code to block immediately (the false-positive cost is one reopened issue, never a lost fix) and leave the rest of the contract on the existing FLIP_BAR. Keep the IAM-parity contract generalised from tests/test_freshness_checker_iam_parity.py to every LeadingKeys-scoped role — it is a contract test on the REAL wire, it fails today on INT-1 and G-3 by construction, and it is the one proposal that turns 'fixture must be the wire' from a memory entry into a red. Kill the 'never-fired ratchet' (a qa-smoke check chronic for 30 days, a grader with graded==0) as a separate test — the ONE closure rule plus the fleet ERROR filter (below) cover it.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: One closure rule, one IAM-parity test family, one fleet-wide ERROR MetricFilter (not four per-function ones).

class_verdicts.class_name: A1-D / A2-3 / A3-3: Guard the instance, not the set (hand-picked scan sets, no positive control)
class_verdicts.reason: The most-recurring lesson in the memory index (10+) and 26 findings here (OBS-4, DES-2/4, SEC-1/2, R2, INT-3, DA-2, a11y-1/2/6, CTO-5, principal-08, AIQ-1 …). The analysts are right about the class and wrong about the closer. Their SCAN-SET RULE — extend #2844's conformance vocabularies to 'hand-typed lists inside tests/ scripts/ deploy/' — is not AST-detectable without a vocabulary; every legitimate literal list trips it and the residue ledger (36 today) becomes hundreds nobody shrinks. KILL that half. Keep two cheap things: (a) A3-3's `## Set` section on every bug/story filed from a review or incident (the enumeration expression + member count today, one mandatory acceptance box) linted by check_backlog_hygiene — this changes INTAKE, which is where the class enters, at zero machinery; (b) the six concrete set-fixes the analysts already name (AlarmTypes on every describe_alarms; DLQ on every Event-invoked target from the synthesized template; hex/matchMedia over site/assets/js; scrollY==0 + text floor over qa_manifest; cast-name scan over deploy/ + config/) as ORDINARY derived tests. Do the six, skip the meta-rule.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: `## Set` at intake + six registry-derived tests. No conformance-guard root expansion, no second residue ledger.

class_verdicts.class_name: A2-1: Born unproven — a guard enters with no must-fail case because the entry bar is an aggregate ceiling (BASELINE_UNPROVEN_GATES=541 vs 538 live)
class_verdicts.reason: The best-formulated proposal in the panel and the one I would make structural change #3. tests/test_gate_census_lane_3000.py:499 ceilings the AGGREGATE, so every proof written elsewhere buys a new unproven entrant ('prove one, mint one'). The fix is per-entrant: 'no gate id new since the committed baseline may be unproven' — this honours owner decision #3329 (no retroactive programme over the 538) while closing the entrance. FREE, one edit to an existing test. But I would pair it with what no analyst proposed: a DELETION quota. A guard nobody can name a must-fail for in five minutes is not proven — it is deleted. Proof costs sessions; deletion costs nothing and removes false green. Kill the companion 'test over tests/' family (A1-D's test_guard_positive_controls, A2-2's test_guard_comparand_derivation, A3-6's test_gate_census_ratchet) — three more meta-tests for the same idea, each with its own ~94-entry residue ledger. One per-entrant rule in the existing census test is the whole mechanism.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Edit check_unproven_ceiling to per-new-id; add a session rule 'every PR that adds a gate retires one unproven gate'; no new test files.

class_verdicts.class_name: A2-2: Self-referential oracle (mock of the subject, threshold copied from another surface, hand-typed mirror of a workflow)
class_verdicts.reason: Members are real (INT-1, G-3, CPO-2, CTO-2, DEVEX-4, COST-01/03, OBS-3, QS-1, DEVEX-5) but the three proposed guards vary wildly in cost. (a) Mock-of-subject AST detector ('patches the same symbol it asserts on') — KILL: every unit test patches collaborators; the false-positive surface is the whole suite. (b) IAM parity for every Lambda — KEEP, already merged into the closure class above. (c) Alarm thresholds must carry a derivation token checked against 'measured median hourly traffic' — MODIFY: measured traffic in CI means a CloudWatch read in CI (creds + rent) or a hand-typed traffic facet that rots (class E again). CTO-2's own corrected root cause says the canary is the real detector and the Errors alarm is a redundancy gap; the honest fix is threshold 1 with digest routing, or delete the alarm. (d) Workflow mirrors derive from YAML — KEEP, mostly landed by #3529/31/34; enrol wait_pr_green.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Errors alarms on multi-endpoint Lambdas → threshold 1 or delete; no reachability test with a traffic facet.

class_verdicts.class_name: A2-5 / A3-6 (waiver half): A waiver outlives its condition (citations by name, chronic warns forever, a11y baseline that disarms itself)
class_verdicts.reason: Small, sharp, FREE, and it closes CTO-3, OBS-2, OBS-7, a11y-3, a11y-6, OBS-1's chronic tag. Citations carry `cause` + `added`; check_alarm_citations fails any lit alarm whose StateTransitionedTimestamp > added or whose cause ≠ cited; a11y serious/critical entries require `issue` (the #2956 twin); chronic warns carry an expiry date past which they count. All at wrap (e10) and in tests. Negative control: a synthetic alarm transitioned after `added` → FAIL. This is the charter's dead-man applied to the ledger ENTRY, which is exactly the primitive that was missing. Kill the OBS-5 NewInteriorGapCount metric+alarm both A2 and A3 leave as optional rent — the condition it exists for may never occur; applying the #2643 absence marker to every DAILY_SOURCE (INT-3's fix) removes the saturation.

class_verdicts.class_name: A1-E / A2-7 / A3-4: Hand copies of a registry fact on reader-bound surfaces (templates, JSON, JS strings, email copy, MEMORY.md prose)
class_verdicts.reason: 18–21 members (G-4/5/6/9, CPO-5, AIQ-4/6/8, COST-02/03/04, CTO-4, INT-4, DEVEX-5/7, R5, DV-1, principal-03/07). The class is right; the proposed DETECTORS are the wrong shape. A1's 'served-string numeric rule' (any `<int> sources` / `n=<int>` in a served string must equal a field) and the value-keyed genesis regex over MEMORY.md/CLAUDE.md are phrase-matchers — the exact #2959/#3003/#3199 family the memory index says has failed in the field every time; DEVEX-5 IS the fifth specimen of a phrase-keyed guard. Prefer DERIVATION over DETECTION: templates render len(SOURCE_REGISTRY); captions render from the payload's n; the wrap status block's numbers come from `sync_doc_metadata --render-status` and are pasted, never typed (A3's proposal — keep it); /api/explain uses the shared phase block; the sender cadence is one function read by /subscribe/ and the confirmation email. Enrol the email template in the existing test_platform_stats_truth. Each member is a one-line derivation fix; the class closes when the literal no longer exists, not when a regex catches it.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Derive at the source; enrol templates in an existing truth test; render the status block. No served-string regex family, no value-keyed prose sweep.

class_verdicts.class_name: A2-7 (Decimal half): No derivation guard on float→Decimal at DDB writes (DA-1)
class_verdicts.reason: DA-1 is real (a crash AFTER the SES send, ledger row stuck 5 days) but 'AST-prove every put_item argument flows through floats_to_decimal' is data-flow analysis Python's ast will not give you reliably. Cheaper: one `ddb_put()/ddb_update()` wrapper in common that coerces, and a grep-level guard that no module outside the wrapper calls `.put_item(`/`.update_item(` directly — a shrink-only allowlist that starts at today's 112 files and only goes down. Plus the ledger-stuck check (rows at `attempting` > 24h) as one Query inside the existing nightly qa_smoke.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Wrapper + call-site allowlist; no flow analysis.

class_verdicts.class_name: A1-F / A4-C4: Arithmetic no gate can see (charts.js builders, stats core, ADR-105 as prose)
class_verdicts.reason: The only class that is genuinely DESIGN-stage and the only one where the fix is the cheapest kind of primitive — a contract test on a pure function. DV-1/2/3/6/7, R3, QS-3/4/5, COST-04. Node-executed charts.js contract test in the Unit Tests job (precedent tests/test_cockpit_scope_history_2672.py); the two-strata calibration fixture; the all-censored survival fixture (p30 ≤ Laplace prior); the horizon check on `cd is None` at site_api_rollups.py:712. Every negative control the analysts state fails against today's code — that is exactly what a contract test should do on day one. Detection: none — a scheduled probe on a pure function is rent for nothing, and the analysts said so.

framing_critique.what_is_wrong: (1) 'Why did we have silent issues? What caused them?' presumes events. Most of the 99 were not caused; they were the platform's steady state — INT-1 for 49 days, G-3 since 08-08, OBS-1 for 30+ days, DES-1 since #151, NARR-5 every reset since cycle 4. They were not silent; they were unobserved, because nothing in the workflow looks at the platform after the merge. (2) 'What would have needed to happen to stop them going to production?' — for ~58% (analyst 1's classes D/E/F) the honest answer is 'a gate that did not exist', and this platform's reflex to that answer is to mint the gate. That reflex produced 597 gates with 50 proven. Asking the question that way guarantees the 598th. (3) 'Do another full review exactly the same and hit all A' is incoherent as stated: every one of the 17 A anchors carries an EXTENSION written on the day of the review (extension_note on all 17 rows). A is the reviewer's frontier, not a fixed point; an identical re-run on Day N will extend the anchors again onto whatever Day N shows. The prior A- grades were also partly false (designer's A- was measured on 7 of 89 pages; 10 lenses were 'grades stand' for five weeks) — so part of '13 dropped' is prior grades being wrong, not the platform decaying. (4) The over-engineering exemption is scoped to 'running cost'. The over-engineering that actually hurt here is FREE: gates, ledgers, residue allowlists, memory entries cost $0 in AWS and are exactly what accumulated unscrutinised to 538 unproven. A cost-only exemption lets the disease through.
framing_critique.what_to_add: (a) A RATE question: how many resets, PRs, guards per week, and is verification keeping pace — the 12:1 gate:proof ratio and 12 resets/55 days are the two numbers that explain most of the 99. (b) A SECOND-READER question: who other than the authoring session looked at this before main? Today: nobody, p50 61 min. (c) A DELETION question: what did we retire this month? PROPORTIONALITY has demote triggers on every row; the framing should ask which were pulled. (d) ATTENTION as a cost class beside dollars: a FREE gate that reds on legitimate work, or a ledger nobody shrinks, is rent paid in session-hours and false green. (e) A TIME axis: 'does it still work at T+24h after a reset' — the one question no instrument asks and the review did.
framing_critique.what_to_drop: Drop 'hit all A grades on an identical re-run' as the target. It rewards anchor-gaming and is unreachable by construction for at least two lenses (narrative's A needs a multi-week coherent story that a weekly-reset cadence cannot produce; growth's A includes measured commercial value, which is a product posture, not engineering). Replace with a target the anchors cannot move: 'the next full review, run on Day 4+, confirms fewer than ~3 findings per lens (vs the 5.8/lens every prior run produced), zero P1s, and no confirmed finding whose class string cites a previously filed issue.' Also drop 'exactly the same' — the surface (Day N), the anchors and the reviewer will all differ; what should be the same is the METHOD (17 lenses, adversarial verification, set-wise, live).

redteam.the_70_answer: Because nothing in your workflow looks at the platform after the merge. Every instrument you own measures the diff, the merge, the closing comment's shape, or the count of gates — and almost every one of the 99 was a live effect: a write the role could not perform for 49 days, a cron that republished what the reset had erased ten hours earlier, a caption that stopped matching its own number, a floor armed on 3 of 89 pages, an alarm whose threshold its surface can never reach. The review was the first thing in twenty days that asked 'is it working, today, live' — on Day 0 of a reset, the one moment none of your 597 gates had ever sampled — and it asked set-wise instead of instance-wise. Add that half of main's commits arrive by a path with no test between the terminal and main, that issues close when the PR merges rather than when the thing first works, that 10 of 17 grades had been carried forward unmeasured for five weeks, and that the platform resets every five days while its verification is built for a quarterly event, and 70 is not a surprise. It is 5.8 findings per lens — the same yield every previous review produced. You ran 17 lenses instead of 7. The platform did not get worse in September; you finally measured all of it, at the worst instant, from the right side.
redteam.path_to_A_reality_check: HONESTLY FREE (engineering alone, no rent): principal (pre-push hook + derived artifact readers + per-entrant proof; 'no unreferenced code' and 'one canonical implementation' are deletions), devex (mirrors derive from YAML — mostly landed #3529/31/34; status block rendered not typed), qs (date-derived stamp, season⊆frozen, two-strata fixture, void-on-record — every item is a test or a one-line derivation), dataviz (charts.js node contract + four method objects), data-architect (census artifact as the required set, reconcile the 26 rows, Decimal wrapper), security (largely landed #3560-2; the remaining piece is an owner decision below), cost (receipts scope field + surge-flip line in monthly_close). The three reader-facing lenses — narrative, reader, cpo — all ride the same three reset↔writer edits (voided-at-wipe, date-derived stamp, extend #3485) and can plausibly reach A- on a Day 4+ re-run, but see the incoherence note on narrative. designer and a11y are FREE in machinery but not in labour: the designer A requires LIFTING 19 tokens.css rules before TEXT_FLOOR_PAGES can derive from qa_manifest, and measuring 89 pages at 390/1280 is Playwright minutes on public Actions ($0); a11y's composited-contrast check is arithmetic, the `issue` field is a schema edit. NEED RENT (small, with triggers): observability and cto share one item — a fleet-wide ERROR MetricFilter + one digest alarm (~$0.10/mo, demote after 60 clean days once IAM-parity is in premerge); cto's DLQ on telegram-coach-worker is an SQS queue at ≈$0; CTO-1's 'reader-audience red reaches a human within one detection interval' is a ROUTING change (canaries to the urgent topic), FREE, but honest A here also depends on the owner reading the urgent channel in September's no-session posture — that is not engineering. integrations: IAM parity FREE; CommitmentsGraded pair ~$0.10/mo if kept. NEED AN OWNER ACT: (1) reset cadence — the single largest lever, ~40% of findings and 6 of 7 P1s; either resets become monthly or a RESET_IN_PROGRESS flag pauses scheduled writers; (2) the ADR-148 bypass actor is the owner's account, so a client-side hook is the only gate on direct pushes — accept that, or route wrap/reset commits through PRs; (3) re-approve the proof bar as PER-ENTRANT (owner decision #3329 declined the retroactive programme; it did not rule on entrants); (4) the generated/ prefix decision for reader PII (SEC-1); (5) cycle 16's attended prereg publish (unsealed until it runs); (6) actually execute the #3390 Day-1 runlist once; (7) pull at least one PROPORTIONALITY demote trigger per month — the ledger exists, the discipline of using it does not. WHAT 'AN IDENTICAL RE-RUN HITS ALL A' WOULD ACTUALLY REQUIRE, and where it is incoherent: (a) all 17 anchors were extended on the day of this review; a re-run extends them again, so 'identical' is not available — the target must be method-identical, not anchor-identical; (b) narrative's A ('one coherent cycle-6 story, reset seams invisible to a binge reader') cannot be reached while the platform resets weekly — the anchor and the operating cadence contradict each other, and only the owner can pick one; (c) growth's A includes 'commercial option value real and measured' — a product posture, not a code property; it stayed C+ across two runs and will stay there until the owner decides what growth means for a solo N=1 experiment; (d) a 17-lens adversarial panel that returns zero confirmed findings is a panel that stopped looking, not a platform that reached A — the review's yield has been ~5.8/lens across three runs regardless of platform state. The coherent target: a Day 4+ re-run, same method, after the landing path is gated and the reset↔writer seam is closed, produces zero P1s, under ~3 confirmed findings per lens, and no finding whose class cites a previously filed issue. On that run I would expect A/A- for principal, devex, qs, security, cost, integrations, data-architect; B+/A- for cto, observability, aiq, dataviz, designer, a11y, reader, cpo; narrative and growth wherever the owner's two decisions above put them.

redteam.persona: Solo technical founder running a one-person product with AI agents doing most of the coding; grades every proposal on "will this still be true in six weeks when nobody remembers writing it", and treats attention, residue files and CI wall-clock as rent, not only AWS dollars.

class_verdicts.class_name: A1-A / A2-4 / A3-1: The ungated landing path (direct pushes, reset pipeline, wrap commit)
class_verdicts.reason: All three analysts are right about the mechanism (verified: 145 direct pushes since 08-22, hooks = commit-msg + pre-commit only, agent_commit.sh has 0 pytest refs, PR template line 19 says 'Targeted pytest'). All three propose the SAME fix: a pre-push hook running the 155s premerge lane on every push to main. That fails the six-weeks test twice: (1) 145 pushes/14d x 155s is ~26 min/day of agent wall-clock, and an agent at 2am with a broken tree WILL reach for --no-verify (CLAUDE.md forbids it; Session U broke main twice anyway); (2) it re-runs in a hook what the PR fast-lane already runs (verified: pr-checks.yml line 106 runs `-m 'premerge and not integration'` on every PR). The class is not 'no tests on push', it is 'code lands without going through the path that has tests'. #3528 is already filed with the pytest-in-hook shape; amend it rather than file a third copy. The reset pipeline's artifact-reader leg is already landing in PR #3581 (#3529).
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: A pre-push hook that REFUSES, not tests: if upstream is main and the diff touches lambdas/ cdk/ deploy/ scripts/ mcp/ tests/ site/ -> refuse with 'open a PR' (the owner's own global rule 'branch first if on the default branch', made structural); docs-only pushes run the derived docs-ci set (docs_ci_gate_commands(), ~30s) and pass. Cost: seconds per push, $0. The only sanctioned code-to-main direct pusher is restart_pipeline, which gets an explicit env bypass AND the derived artifact-reader test set (#3581). Negative control: commit touching lambdas/x.py, push to main -> refused naming the path; docs-only commit -> pushes in <30s. Dead-man for --no-verify: the wrap (e2) gate counts code-touching non-PR commits on main in the trailing 7d via one gh read and reds above 0 — but see missing class 'no-session posture': that count must ALSO print in the Monday digest, because in September the wrap may not run for a week.
class_verdicts.merge_with: A2-4, A3-1 (one class, one issue: #3528 amended)

class_verdicts.class_name: A1-B / A3-5 / A4-C1 / A4-C2: Point-in-time reset verification while scheduled writers rewrite the surface
class_verdicts.reason: The strongest class in the whole exercise — 6 of 7 P1s, all four analysts independently converge, and A4's frequency arithmetic is the decisive fact (12 resets in 55 days vs PROPORTIONALITY row 86's 'a few times a quarter'). The reset is the platform's most frequent state transition and its only writer-side check (restart_verify check 14) is attended and was never run for cycle 15. Epic #3490 exists. The primitive naming is right: contract on the writer<->wipe seam and a dead-man at the served surface. But the four analysts between them propose ~11 mechanisms for one root; rank them and ship the top four, kill the rest (see over-engineering flags for DERIVED_ARTIFACTS registry, CoOwned registry kind, restart-reverify.yml).
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Ship in this order, all FREE: (1) experiment_stamp(as_of)/tag_record derive phase from as_of >= EXPERIMENT_START_DATE, never from the SSM cycle constant (A4-C3's fix — it makes the pre-genesis window unwritable-as-experiment, which retires most of the sweep's reason to exist); (2) the wipe flips status->voided on every draft it tombstones (one line in build_update) so an age-keyed selector cannot re-select; (3) generalise #2119's writer set-guard from COACH#/ENSEMBLE# put_item to every put/update whose pk classify()==EXPERIMENT_SCOPED, seeded with the current 31 residue seams as a shrink-only baseline; (4) extend the #3485 nightly qa-smoke contract with 'every 200 under /journal/posts/week-NN/ is in posts.json' and 'newest entry >= genesis while day_n>=0' — the nightly run IS the T+24h re-verify, no new workflow. Negative control for (2): tombstoned draft inside the 48h..10d window must NOT be returned by _find_stale_drafts; identical un-tombstoned row MUST be.
class_verdicts.merge_with: A3-5, A4-C1, A4-C2, A4-C3 (C3 is the fix, not a separate class)

class_verdicts.class_name: A4-C3: Write-time provenance from a constant / pre-start is not a phase the registry knows
class_verdicts.reason: Correct diagnosis (experiment_stamp returns the constant phase and SSM's already-bumped cycle; PHASE_FILTER_EXPRESSION admits attribute_not_exists(phase) forever; DA-7's rows written 32 min after the tagger). But it is the ROOT of A4-C1/A1-B, not a sibling — deriving phase from date is the single change that closes CPO-1/NARR-1/NARR-2/R1/QS-1/DA-7 at birth. Keep A4's fix; drop the separate 'PRESTART' registry value unless a reader actually needs to see pre-start rows (none does — hidden is the point).
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Stamp pre-genesis writes as phase=pilot (existing vocabulary, hidden by every existing filter) rather than minting a new PRESTART value that needs its own filter member and doc rows. Add the season-subset-of-frozen contract (every non-voided PREDICTION# with created_date <= genesis has an id in the sealed artifact) as one test in restart_verify + CI. Both FREE.

class_verdicts.class_name: A4-C6: Derived S3 artifacts (pages, share kits, OG cards, catalogs) outside the taxonomy, slug-keyed once-only archive
class_verdicts.reason: The specimens are real and recurring (G-1/NARR-5: html_files_archived=0 / already_archived=29 every reset since cycle 4 — a step whose success condition is exactly its failure). But the proposed fix — a DERIVED_ARTIFACTS registry inside phase_taxonomy with its own coverage assertion — is the C5 failure mode (a registry that needs a hand-typed twin) applied to a sixth surface. Six weeks from now that registry is one more list a session forgets to extend when it adds an OG card.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Three code changes, no registry: archive_one keys on (slug, cycle) and reports acted_count (0 with input>0 = red, the work-contract rule from A4-C2); og_moments purges kits/cards whose canonical_url left posts.json; restart_verify asserts 'every 200 under /journal/posts/ is in posts.json' with a planted stale-page fixture. The nightly qa-smoke HEAD sweep from the B class is the dead-man. challenges_catalog: require evidence_cycle on digit-bearing entries (one test over one JSON file, #3521). All FREE.

class_verdicts.class_name: A4-C5: Reset tools enumerate from hand-typed lists where the registry rules per prefix
class_verdicts.reason: Small, sharp, and its own thing: assert_registry_coverage compares two copies of the same hand list (OPERATIONAL_COACH_IDS vs COACH_PARTITIONS), so COACH#nudge_ledger survived three resets (DA-2) and the wipe's CI twin passes by construction. The fix is the derivation guard applied to the reset tools themselves — the pipeline's step-0 census already enumerates every live pk family, so the required set is one artifact write away. #3514 filed. Six-weeks true: yes, because the census is machine-derived from the table, not typed.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: n/a — the proposal (write pk_family_census.json at step 0; wipe/audit/sweep assert classify()==EXPERIMENT_SCOPED families are covered) is already the cheapest form. Skip the 'git blame date vs last reconcile record' test — a reconcile is a one-off owner-approved DDB write (26 rows), do it once and do not build a detector for a thing that has happened once.

class_verdicts.class_name: A1-C / A2-6 / A3-2: Fail-soft instruments closed on merge, never observed producing their first real output
class_verdicts.reason: The specimens are the most expensive findings in the review (INT-1 49 days, G-3 28 days, OBS-1 never, CPO-2 21 runs of kept=0) and all three analysts see the mechanism. But all three reach for the same fix: closure-contract requirements 7/8 ('**Observed:** <timestamp>', 'first non-degraded output'). That will not survive six weeks: the closure contract is DEFAULT_MODE=warn with a flip bar of 10 consecutive clean wraps that a bug-fix-only September cannot reach, and — A2's own words — the close is 'the instrument agreeing with itself, one level up': the session that wrote the fix writes the timestamp. A self-graded line is exactly the shape that produced #3477's 'realized' six hours before its class recurred. The defect that matters is IAM: a FakeDdbTable cannot deny a put_item. Guard the wire, not the comment.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: (1) Generalise tests/test_freshness_checker_iam_parity.py + test_site_api_write_scope.py into ONE role-family test: for every role in role_policies*.py carrying LeadingKeys/action allowlists, AST-derive the owning module's DDB/S3/SES verbs and pk literals, assert containment. Must be RED today on INT-1's notion pk and G-3's PutItem (that is the positive control). FREE, premerge lane. (2) The 'never produced' ratchet in qa_smoke: a chronic=True check with zero non-chronic results in 30d is a FAIL, not a WARN — FREE, one comparison over the existing log. (3) ONE fleet-wide Logs MetricFilter on level=ERROR across /aws/lambda/life-platform-* routed to the digest (STANDING RENT ~$0.10/mo, one alarm; demote: 60 consecutive days of zero datapoints once (1) is enrolled, at which point the filter stays as a dashboard line and the alarm goes). Not four per-function filters. Keep 'Observed:' as a template line in the closing-comment skill, not as a contract requirement; it is documentation, not a gate.

class_verdicts.class_name: A2-1: Born unproven — a guard enters main with no synthetic must-fail case because the entry bar is an aggregate ceiling
class_verdicts.reason: The diagnosis is the best single sentence in the four reports: 'prove one, mint one' — the #3000 ratchet ceilings the aggregate (541 vs 536-538 live) so a new unproven guard is invisible while the total has headroom. The per-entrant ratchet is right and #3536 is already filed for it. The second half — a structural AST test that every source-scanning tests/test_*.py 'contains a synthetic must-fail case' — is the #2959/#3003/#3199 phrase-matched-suppressor family in new clothes: detecting 'builds a synthetic input and asserts the failure branch' by AST is a heuristic, and an agent will satisfy it with a trivial pytest.raises in six weeks flat, at which point the rule reports 100% coverage and means nothing.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Keep only the per-entrant census ratchet (#3536): any gate id new since the committed baseline must appear in PROVEN_CAN_FAIL with a recorded mutation command, or in a dated exemption — the Proof record names a command a reviewer can re-run, which a pytest.raises decoration does not. Print 'unproven ids new since baseline' in the wrap battery AND in the Monday digest. Drop the AST has-a-must-fail-case detector.
class_verdicts.merge_with: A1-D / A3-6 (the 'instruments that report green without measuring' cluster)

class_verdicts.class_name: A2-2: Self-referential oracle — the guard's comparand is a copy of the claim (mock of subject, copied threshold, hand-typed mirror, pinned prose)
class_verdicts.reason: Real class with 17 members and the sharpest framing ('mutation-provable is not the same as true — the fixture is not the wire'). Two of its three proposals are already covered elsewhere: the mirror-derivation family is landing in PR #3581, and IAM-parity is the fix I keep for the fail-soft class. The novel proposal — a 'mock-of-subject' AST detector (test patches the same symbol it asserts on) — is heuristic, false-positive-prone (patching a collaborator and asserting on the caller is normal), and will need an allowlist that grows. Alarm-threshold reachability (CTO-2, #3500) is a real derivation guard and cheap.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Keep: tests/test_alarm_threshold_reachability.py (every Errors alarm threshold <=1 OR rate-with-floor OR dated registry entry with measured traffic) and the IAM-parity role-family test. Drop the mock-of-subject detector; instead, for the one grader that only ever met a mock (CPO-2, #3553), write the one test that drives the real evaluator to a non-inconclusive verdict. Comparand-must-derive for alarm thresholds = the reachability test; do not add a 'derivation token' schema to every CDK alarm.
class_verdicts.merge_with: A1-C (fail-soft) for IAM; A3-4 (mirrors) for the YAML-derived stand-ins

class_verdicts.class_name: A1-D / A2-3 / A3-3: Guard the instance, not the set — the fix lands on the specimen, the scan set is a hand-picked subset
class_verdicts.reason: 26 members by A1's count, 33 of 99 findings cite the prior issue they re-instantiate (A3), and the memory index itself records '10+ recurrences'. This is the platform's signature defect and the charter's own exemplar sentence. The intake-stage fix (A3: a `## Set` section with an enumeration query and member count in every filed bug; worktree-implementer pastes the member list into the PR body) is the highest-leverage FREE change in the whole exercise because it operates on the fresh-context agent at the one moment it is guaranteed to be reading — the issue body — and a missing heading is unambiguous to lint. Six weeks true: yes; it is a template plus a hygiene lint that already runs at wrap (e7).
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Do the `## Set` section + backlog-hygiene lint (heading present, contains an integer count) + the worktree-implementer step 6b. Do the specific set-derivations that had specimens: AlarmTypes on every describe_alarms via one AST test (OBS-4), DLQ/OnFailure on every Event-invoked target from the synthesized template (CTO-5), TEXT_FLOOR_PAGES and the scroll assertion from qa_manifest (DES-1/2), cast scan over deploy/ + config/ (R2), DAILY_SOURCES under test_source_enumeration_drift (INT-3). Do NOT extend #2844's conformance guard to tests/ scripts/ deploy/ with hand-typed lists as a vocabulary (see over-engineering flag) — that is the residue-explosion path.

class_verdicts.class_name: A1-E / A2-7 / A3-4: Hand copy of a registry fact on a non-Python, reader-bound surface (templates, JSON config, JS strings, email copy, memory prose)
class_verdicts.reason: The specimens are real (G-6 '19 sources' vs 20 vs 22; G-4 one Wednesday email vs three schedules; DEVEX-5 MEMORY.md genesis 09-04 vs 09-05; DV-1 'n=2' beside len(priors)=15). But the proposals are a net-widening programme: extend #2844's vocabularies to genesis dates, counts, cadences, rosters and phase labels, with roots into config/, site/assets/js, email templates, tests/js, MEMORY.md and CLAUDE.md prose, each pre-existing hit into conformance_residue.py. That residue file goes from 36 entries to several hundred on day one, and 'value-keyed' rules over prose ('any ISO date within +-60 days of genesis in a genesis-context sentence') are heuristics with a false-positive farm in 403 memory files full of historical dates. Six weeks later the residue file is the new memory file nobody reads. The class is closed by DERIVING the copy, not by scanning for it.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: (1) Fix the six specimens by making each surface a consumer: the confirmation email reads len(SOURCE_REGISTRY) (and record the curated-vs-registry semantic once, in the registry); /subscribe/ copy derives from email_stack schedule literals; the survival caption reads len(priors); the explain door uses the #1086 shared phase block; the brief inventory renders the paused/lag facet. (2) One served-string rule in the existing nightly qa-smoke: any 'n=<int>' / '<int> sources' literal in a served payload must equal a numeric field in the same payload — FREE, rides an existing Lambda, catches the NEXT hand copy on the night it goes stale. (3) DEVEX-5: SUBTRACT — the /wrap skill stops writing genesis dates into memory prose; the boot brief already prints genesis from constants. Drop the value-keyed rule over MEMORY.md/CLAUDE.md prose and the tests/js vocabulary extension.
class_verdicts.merge_with: A2-7, A3-4 (the mirror-of-CI half is already landing in PR #3581 and is not this class)

class_verdicts.class_name: A1-F / A4-C4: Arithmetic no gate can see — shared chart builders and the stats core with no contract test; ADR-105 has no executable owner
class_verdicts.reason: The one class that genuinely is 'no gate existed' rather than 'a gate looked away'. The fixes are pure tests: a Node-executed charts.js contract (precedent exists in test_cockpit_scope_history_2672.py), an all-censored survival fixture that bounds p30 by the Laplace prior (DV-1/R3, the P1 #3549), a two-strata calibration fixture (QS-3), a claim-shape classifier fixture (QS-4). All FREE, deterministic, and — as A1 rightly says — need no scheduled probe because a pure function does not drift. Six weeks true: yes; a contract test on a pure function is the most durable artifact on the platform.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Scope the 'ADR-105 emission contract' to the four endpoints that had specimens (survival, calibration, receipts, predictions) — a `method` object built by the same function as the number, required in their api_schemas. Do NOT retrofit 'every served statistic object' across ~134 endpoints; that is a schema migration with no specimen behind it. Add the CONVENTIONS §9 row naming the survival test as ADR-105's owner so the next statistical claim has a gate to be asked about.

class_verdicts.class_name: A2-5: A waiver outlives its condition — citations, exemptions, chronic warns and debt baselines are checked for existence and date, never re-derived against the condition
class_verdicts.reason: Small, precise, and its fixes are single comparisons in scripts that already run: check_alarm_citations.py has no StateTransitionedTimestamp comparison (verified: only 'expiry' wording at lines 45/660); a11y ledger serious entries need no `issue` field; chronic=True warns are permanent. CTO-3 (qa-smoke-failures lit for a new cause under a 'CURED and PROVEN LIVE' citation) is the specimen. #3501 and #3546/#3548 filed. Six weeks true: yes — a timestamp comparison does not rot.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Ship the three comparisons (citation.added < StateTransitionedTimestamp -> UNCITED; serious a11y entry without `issue` -> red; chronic warn with no non-chronic result in 30d -> FAIL). Skip the `cause` fingerprint dimension on qa-smoke unless the timestamp rule proves insufficient — the timestamp alone would have caught CTO-3. Skip NewInteriorGapCount (OBS-5) until the #2643 absence marker is applied to every DAILY_SOURCE; that derivation removes the saturation, and a metric to detect a condition you are about to make impossible is rent for nothing.

class_verdicts.class_name: A3-6: Instruments that report green without measuring — guards without a control, acknowledgement layers that age
class_verdicts.reason: A3 bundles two classes that have different fixes and different stages: the guard-without-a-control half is A2-1 / A1-D (per-entrant census ratchet, intake `## Set` section), and the acknowledgement-layer half is A2-5 (waiver staleness). Keeping it as a seventh cluster only adds a name to remember. Its one novel item — 'the census counters become CI ratchets' — is #3536.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: None needed; its members are covered by the two classes it splits into.

class_verdicts.class_name: A3-7: Review cadence as intake — grades carried forward across resets, path-to-A B items never owned, delta selects rows by diff instead of event
class_verdicts.reason: The measured facts are decisive and every other analyst missed them: 8 of 17 lenses were last graded from scratch on 07-28/08-02; the 08-27 delta was held; no review of any breadth ran 08-16 -> 09-05; every prior review ran on Day 1-6, 09-05 was the first ever on Day 0. This is most of the answer to 'why 70' and it is FREE to fix (a 28-day carry-forward cap as a dead-man on the grade; a reset-event term in delta row selection). What A3 under-states: the review is the platform's single most expensive instrument — not in AWS dollars but in session-hours (memory: a 5h window killed 17 graders and 2 lanes at ~70 min), and 'review as intake' makes that a standing cost the PROPORTIONALITY ledger does not carry.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Keep the 28-day cap and the reset-event term (FREE, in operating_calendar.py and full.md). Add a PROPORTIONALITY row for the review ritual itself with its measured session-hours and token cost per full run, and a demote trigger (two consecutive fulls with <10 confirmed findings -> drop to quarterly). Drop the 'B-class path-to-A items become mandatory epic acceptance boxes' — epic checklists are stale by construction (memory) and 84 issues are already the carrier.

class_verdicts.class_name: A1 the_70 point (4) / A2 'why memory does not stop it': lessons exist as recall (memory, skills), not enforcement
class_verdicts.reason: Not filed as a class by anyone but it is the meta-cause under every class above and it is verified: /prove-it and /new-machinery are referenced only by themselves and /incident; /land, /wrap, worktree-implementer.md and issue-filer.md contain none of 'prove-it', 'must-fail', 'positive control', 'what would make'. 85 review-discipline memory entries and a memory index that itself carried a wrong genesis date. A fresh-context agent reads the issue body, the PR template, the skill it was invoked with, and CI's red — nothing else reliably. The fix is to put the three questions where those four things are.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: FREE, four edits: PR template line 19 becomes 'If this PR adds or changes a gate/check/alarm/sweep: the must-fail case is at <file::test>; the SET it enumerates and its registry: <...>'; issue-filer emits `## Set`; /land §5 asks 'what is the first live output and where will it appear'; /wrap prints the census entrant line. No new skill, no new memory file — memory files are the problem, not the fix.

missing_classes.name: Reset frequency as a multiplier, not a defect (the platform's most frequent state transition is sized as a rare one)
missing_classes.evidence: CYCLE_GENESES: 12 resets in 55 days (cycles 5-16, six of them within 10 days in July, then weekly, then a typo re-anchor on 09-04). PROPORTIONALITY row 86 sizes the reset sweep for 'a few times a quarter'. A4 states the arithmetic in its the_70 but no analyst makes it a class with a prevention. Every reset-window class fires PER reset; the survival statistic (DV-1/R3, the P1) is literally the reset frequency counted as day-30 survivors; OBS-6's alarms flap on every reset-day multi-regen; CTO-3 is the #1985 class on its THIRD reset; principal-02 redded main at BOTH resets in the window. Prevention is partly an OWNER act (a date change should not be a full pipeline run — the 09-04 typo cost a second reset; decide whether weekly re-anchors are an experiment design or a habit) and partly FREE: correct row 86 to the measured cadence and let the demote triggers on the reset machinery be judged against 12/quarter, not 3.

missing_classes.name: Detection that only fires when a session runs — dead in the September no-session posture
missing_classes.evidence: CTO-1 (#3499): a Friday /api/board_ask failure is detected Monday (~72h), digested Tuesday, agent-escalated Wednesday, because the only readers of the canary run on slower or inverted clocks. But the same flaw runs through the four analysts' OWN proposals: they place ~10 detections 'FREE, in the wrap battery' (direct-push red count, census entrants, citation staleness, a11y shrink list, unchanged_lenses age). The wrap runs at session close; September is bug-fix-only sessions on demand; the closure contract's flip bar is '10 consecutive clean wraps' — calendar-shaped in a month with few wraps. A detection that fires at wrap in a no-wrap month is the a11y-3 shrink line: printed daily into a job nothing reads. Members also include OBS-3 (the remediation agent repeating a stale needs-human line verbatim, no terminal condition) and DEVEX-1/2 (main-green is only read at wrap). Prevention, FREE: every wrap-battery detection that is a gh/CloudWatch read ALSO prints in the Monday digest / the remediation agent's report (both already scheduled); the ONE standing-rent item worth taking is routing READER_AUDIENCE_ALARMS to the existing immediate-email topic ($0 — the topic and alarms exist; only AlarmActions change). Negative control: a synthetic red on a Friday with no session until Monday must reach the owner's inbox Saturday.

missing_classes.name: Deferred with no carrier — 'revisit', 'fast-follow', 'step 4', 'measure clean first then extend' with no date and no issue
missing_classes.evidence: OBS-5/OBS-7/COST-01/DEVEX-8 thresholds and waivers 'sized on a founding-week snapshot with a revisit clause that has no carrier' (A1 lists them under C but they are not fail-soft instruments); DES-2 armed on 3 of 89 pages with 'measure clean first' and no clock (#2674); a11y-3's 'July step 4' never ticketed; INT-3's fast-follow after #2877 never filed; #3477's unchecked JS-fixture box. The closure contract already has a `residual-homed` requirement — in warn mode. This is the one place a flip to block is cheap and the false-positive cost is nil (a reopened issue). Prevention, FREE: flip `residual-homed` alone to block now, by owner decision, without waiting for a 10-wrap bar that a no-session month cannot reach; the issue-filer refuses a body containing 'later|revisit|fast-follow|step N' without a `#N`. Negative control: the real #3477 closing comment must fail.

missing_classes.name: A new KIND of surface skips the paved road because the checklist is per-kind and nothing asks which kind it is
missing_classes.evidence: SEC-1: two reader-input doors (board_question, findings) added with no DATA_GOVERNANCE row and no prefix decision, landing reader email + ip_hash in the anonymous-readable generated/ prefix — NEW_SIGNAL_PLAYBOOK/ADR-154's 'privacy tier BEFORE the first write' exists for signals, not for doors; SEC-4 (remediation role Resource:* on ses/logs); INT-5 (a Dropbox upload that is a capture channel the registry does not model); CTO-5 (an Event-invoked Lambda outside the ingestion-cohort DLQ contract). The charter's paved roads are 'signal/lambda/page/coach/gate'; a reader-input write path is none of those, so no road was taken. Prevention, FREE: a derivation guard over reader-input write sites (every put_capture_record key vs the bucket policy's anonymous-read prefixes, enrolled beside test_privacy_tier_wiring_2803) and the DLQ contract over the set of Event-invoked targets from the synthesized template. No new playbook — two set-guards.

over_engineering_flags.proposal: Pre-push hook that runs the 155s premerge lane on every push to main (A1-A, A2-4, A3-1, and #3528 as filed)
over_engineering_flags.why: 145 direct pushes in 14 days x 155s = ~26 min/day of agent wall-clock, duplicating a lane the PR path already runs; a hook agents can --no-verify past WILL be bypassed at 2am (Session U broke main twice with the rule already written down).
