framing_critique.what_is_wrong: Three of the owner's four premises are off. (1) 'Why did we have SILENT issues' — most were not silent, they were unread: INT-1 logged an AccessDenied at ERROR on every run for 49 days; CPO-2 logged kept=0 broken=0 for 21 consecutive days; the a11y shrink line printed 7/7/5/11 candidates daily into a job nothing consumes; qa-smoke-failures has been lit since 09-03 under a citation that says cured. The platform emits; it does not read. 'Silent' locates the fault in the instrument when the fault is the absence of a reader on a clock. (2) 'What would have needed to happen to stop them going to production' assumes production is a line crossed once at merge. On this platform production is rewritten by 104 schedules daily and by a reset roughly weekly (12 in 55 days); ~40 of the 99 findings entered AFTER a green deploy — writers running after a snapshot, instruments dying on first live run after a green merge. The gate you are asking for exists (the PR fast-lane runs 8,813 tests); the path most code takes (145 direct pushes in 14 days) skips it, and the stage that actually leaks is operate/reset, which has no re-assertion. (3) 'Do another full review exactly the same and hit all A' is incoherent as stated — see the reality check: the A anchors were extended on 09-05 with Day-0 clauses no prior review had ever exercised, so 'identical' cannot mean 'same bar'; and the reader/narrative/CPO anchors are taste verdicts ('a stranger from Reddit gets it in one screen') that a grader gives, not a state the platform holds. (4) The over-engineering exception is aimed at the wrong ledger: the AWS-dollar exposure of all 26 proposed classes combined is under $2/month. The rent on this platform is attention — residue files, allowlists, exemption ledgers, a 403-file memory directory, closure comments a session must write, hooks that add minutes per push — and PROPORTIONALITY's 'Mind' column already knows it. Scrutinising dollars while waving through a 300-row residue ledger gets the trade exactly backwards.
framing_critique.what_to_add: (a) A fourth question: 'what re-asserts it AFTER it is in production, on what clock, and who reads that in a week with no session?' — that is where 6 of 7 P1s live. (b) The reset frequency as an explicit design variable the owner owns: every reset-window class fires per reset; the machinery is sized for 3/quarter and running at 12/quarter. (c) A rent definition that counts files a future session must read or maintain (allowlists, residue, exemptions, template lines, closure sentences) alongside dollars — with the same 'state the demote trigger' rule. (d) A cadence rule for the review itself: no lens carried forward more than 28 days without a from-scratch grade, and a PROPORTIONALITY row for the review's own session-hour cost. (e) The intake stage: the `## Set` section in every filed bug, because the fresh-context agent reads the issue body and nothing else with certainty.
framing_critique.what_to_drop: Drop '70 — why?' as if the count were the anomaly: per-lens yield has been ~4-6 findings/lens on every review since July (41/7, 27/7, 99/17); what changed was the denominator (17 lenses instead of 7) and the staleness (8 lenses ungraded for 5 weeks). Drop 'stop them going to production' as the goal — replace with 'shorten the time a live defect goes unread'. Drop 'all A on an identical re-run' as a target — replace with a target the platform can actually hold: zero P1/P2 on the next full, every lens at B+ or better, no grade older than 28 days, and a from-scratch run on the same day-of-cycle. Drop the AWS-dollar threshold as the sole scrutiny trigger for over-engineering; keep the scrutiny, widen the ledger.

redteam.path_to_A_reality_check: HONESTLY REACHABLE FOR FREE (tests, derivations, skill/template edits; no AWS objects): principal (needs #3528 in its refuse-not-test form, #3536 per-entrant ratchet, #3581/#3588 landing — all in flight or filed), devex (all FREE; the mirror-derivation class is PR #3581; concurrency-on-sha for docs-ci/v4-gate is a YAML edit), dataviz (charts.js node contract + survival bound + goal-out-of-domain fix — pure tests and one chart routing), qs (date-derived experiment_stamp, season-subset-of-frozen contract, two-strata and claim-shape fixtures; the 'every public claim carries a resolvable citation' clause is content work an agent can do), designer (scroll assertion + text floor from qa_manifest + JS hex sweep — FREE), a11y (#3580 blocked-but-green covers the two P2s; ledger `issue` rule and shrink-list read are FREE; the 'both themes verified by automated contrast check' anchor is a test), security (three set-guards FREE; the reader-input prefix move is a small data migration the owner approves once), data-architect (census artifact + writer set-guard FREE; the 26-row reconcile is a one-off approved DDB write, not rent), narrative and reader (the structural fixes are FREE — but their A anchors are partly taste: 'one coherent cycle-6 story to a binge reader' and 'a stranger from Reddit gets it in one screen' are grader verdicts, so FREE gets you to 'no P1/P2', not to a guaranteed A). NEEDS STANDING RENT (small, each with a demote trigger): observability and cto share one item — reader-facing escalation routed to the existing immediate-email topic ($0 marginal; the topic and alarms exist), plus one fleet-wide ERROR log filter (~$0.10/mo, demote at 60 zero-datapoint days once IAM-parity is enrolled); raising the public-AI canary from 3x/week to daily is a Bedrock call per day (a few cents; demote if 90 days clean); integrations rides the same ERROR filter; cost needs a surge-flip dead-man alarm (~$0.10/mo) or, cheaper, a line in the monthly close (FREE, but then detection is monthly — the owner picks). Total honest rent for every A-path across all 17 lenses: under $1/month AWS. NEEDS AN OWNER ACT (no agent can close these): growth (SES sender identity on a real domain; decide the subscriber cadence you actually promise — one email or three; record the curated-vs-registry source-count semantic), cpo (whether Day 1 reads as a premiere on Home is a product decision; whether the commitments ledger lives or is retired), integrations (INT-5 — is the Dropbox CSV a capture channel), cost (#2883 on 09-06 only if the drift alarm is proven; #3373 kill switch), observability (#3390's attended runlist — either run it once or delete it and let the nightly own it), reader/narrative (cast portraits are ADR-106 owner-only), and the reset frequency itself. WHAT 'AN IDENTICAL RE-RUN HITS ALL A' WOULD ACTUALLY REQUIRE, and where it is incoherent: (1) every lens's A anchor was EXTENDED on 09-05 with Day-0/reset-window clauses no earlier review had ever exercised — so an identical re-run on Day 20 of a cycle cannot exercise them and a re-run on Day 0 of the next reset re-tests the reset; the grade is a function of when you run it, and 'identical' must therefore mean 'same day-of-cycle', which the current calendar does not specify; (2) three anchors (reader, narrative, cpo) are taste judgements a grader gives, not states the platform holds — 'all A' there is a verdict about the grader's mood on the day as much as about the platform, so the coherent target is 'zero P1/P2 and B+ or better' with an A as a bonus; (3) at least six lenses have an owner-act dependency, so 'all A' is not reachable by agent work alone at any budget; (4) the review method's own defect (it sampled 7 pages of 89 when it gave designer its prior A-) means the earlier A- grades were themselves under-measured — some of the 13 drops are the bar being measured properly for the first time, not decay, and a re-run cannot recover a grade that was never earned. The coherent goal, restated: on the next monthly full, run on the same day-of-cycle, no lens carried forward >28 days, zero P1/P2, every lens B+ or better, total new standing rent under $1/mo, and every filed issue carrying a `## Set` — and then grade trajectory across three fulls, not identity with one.
redteam.the_70_answer: One review found 70 because it was the first instrument in five weeks to ask "does it work live, today, after the reset" across all seventeen areas at once — and nothing on the platform asks that on a clock. Per-lens yield did not spike (about five or six findings per lens, the same as July and August); what changed was that seventeen lenses ran instead of seven, eight of them had not been graded from scratch since early August while ~600 commits and twelve resets went by, and the run landed on Day 0 of a reset, ten hours after a scheduled writer had republished a tombstoned post — the one moment every pre-start, phase and tombstone branch is exercised together, which no prior review had ever sampled. Underneath that, the platform's gates are metadata-shaped (a run rollup, an alarm name matched to a citation, a closing comment's headings, a count of gates) while the defects are content-shaped (served bytes, a denied put_item, a pooled base rate, a y-domain), so about ninety percent of the 99 entered where no gate could see them rather than where one was bypassed: half of main lands by direct push with no test between the terminal and main; instruments ship dead behind mocked wires and are closed on the merge; fixes land on the one specimen and the guard scans a hand-picked subset; and the reset — sized in the ledger as a quarterly event, actually weekly — verifies the read side once and never re-asserts after the writers run. The lessons for every one of these were already written down, in 85 memory entries and two skills nothing invokes; they were recall, not enforcement. The fix is not seventy issues, it is roughly six FREE structural changes (a refusing pre-push hook, date-derived provenance plus a void on tombstone, a per-entrant proof ratchet, a `## Set` section at intake, IAM-parity on the real wire, a 28-day cap on carried-forward grades) plus under a dollar a month of rent for one escalation route and one error filter — and an honest decision from you about how often the platform resets.

redteam.persona: Staff SRE who has dismantled more monitoring than built. Working rule: every alarm is a page nobody reads at 3am, every cron is a thing that silently stops, and a 'dead-man per incident' programme ends with a digest nobody opens. I kill standing machinery unless the test-time equivalent is shown to be impossible, and I count attention as rent, not just dollars. Ground truth I checked read-only before writing: 120 alarms / 88 schedules / 104 Lambdas in model/platform_model.json; 4 alarms in ALARM right now (freshness-interior-gap since 08-31 with 9 agent renewals, qa-smoke-failures since 09-03 under a rotted citation, qa-smoke-warnings, token-alarm-genesis-window-active since 09-01); qa_smoke_lambda has 11 check_ functions behind ONE count-aggregated FailCount alarm; closure_contract.py DEFAULT_MODE='warn' with a flip bar never met; .git/hooks holds commit-msg + pre-commit only and agent_commit.sh has zero pytest; 1,056 test files, gate census 597/50 proven; pair_contract_registry 9 register() calls, pair_seam_residue 346 lines, conformance_residue 54 lines; CYCLE_GENESES lists 15 resets; the September posture is 'owner operates, sessions bug-fix-only' (OPERATING_CALENDAR.md:56), which means every 'FREE detection at wrap' the analysts propose runs only when a session happens to run.

class_verdicts.class_name: SDLC-A / Oracle-4 / EM-1 — The ungated landing path (direct push, reset pipeline, wrap commit meet only the format hook)
class_verdicts.merge_with: One class: 'the landing path most commits use has no test leg'. Keep SDLC-A's statement; fold Oracle-4 and EM-1 into it.
class_verdicts.reason: Three analysts independently measured the same thing (302/613 direct pushes, 26/29 red Unit-Test runs were direct pushes, agent_commit.sh has 0 pytest — I re-checked the last two facts). It is real and it is the only class where a gate EXISTED and the path skipped it. But all three propose the same over-built shape: a pre-push hook PLUS a test that 'asserts the hook is installed' PLUS a weekly sentinel/wrap leg counting red direct-push runs. The install-asserting test cannot fail where it runs (a fresh CI checkout has no .git/hooks; it would have to test install_hooks.sh's text, i.e. a phrase match — the #2959 family). The detection leg is a THIRD reader of a signal that already has two: CI emails a failure on every red push (CLAUDE.md format-gate section says so) and the remediation agent already triages failed CI runs Mon/Wed/Fri (CLAUDE.md remediation section). The failure was never detection; it was that nobody acts on the email.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Put the premerge lane INSIDE deploy/agent_commit.sh --push (fail-closed in the script every producer already calls — reset pipeline, wrap, fix commits), so it cannot be 'not installed'. The hook is a belt, optional. Negative control: a broken premerge test + `agent_commit.sh --push` exits non-zero naming the test. Drop the install-asserting test and the weekly count. Keep the one-line docs-ci.yml/v4-gate.yml concurrency-on-sha change (DEVEX-2) — that is a real, free fix. For the reset leg specifically see missing class M3: running the reset from a workflow_dispatch job gets the full suite for free without any hook.

class_verdicts.class_name: SDLC-B — Point-in-time verification of a surface that scheduled writers keep rewriting
class_verdicts.merge_with: DA-C1 (writer↔reset contract) as the primary statement; EM-5, DA-C2, DA-C3, DA-C6 fold in.
class_verdicts.reason: SDLC-B correctly names the time axis but bundles three different missing primitives (writer contract, pre-start registry value, derived-artifact registry) plus acknowledgement-staleness (OBS-2/CTO-3/OBS-3/a11y-3), which belong to Oracle-5. Its detection proposal — a nightly served-surface contract inside qa_smoke — is proposed in near-identical form by EM-5, DA-C1, DA-C2 and DA-C6 (five legs, each '≈$0'). They compound into a 16-check nightly behind ONE FailCount alarm that is lit right now under a citation whose cause is wrong (CTO-3). Adding checks to a saturated, mis-cited alarm is not detection; it is more red that gets renewed.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Prevention as stated (wipe voids drafts; writer set-guard derived from classify(); archive keyed on (slug,cycle)). Detection: ONE census leg in qa_smoke, added only AFTER qa-smoke's failing check ids are surfaced (a log line the citation gate reads via FilterLogEvents at wrap, $0) so the alarm carries cause identity. Rule for the owner: no new qa-smoke check while qa-smoke-failures is red. Demote: two resets with zero census findings once the writer guard's residue baseline is zero (DA-C1's own trigger, keep it).

class_verdicts.class_name: SDLC-C — Instruments that cannot fail, closed on the merge
class_verdicts.reason: Two classes glued together: 'born unable to fail' (Oracle-1/2, EM-6) and 'closed before first live output' (Oracle-6, EM-2). The prevention list is mostly right and FREE (IAM-parity set test — this alone deterministically catches INT-1 and G-3 today; UNEVALUATED judge outcome — already merged #3540; never-fired ratchet). The detection is where I object: 'a Logs MetricFilter on level=ERROR for four operational checkers + two alarms + a CommitmentsGraded/Due metric pair + one alarm' at a claimed $0.20–0.40/mo. Each MetricFilter mints a custom metric ($0.30/mo list price once past the 10-metric free tier this account is far beyond — inference from list pricing, not the bill), so 4 filters + 4 alarms ≈ $1.60/mo, and the attention rent is the real cost: this platform has 120 alarms and 4 standing reds today. A fleet-wide ERROR filter is also the OBS-5 saturation shape — many Lambdas log ERROR benignly (INT-1 itself logged 'non-fatal' at ERROR for 49 days), so it lights and stays lit.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: The remediation agent already holds logs:FilterLogEvents on Resource:* (SEC-4) and already emails Mon/Wed/Fri: add one Logs Insights query (`filter level='ERROR' | stats count() by @log` over 7d, for the operational checker log groups derived from the CDK template) as a report section. Zero metrics, zero alarms, a line in an email that already goes out, and it catches INT-1 within 3 days instead of never. For CPO-2 see over-engineering flag: a grader with 0 output in 21 days is a demote candidate under ADR-144, not an alarm candidate — qa-smoke can Query the grader's own output partition ($0) if the feature is kept.

class_verdicts.class_name: SDLC-D — Guard the instance, not the set
class_verdicts.merge_with: Oracle-3 + EM-3 + DA-C5 — one class, SDLC-D's two structural tests as the fix.
class_verdicts.reason: The best-evidenced class in all four reports (26 members; 'guard the SET' is the charter's own exemplar sentence and the most-repeated memory lesson). SDLC-D's two structural tests over tests/ (positive-control rule; scan-set-derives-from-a-registry rule) are the correct, FREE, deterministic fix with a real negative control. EM-3's additions (a `## Set` heading in every issue, a hygiene lint on it, worktree-implementer step 6b, closure rule 7 `set-named`) are process on top of a warn-mode contract, for a board turning over ~300 issues per fortnight — the heading becomes the next phrase-keyed thing that gets typed to pass the lint.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Ship SDLC-D's two tests; one line in the PR template ('name the SET this guard enumerates and the registry it derives from'). Drop closure rule 7 and the `## Set` lint. The detection ('unproven count as a ratchet') is fine but see Oracle-1: make it per-ENTRANT, not a second aggregate counter.

class_verdicts.class_name: SDLC-E — Hand copy of a registry vocabulary or a literal restating a derived number on a reader-bound surface
class_verdicts.reason: Real class (18 members), but the six-rule 'extend the derivation net to every reader-bound surface structurally' plan — served-string numeric rule, genesis/cycle token rule across MEMORY.md + CLAUDE.md prose, sender-registry contract, disclaimer-condition grep, inventory derivation per facet, fence-aware link resolver — is a regex net being widened one surface at a time. That is exactly how the #2959/#3003/#3199 family was built, and DEVEX-5 is its fifth failure. EM-4's '±60 days of genesis in a genesis-context sentence' rule will flag half the fixtures in tests/. The class recurs because the FACT is restated, not because the net has holes.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Derive at the SOURCE for the five facts that actually bit: (1) source count → one template helper reading len(SOURCE_REGISTRY) with the curated-vs-registry semantic written down once (G-6); (2) phase/day line → build_experiment_phase_context is the only writer (AIQ-6/AIQ-8/CPO-5); (3) subscriber cadence → the /subscribe/ copy and confirmation email render from email_stack's schedule literal (G-4/G-9); (4) 'n=' captions → rendered from the computed value (DV-1, falls under SDLC-F); (5) genesis → MEMORY.md/CLAUDE.md status numbers pasted from `sync_doc_metadata --render-status` (EM-4's wrap rule — keep that one). Keep the mirror-derivation contract for CI stand-ins (deterministic YAML parse). Drop the served-string regex and the ±60-day date rule.

class_verdicts.class_name: SDLC-F — Arithmetic no gate can see (shared chart builders, stats core, ADR-105 as prose)
class_verdicts.reason: Cleanest class in the set: pure functions, deterministic defects, contract tests with negative controls that fail against today's code (goal-in-y-domain, all-censored p30=47%, two unskilled strata pooled 'skilled', point claim typed directional). Detection is correctly 'none new' — the only analyst who resisted adding a scheduled probe for a pure function. Merge DA-C4 into it, minus DA-C4's live regex leg.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: n/a — already the cheapest form. Scope DA-C4's 'method object on every statistic endpoint + schema requirement' to the five endpoints named (survival, calibration, receipts, predictions, body-comp) rather than a ~134-endpoint API shape change.

class_verdicts.class_name: Oracle-1 — Born unproven: a guard enters with no must-fail case because the entry bar is an aggregate ceiling with headroom
class_verdicts.reason: The single highest-leverage FREE change in all four reports, and only this analyst found it: BASELINE_UNPROVEN_GATES=541 vs 538 live means 'prove one, mint one' — a new unproven gate is invisible while the aggregate has headroom, and the review's own principal-05 was downgraded to PLAUSIBLE because that ratchet exists. Flipping test_gate_census_lane_3000 from 'aggregate ≤ 541' to 'no gate id NEW since the committed baseline is unproven' honours owner decision #3329 (no retroactive programme) while closing the entrance. Its negative control is stated correctly (one new unproven id must red even under the ceiling — today that case passes, which is the vacuous control).
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: n/a. Drop the second half's PR-template rewrite only if it duplicates SDLC-D's one line.

class_verdicts.class_name: Oracle-2 — Self-referential oracle: the guard's comparand is a copy of the claim (mocked subject, copied threshold, hand mirror, pinned prose, own stamp as provenance)
class_verdicts.reason: Correct diagnosis (17 members, INT-1/G-3/CPO-2/CTO-2/DEVEX-4/QS-1 are all 'the expected value was a copy'). Of its three guards, (b) IAM-parity-for-every-Lambda is deterministic and catches the two most expensive findings today — KEEP. (a) the 'mock-of-subject AST detector' is a heuristic over 1,056 test files that will seed a residue ledger of hundreds and flag legitimate boundary mocks — it is a new instrument that reports plausibly without measuring, the very class it is meant to close. (c) 'alarm thresholds carry a parseable derivation token re-verified weekly by the sentinel from CloudWatch' creates a threshold LEDGER that rots exactly like docs/alarm_citations.json rotted (CTO-3).
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: (a) → drop; rely on (b) plus Oracle-1's entrant rule. (c) → a static rule over the synthesized template with no registry: an AWS/Lambda Errors alarm on a function is threshold 1 or metric-math rate-with-floor; a higher count needs a dated in-code exemption comment the test reads. No weekly re-verification, no new ledger. CTO-2/CTO-5 close under it.

class_verdicts.class_name: Oracle-3 — Instance-scoped guard, set enumerated by hand
class_verdicts.reason: Same class as SDLC-D with a closure-contract rule 7 bolted on. The conformance-guard root/vocabulary extension into tests/scripts/deploy is the right structural move and is FREE; the closure rule is a warn-mode line (see Oracle-6).
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: SDLC-D's two structural tests + Oracle-3's root extension; drop rule 7.

class_verdicts.class_name: Oracle-4 — Subset-of-the-gate on the landing path (local stand-ins run part of CI, direct push runs none)
class_verdicts.reason: Same class; its one distinct and valuable addition — a test that ENUMERATES every stand-in (any script under scripts/ or deploy/ that names a workflow job or calls `git push`) so a new stand-in is enrolled or red — is the derivation-guard applied to the stand-in set and should survive the merge. Its detection (weekly gh count of red direct-push runs) is the same third reader SDLC-A proposes — drop.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Keep the stand-in enumeration test and ci_gate_commands(workflow); drop the weekly count.

class_verdicts.class_name: Oracle-5 — A waiver outlives its condition (citations, exemptions, chronic warns, debt baselines checked for existence, never re-derived)
class_verdicts.reason: The class that explains why the platform's 120 alarms fail to mean anything: every acknowledgement layer is a ledger entry matched by name and date. The fix is one CONVENTIONS rule plus four small deterministic edits (citation carries cause+added and the gate compares to StateTransitionedTimestamp; chronic warns get a 30-day never-non-chronic ratchet; a11y serious entries require an issue; exemption cadences parsed against the schedule literal). All at wrap/CI, $0, and each has a real negative control. The optional NewInteriorGapCount metric+alarm for OBS-5 is the only rent here — see over-engineering flag; the cheaper fix is to make the alarm's own statistic honest.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: For the CTO-3 cause comparison do NOT add per-check metric dimensions (11 checks × $0.30/mo); have qa-smoke log its failing check ids on one line and let check_alarm_citations read the latest via FilterLogEvents at wrap.

class_verdicts.class_name: Oracle-6 — Closed on merge, not on first real output
class_verdicts.reason: Diagnosis correct (INT-1 49 days, G-3 28 days, OBS-1 30+, CPO-2 21). But the remedy — closure-contract rule 8 `first-output-observed` + a backlog-hygiene `Live:` box lint + a charter amendment + the MetricFilter dead-man — piles onto scripts/closure_contract.py, which is DEFAULT_MODE='warn' and whose flip bar (10 clean wraps / 25 merges) has not been met in the weeks it has existed. A new requirement in a warn-mode contract is a warn line, i.e. one more thing nobody reads. The three analysts who propose it all also propose the standing-rent ERROR alarm as backup, which tells you they don't believe the rule will bite.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: A convention with no detector at all: a PR whose diff touches an instrument, an alarm, or a fail-soft write uses `Refs #N`, never `Fixes #N`; the issue closes by hand when the first live output is pasted. That is a one-line change to the PR template, issue-filer and /land, costs nothing, and removes the mechanism (auto-close on merge) rather than adding a checker of it. Pair with Oracle-2(b) IAM-parity at PR time, which removes the biggest sub-class (denied writes) deterministically. ERROR visibility: the remediation agent Logs Insights query from SDLC-C's alternative.

class_verdicts.class_name: Oracle-7 — Vocabulary copies outside the conformance guard's vocabularies and roots
class_verdicts.reason: Same class as SDLC-E/EM-4. Its distinct contribution, the Decimal derivation guard (every put_item argument flows through floats_to_decimal/tag_record), is a deterministic AST rule with a real negative control and closes DA-1's mechanism — keep it. The proposal to extend vocabularies to genesis/cycle/day literals, counts, cadences, rosters and phase labels across config/, deploy/, site/assets/js/, templates and tests/js is the same net-widening SDLC-E is faulted for: conformance_residue.py (54 lines today) becomes hundreds, and 'once grows then shrinks' is a promise this platform's 346-line pair_seam_residue.py already shows is not kept.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Keep the Decimal guard. Derive the five facts at source (SDLC-E alternative) instead of widening vocabularies.

class_verdicts.class_name: EM-1 — The ungated landing path
class_verdicts.reason: Identical class and identical remedy shape (pre-push hook, install test, wrap-battery gh count). Its sharpest added fact — 'a red main still ships because deploy needs [reconcile, plan] and plan needs only test-critical (ADR-117)' — is the ADR the owner chose; changing it is a bar-raising decision for the owner, not a gate proposal.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: SDLC-A's alternative (lane inside agent_commit.sh --push).

class_verdicts.class_name: EM-2 — Closure on merge, not on live effect
class_verdicts.reason: Same class, same rule-8 + MetricFilter shape, with the honest measurement that 186/229 issues close inside 24h — which is the argument AGAINST a comment-shape rule: the close happens before any live run exists, so a checker of the closing comment can only ever produce warn lines. Also proposes a ledger-stuck check in qa-smoke for DA-1 — already shipped by #3569 (nudge_ledger_qa, PROPORTIONALITY row 88).
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: `Refs` not `Fixes` for instrument PRs; IAM-parity set test.

class_verdicts.class_name: EM-3 — Instance fixed, set never swept
class_verdicts.reason: Same class; the ADR-099 'Effort in the denominator favours instance fixes' observation is the one novel and important mechanism (a 9h instance fix outranks a class sweep by construction) — that is an owner-level scoring decision, not a gate. The `## Set` section + hygiene lint + implementer step 6b are process expansion on a 300-issues/fortnight board.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: SDLC-D's two structural tests; and put the ADR-099 scoring inversion in front of the owner as a decision ('prio:P0 escape hatch' is the current workaround per memory).

class_verdicts.class_name: EM-4 — Hand-typed mirrors of a fact the platform already owns
class_verdicts.reason: Same class. Keep two things from it: the mirror-derivation contract for CI stand-ins (deterministic YAML parse — good) and the wrap rule that status-block numbers are rendered by sync_doc_metadata and pasted, never typed. Drop the '±60 days of genesis' value-keyed date rule (false positives on every dated fixture) in favour of derive-at-source.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: See SDLC-E.

class_verdicts.class_name: EM-5 — Reset-time verification is a snapshot; scheduled writers re-populate what the reset emptied
class_verdicts.reason: Same class as SDLC-B/DA-C1/C2/C3 with a fourth copy of the nightly qa-smoke census AND a fifth mechanism — a `restart-reverify.yml` Actions job re-running restart_verify after the writer window. Two re-verifiers of the same surface is one too many; workflows are instruments that rot (docs-ci.yml's cancel-in-progress is DEVEX-2) and 'public-repo minutes are free' hides the maintenance.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: One nightly census leg (SDLC-B alternative) IS the T+N re-verify; no new workflow. Keep EM-5's 'assert_registry_coverage derives from classify()' — it is DA-C5's fix and is FREE.

class_verdicts.class_name: EM-6 — Instruments that report green without measuring; acknowledgement layers that age without a staleness rule
class_verdicts.reason: Two classes glued: the gate-estate half is Oracle-1, the acknowledgement half is Oracle-5. Its proposal to make THREE census counters (unproven, vacuous-empty, swallowed-exit) shrink-only CI ratchets contradicts owner decision #3329 (aggregate ratchet, no proof programme) and, more importantly, three aggregate counters have the same 'prove one, mint one' hole Oracle-1 found — only the per-entrant rule closes it. Its detection adds NewInteriorGapCount (metric + 1–2 alarms) for OBS-5.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Oracle-1's per-entrant rule; Oracle-5's citation rule. For OBS-5: change the existing alarm's statistic/lookback (Sum over 1 day, or apply the #2643 absence marker to every DAILY_SOURCE derived from the registry so the unfillable member cannot enter the window) — $0, removes the condition instead of instrumenting it.

class_verdicts.class_name: EM-7 — Review cadence as intake: grades carried forward across resets, delta selects rows by diff not by event
class_verdicts.reason: Only one analyst named it and it is the honest answer to the owner's '70' question: 8 of 17 lenses were last graded from scratch on 07-28/08-02, the 08-27 delta was held, every prior review ran on Day 1–6 and this one ran on Day 0, and the anchors were EXTENDED the same day. The fixes are all FREE and touch only the review skill and the operating-calendar probe (28-day carry-forward cap; an EVENT term so a reset selects the reset-touching rows; day-of-cycle recorded in the artifact; B-class path-to-A items filed as epic boxes). No token cost added — it changes which rows a delta selects.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: n/a. One caution: the 'B-class path-to-A items become mandatory epic boxes' rule is what produced 84 issues this time; make it 'filed or explicitly declined with a reason', not mandatory-filed.

class_verdicts.class_name: DA-C1 — Scheduled writers select by status/timestamp and never by the wipe's stamp
class_verdicts.reason: The best-stated version of the reset class: the WRITER side has no contract with the reset (with_phase_filter in 76 files, experiment_stamp in 14; #2119's guard is COACH#/ENSEMBLE# put_item only; 31 writer seams frozen as residue with no countdown; pair registry has 0 writer↔writer entries — I confirmed 9 register() calls). Its prevention is the right shape (taxonomy-derived writer set-guard seeded on the residue as a shrink-only baseline; the wipe voids drafts; CoOwned registry entries) and it is FREE. Its nightly census is the ONE qa-smoke leg I would allow, with a real demote trigger already written.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Sequence: land the census only after the CTO-3 cause fix so it does not join an already-red, mis-cited alarm.

class_verdicts.class_name: DA-C2 — The reset verifies the READ side once and defers the WRITE side to an attended runlist nobody is obliged to run
class_verdicts.reason: Its 'work contract per step' (every restart_* sub-script reports input/acted/skipped and the pipeline reds on input>0 ∧ acted==0 without a named reason) is the single cheapest fix for NARR-5/G-1 — a silent no-op has been reported as success at every reset since cycle 4 — and it is FREE with a fixture that fails today. KEEP that. Its detection ('move check 14 into qa-smoke for the 10 nights after any genesis') is a duplicate of the DA-C1 census leg; and it correctly notes PROPORTIONALITY row 86 prices the reset as 'a few times a quarter' when it ran 12–15 times in 55 days — that is a design decision (see missing class M3), not a check.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Keep the step work-contract and the derived pytest leg; drop the separate 10-night sweep (DA-C1's census covers it); correct row 86 to the measured cadence.

class_verdicts.class_name: DA-C3 — Write-time provenance and rendered tense come from a constant/SSM; the pre-start window is not a phase the registry knows
class_verdicts.reason: The one class whose missing primitive is the REGISTRY itself (no pre-start value exists, so nothing could derive from it) — different fix location from C1, so keeping it separate is justified. experiment_stamp(as_of) deriving phase from date-vs-genesis removes the countdown-window residue at source, which is better than any sweep; the season⊆frozen contract is deterministic and FREE. Detection correctly rides existing runs ($0).

class_verdicts.class_name: DA-C4 — Served statistics whose caption/method/label is a second hand-typed writer beside the computation
class_verdicts.reason: Same class as SDLC-F (pure-function contracts). Its 'method object built by the same function as the number' is the right derivation move, scoped to the named endpoints. Its detection — a nightly regex over live payloads for 'n=<int>' — is rent for a deterministic fact: once the caption derives from the computation the live check can only ever pass, and it adds another check to the saturated qa-smoke alarm.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Contract tests only; no live regex.

class_verdicts.class_name: DA-C5 — The reset tools enumerate from hand-typed lists where the registry rules per row/prefix
class_verdicts.merge_with: SDLC-D (guard the set) — with its census-artifact fix kept
class_verdicts.reason: The 'assert_registry_coverage compares two copies of the same hand list' finding is the sharpest specimen of SDLC-D in the estate, and 'write the step-0 pk-family census to deploy/generated/pk_family_census.json and derive every coverage assertion from it' is the right FREE fix. class_verdicts.class_name: DA-C6 — Derived artifacts (S3 pages, share kits, OG cards, catalogs, proof stamps) sit outside the taxonomy
class_verdicts.reason: Correct that ADR-077 is a DDB registry and S3 derivatives have no class, no cycle in their key, and a slug-idempotent archive that has archived nothing since 2026-07-10 (html_files_archived=0). The DERIVED_ARTIFACTS registry entry is the right primitive. But 'every 200 under /journal/posts/week-NN/ ∈ posts.json via HEAD over the slug registry' nightly is the same served-surface leg as DA-C1/SDLC-B/EM-5 — fold it in as ONE more assertion, not a fourth leg — and keep the registry to the four prefixes that actually bit (journal posts, share kits, moments index, chronicle PNGs) rather than a general S3 taxonomy.

missing_classes.name: M1 — A signal with no scheduled reader: detection exists, the reader runs on a slower or inverted clock, or does not run at all in the no-session posture
missing_classes.evidence: Not named as a class by any analyst, yet it is why the findings were 'silent'. CI already emails every red push and the agent already triages failed CI — the SDLC/Oracle/EM analysts each add a THIRD reader of that signal. Missing primitive: a RATCHET on the alarm/digest estate (120 alarms, 88 schedules — shrink-only; any proposal that adds a line names the line it deletes) and a dead-man on the READER (the digest section that lists standing reds older than 72h and refuses to be renewed a 10th time). Coach-nudge persisted nothing for 25 days (#3569, fixed). PROPORTIONALITY.md carries a demote trigger on ~every row but there is no ledger of triggers EVALUATED — the trigger is prose with no executor. Missing primitive: the ratchet's demote half with an executor — one line in the existing monthly close (scripts/monthly_close.py, #3375) listing instruments with zero non-degraded output in 30 days as DEMOTE candidates, routed to the owner as a decision, not as an alarm. missing_classes.name: M3 — The reset is a routine, owner-triggered, locally-run operation with an exceptional-event verification budget
missing_classes.evidence: 15 entries in CYCLE_GENESES; 12 resets in 55 days (DA analyst, confirmed by the literal list); PROPORTIONALITY row 86 prices the sweep at 'a few times a quarter'. The reset is a DIRECT PUSH from a laptop (restart_pipeline.py:1184 'commit the regenerated files … from MAIN'), its sweep runs against the working tree so history-keyed gates cannot see it (DEVEX-6), it redded main at both resets in the window (principal-02), tripped a Sum/day alarm on the re-anchor (OBS-6), skipped the frozen-artifact sweep on override (CTO-3), and has archived nothing since cycle 4 (NARR-5/G-1). 6 of 7 P1s live in its writer window. The analysts fix the reset's checks; none names the two design choices: (a) OWNER ACT — fewer resets (the Friday→Saturday re-anchor was a typo; a 1-day cycle is a data-quality event in itself, see DV-1/R3 where 1–7-day cycles inflate a survival statistic); (b) run the reset as a workflow_dispatch job on the existing OIDC deploy role — it then gets the FULL suite, a history-visible commit, and a scheduled T+N re-run for free, which closes SDLC-A's reset leg, DEVEX-6 and the T+writers re-verify at once without any hook or new Lambda. Zero metrics, zero alarms, one section in an email that already goes out. Catches INT-1 in ≤3 days.

framing_critique.what_is_wrong: Three assumptions in the three questions. (1) 'Why did we have silent issues' assumes silence is an anomaly. On this platform silence is the DEFAULT OUTPUT of the estate: 597 gates of which 50 are proven able to fail, 120 alarms of which four are lit right now for 5–37 days (one renewed nine times), a closure contract armed 'warn' with a flip bar never met, and a delta review that carried 8 of 17 lenses forward for five weeks. The issues were not silent — the qa-smoke alarm has been red since 09-03, CI emailed every red push, the a11y shrink line printed daily. The READERS were absent, or ran on the wrong clock (CTO-1: detector Friday, reader Wednesday), or read a rollup instead of the jobs (DEVEX-1). (2) 'What would have stopped them going to production' assumes a merge gate is the choke point. By the SDLC analyst's own count only ~10 of 99 passed a gate that existed; ~58 entered at design/implement where no gate could see them (a hand copy, a hand list, an untested builder), and 18 entered AFTER production via scheduled writers a reset never contracted with. The choke points are the stamp function, the shared builder, the archive step and the landing path — not 'production'. (3) 'Hit all A grades on an identical re-run' is incoherent for at least four lenses, and the owner's own over-engineering clause is what the analysts violated: 20+ new tests is fine, but they also proposed 6+ new alarms, 6 nightly legs and 3 new ledgers against an estate whose problem is that nothing already emitted gets read.
framing_critique.what_to_add: (a) A fourth question: WHICH INSTRUMENTS DO WE DELETE — the alarm/schedule estate needs a shrink-only ratchet (120 alarms, 88 schedules) and every proposal that adds a line names the line it retires; 'proactive' must include WHO reads it and WHEN, in a posture where sessions are bug-fix-only. (b) The reset-frequency decision as an explicit owner choice: 12–15 resets in 55 days is the single most frequent state transition and the parent of 6 of 7 P1s and of the inflated survival statistic; either resets become rare (owner behaviour) or the reset becomes a CI-run operation with the full suite by construction. (c) A demote pass, not an alarm pass, for instruments with zero output since birth (CPO-2, OBS-1, G-8, G-3): ADR-144's demote triggers exist on paper with no executor. (d) Replace 'all A' with a target that can be measured identically twice: zero confirmed P1/P2 in the reset↔writer class on a Day-0 run, zero alarms lit >72h without a cause-matched citation, and no lens carried forward >28 days. (e) Sequencing: the cause-identity fix on qa-smoke (CTO-3) BEFORE any new nightly check; the per-entrant proof rule (Oracle-1) BEFORE any new guard; `Refs` not `Fixes` BEFORE any closure-contract rule.
framing_critique.what_to_drop: Drop 'all A on an identical re-run' as a goal: the rubric extends every lens's anchor on the day it runs (all 17 carry extension notes this time), the adversarial verifier's yield has been ~5.8 findings per lens at every breadth (41/7, 27/7, 99/17), and 13 anchors say 'on ANY day of a cycle' — an identical Day-0 run is the hardest case by construction. Drop 'why were they silent' as an anomaly question — reframe as 'why does nobody read what is already red'. Drop the implicit equation 'a class is closed when it has a dead-man' — three analysts reached for a MetricFilter-and-alarm on a platform whose review just found that alarms sit lit under rotted citations; a dead-man with no reader is the OBS-5 class wearing a new name. Drop 'a review that files 70 issues is a review that worked' — 84 filed / 28 closed in a week is the cadence that produces instance fixes (ADR-099's Effort denominator) and the next 70.

redteam.the_70_answer: One review found 70 because it was the first instrument in five weeks that measured the platform the way it actually fails: it asked 'what would make this red' against LIVE state, across all 17 lenses at once, on Day 0 of a reset, ten hours before the scheduled writers ran. Nothing you own does that. Your gates measure diffs (and half your commits skip them — 302 of 613 were direct pushes meeting only a format hook); your closures measure the closing comment's shape, in warn mode, nine hours after filing; your reset verifies the read side once at T0 while 104 schedules write afterwards with no contract; your alarms are matched to citations by name so four can sit lit for 5–37 days and read as explained; your delta reviews carried 8 of 17 grades forward for five weeks because a reset touches no file path; and 538 of 597 gates have never been shown able to fail, with an aggregate ceiling that lets each new proof admit a new unproven one. The per-lens yield was the same as every prior review (~5.8) — what changed was breadth (17 lenses, not 7) and the sampled instant (Day 0, never before observed). So the 70 are not a regression; they are the standing residue the estate cannot see, made visible once. The fix is not seventy fixes and not thirty new detectors: it is five entrances — the landing path runs the lane, a guard proves it can fail before it lands, writers derive phase from the date and the wipe voids what it tombstones, captions and counts derive from the computation, citations and waivers carry a cause and a date — plus two things only you can decide: reset less, and delete instruments nobody reads before adding any that cost money.
redteam.path_to_A_reality_check: FREE and honestly reachable to A with code only (tests, ratchets, derivations, script edits): PRINCIPAL (lane in agent_commit --push, dead-def guard on common/ai, ratchet counts logical lines, comment numbers derived), DESIGNER (text floor over qa_manifest after the 19 tokens.css rules lift, scrollY assertion, hex sweep over JS), DATAVIZ (charts.js node contract tests; DV-1's derived n), A11Y (ledger entries require an issue, shrink consumer at wrap, contrast already landed #3544/5), DEVEX (mirror-derivation from YAML, concurrency-on-sha, status block pasted from sync), COST (receipts scope/triple-count/disclaimer-condition, surge-flip line in monthly close), READER (class-2 fixes + honest-absence copy), AIQ (temporal rule registered, #3050 full ordering, UNEVALUATED already merged) — all reachable by an identical re-run IF the anchors are pinned; each carries the caveat that its A anchor was extended on 09-05 and can be extended again. FREE plus ONE OWNER ACT: SECURITY (SEC-4 role scoping is a hand-applied IAM change — ask-first mutation; the rest is set-guards), INTEGRATIONS (INT-1's grant or pk move is a CDK deploy; the rest derives from the registry), DATA-ARCHITECT (the 26-row reconcile is an owner-approved DDB write; census-derived coverage and idempotency test are free), CTO (the A anchor's 'a reader-audience red reaches a human within one detection interval independent of any session' needs a routing change onto the existing ADR-143 SMS topic — $0 in AWS but the owner must agree to be paged — and 'no alarm lit unexplained >72h' needs the owner to clear the four standing reds and rule on freshness-interior-gap). OBSERVABILITY is the trap: its A anchor is 'every alarm state honest, nothing permanently red, every producer verified emitting' — reachable FREE (IAM parity, producer census, citation cause rule) but ONLY if the owner clears the standing reds and the analysts' new alarms are NOT added; every MetricFilter proposal moves this lens away from A. RENT-OR-NEVER: NARRATIVE (the mechanics — wipe voids drafts, writer guard, cycle-keyed archive — are free and get to B+; the A anchor's 'each coach distinguishable blind with scoreboard evidence' needs the voice-fidelity scoreboard, an AI-call surface already inside the $215 ceiling, and needs cycles long enough to accumulate evidence). STRUCTURALLY INCOHERENT ON AN IDENTICAL DAY-0 RE-RUN: QS ('every pre-registered bet graded or explicitly voided ON THE RECORD across resets' — a Day-0 run has zero gradeable bets by construction, cycle 16's prereg is unpublished until the attended publish, and 1–7-day cycles cannot grade a 30-day bet; A requires the OWNER to stop re-anchoring), CPO ('every engagement hook demonstrably alive on ANY day including Day 4 of a fresh reset' — the commitment loop has 0 graded of 480; either it ships for real or is demoted, and predict-the-week needs readers to predict), GROWTH (C+ → C+, 'subscriber conversion visible' and 'fixed cadence matching promise copy' need a product decision on cadence and real subscribers to measure; two dead pendings from 07-03 are the entire funnel — grading growth at A on a site with no traffic is measuring a thing that does not exist yet). What 'an identical re-run hits all A' would actually require: (1) pin the 17 anchor texts so 'identical' is even defined — the rubric extends anchors every run, so the target moves by construction; (2) choose the day-of-cycle — 13 anchors say 'ANY day', and Day 0 is the hardest, so the run must be Day 0 to be identical and Day ≥ 30 for QS/CPO/NARRATIVE to have evidence, which is a contradiction unless cycles last that long; (3) zero open owner-act items (SEC-4, INT-1 grant, the four standing reds, the prereg publish, the subscribe cadence decision, the reset-frequency decision) — at least six today; (4) an adversarial verifier that has yielded ~5.8 confirmed findings per lens at every breadth must yield zero P1/P2 — realistic only if the reset↔writer class is closed at the stamp function and the reset stops being weekly. The coherent target is 'no P1/P2, no lens below B+, no lens carried forward >28 days, no alarm lit >72h without a cause-matched citation' — measurable twice, and reachable for FREE plus the owner acts named; 'all A' is not a property of the platform, it is a property of the rubric on the day it runs.

redteam.persona: Review-methodology critic and the owner's devil's advocate. My brief was to attack the prompt, not the platform: is "three parts + path to A" the right shape, is "all A on an identical re-run" a coherent target, and what is the owner actually asking. Method: read the 99 findings, the 17 process verdicts, the 84 path-to-A actions and the grade table; re-read the rubric (SKILL.md, full.md), the PR template, closure_contract.py, the gate-census ratchet, PROPORTIONALITY row 86, CYCLE_GENESES and the 09-05 artifact's own method line. Read-only; no scripts run (the Bash classifier was rate-limited this session), so every count I did not re-derive is cited to its source. Bias I am correcting for: four analysts converged on the same six classes and then proposed ~35 new instruments — the critic's job is to ask what those instruments cost in the only currency this platform is actually short of, which is instrument count and attention, not dollars.

The landing-path question is ultimately an ADR-148 owner decision.

(2) Put the premerge lane inside deploy/agent_commit.sh's push mode — sessions already invoke it unpiped (memory rule), and a script is harder to skip than a hook. The Node contract test for charts.js is the cheapest item in the entire input — one file, five fixtures, five findings. class_verdicts.class_name: DA-C4 — Served statistics whose caption/method/label is a second hand-typed writer beside the computation

Its point that DV-1 is 'the reset frequency leaking into a statistic' (seven 1-7-day re-anchored cycles counted as day-30 survivors) belongs in missing class M1. class_verdicts.class_name: DA-C5 — The reset tools enumerate from hand-typed lists where the registry rules per row/prefix

Keep its 'live census as the required set' via deploy/generated/pk_family_census.json — with one warning the #3477 class taught: a regenerated artifact needs the tests that read it inside the regeneration's own gate, or every reset reds main on it (principal-02, both resets in the window).

missing_classes.name: M1 — Operating cadence exceeds the machinery's design cadence: the reset itself is the writer of the P1 class
missing_classes.evidence: CYCLE_GENESES 5→16 (site_api_data.py:108-124) is 12 geneses in 55 days; cycles 13/14/15 lasted 15/15/3 days (CPO-2 corrected cause); PROPORTIONALITY row 86 prices the reset sweep for 'a few times a quarter'. 39/99 findings are reset/phase/genesis defects and 6/7 P1s are the reset→first-cron window (EM the_70 fact 3). Two findings are literally the cadence leaking into product: DV-1/R3 (47% odds manufactured by seven 1-7-day re-anchored cycles counted as day-30 survivors) and CPO-2(b) (no commitment has ever reached its due date because resets tombstone them first — 480 records, 0 graded). Every future-genesis reset re-mints DA-C3's countdown-window class; every reset within 10 days of a Wednesday draft re-mints CPO-1. No analyst names the cadence as a cause; the data-architect calls it 'arithmetic' and then proposes machinery for a weekly event. Stage: reset. Cost: FREE — an owner rule plus restart_pipeline refusing a second --apply within N days of the last genesis unless --reanchor-of names it (the DA path-to-A #2 flag, generalised). Negative control: a dry --apply 3 days after a genesis without --reanchor-of exits non-zero naming the prior genesis; with the flag it proceeds. Demote: n/a. The primitive missing is the RATCHET on the operation's frequency, not on its code.

missing_classes.name: M2 — The author is the only oracle: the same session writes the guard, its expected value, the Outcome sentence, the closure verdict — and, at review time, the anchor extension it is graded against
missing_classes.evidence: TO's the_70 names it in passing ('the instrument agreeing with itself, one level up') and no class owns it. Specimens: #3477 closed 'Outcome: realized' by its author at 06:17Z and its class recurred by afternoon (principal-02); #1956 closed 'partial' by its author with the instrument never having produced a value (OBS-1); DEVEX-6's read-only contract asserted by the sweep's own author as the absence of '--apply'; COST-03's test pins the author's false sentence; QS-1's countdown-sweep test pinned the sanctioning rule that blinded the sweep; CPO-2's only test mocks the grader. And at the top: all 17 A anchors were extended in-run by the graders who then graded against them (every extension_note in the 09-05 artifact; SKILL.md:84-87 permits it). p50 open→merge 61 min, no code-review workflow (TO evidence). This is not 'hire a reviewer' — it is TIME separation, not person separation: closure verified by a later session or a scheduled instrument, never by the closing one. Stage: closure. Cost: FREE — wrap (e8) already runs detector A over 'THIS session's closures'; change the window to 'every close since the previous wrap, by any session' so the next session grades the last one's Outcome sentences against live state; and anchor extensions land as a rubric PR BEFORE a run, never inside it. Negative control: a close two sessions old whose `Observed:` line is absent → flagged at this wrap; an anchor whose text differs from the versioned rubric file → the grades JSON fails its shape test.

missing_classes.name: M3 — A decision or revisit deferred in prose with no carrier (the operating calendar's dead-man never applied to ADR consequences, citations, exemptions, 'fast-follow' and 'owner decides' clauses)
missing_classes.evidence: G-9 corrected cause: 'no ADR records the decision to send reader mail from a personal domain'; G-4(b): the Friday delivery is 'an approval-latency artifact' — a standing owner decision nobody scheduled; INT-5: 'the fix is an owner decision on the #746 channel set'; COST-01: 'ADR-133's own consequences clause already owes this revisit'; OBS-5: 'the citation's OWNER DECISION has no carrier'; OBS-7/DEVEX-8: 'revisit' clauses with no clock; G-6: 'curated vs registry has no recorded semantic'; a11y-3: 'the July path-to-A step 4 never landed'; DES-2: armed on 3 pages 'with no clock to extend it'; INT-3: '#2877's fast-follow was never ticketed'. Eleven findings share one mechanism: an obligation written where no probe reads it. The platform owns the exact primitive (scripts/operating_calendar.py's dated obligations + check_residual_queue's `not-work — <home>` grammar) and applied it to handovers and calendar entries only. Stage: design/closure. Cost: FREE — a doc-facts rule that an obligation marker (a small OWNED vocabulary: revisit / owner decides / fast-follow / step N / TODO-by, the check_residual_queue precedent, structural not phrase-matched because the vocabulary is the registry) must carry `#N` or a date within 90 days, in ADRs, citations, exemptions and PROPORTIONALITY rows. Negative control: plant 'revisit when traffic grows' in an ADR with no carrier → red; with '#1234' → green.

missing_classes.name: M4 — The review instrument has no negative control of its own (the class the review found 37 times, unapplied to the review)
missing_classes.evidence: 09-05 artifact method line: '99 CONFIRMED, 5 PLAUSIBLE, 12 REFUTED — a 10% first-pass refutation rate against the historical ~50%'. Nothing distinguishes 'verification got better' from 'verifiers got compliant' — no planted false finding was fed to any verifier batch, no planted true defect measured grader recall. The designer's prior A- was measured on '7 pages rendered' of 89 (SDLC the_70); the delta selected rows by diff so a reset never selected the narrative row; every grader extended its own A anchor in the run it graded (SKILL.md:84-87 sanctions this), so 13 of 17 drops are partly a bar moving, unseparable from decay ('cannot be separated from the artifact' — EM evidence_quality (d)). full.md:145-147 makes finding something a success condition ('at least one same-class defect the human missed was found and confirmed') — the review is structurally required to find, so a 17-A run fails its own bar. Yield has been ~5.8 findings/lens across three runs regardless of platform state — the number is a property of the instrument. Stage: intake (the review IS the intake for most of the backlog: 84 of 297 issues since 08-22). Cost: FREE in dollars (tokens already spent; ~7.2M subagent tokens per full run is the unstated rent). Fix: (a) 2-3 planted false findings per verifier batch (a true claim written as a defect) — the verifier's refutation of them is its positive control; (b) 2-3 known open issues withheld from the do-not-refile list — grader recall; (c) anchors versioned in a rubric file, frozen for a run, extended only by PR between runs; (d) record day-of-cycle in method (done 09-05 — keep it). Negative control: a run whose verifiers confirm a planted false finding is marked UNCALIBRATED in its own artifact and does not reset the calendar clock.
member_findings: (process, not findings) every extension_note in fullreview_grades_2026-09-05.json

Negative control: two different failing check ids on consecutive nights under one citation → the citation gate names the new cause.
