framing_critique.what_is_wrong: Four things. (1) 'Why did we have SILENT issues' presumes silence is the anomaly. On this workflow silence is the default output: a direct push meets no test (PR template :19 asks for targeted pytest; agent_commit.sh runs none), a merge closes the issue before deploy, closure_contract is warn-mode with a flip bar never met, a fail-soft write logs 'non-fatal', a citation is matched by name, a gate is counted whether or not it can fail (597 gates / 50 proven), and a delta review carries a grade forward for five weeks. Nothing in the loop asks 'does it work live, today, after the reset' — the review was the first instrument in 20 days that did, so it found 70. That is the answer, and it is a workflow fact, not a defect list. (2) 'What would have needed to happen to stop them going to production' presumes entry at implement/merge. By the SDLC lens's own stage forensics only ~10% were a gate bypassed; ~18-23 entered at OPERATE/RESET after a green point-in-time verify (the P1 cluster) and ~13 at CLOSURE — there is no 'production gate' for a defect that is born in production by a scheduled writer or that was closed non-functional. The right question is 'what bounds how long a live defect stays silent' — a time-to-detection number — not 'which gate at merge'. (3) 'Do another full review exactly the same and hit all A' is incoherent as stated, on four independent grounds: (a) the rubric REQUIRES anchors to be extended in-run (SKILL.md:84-87), and all 17 were on 09-05 — the bar moves with every run, so 13 drops are partly a raised bar and no one can say how much (EM evidence_quality (d)); (b) full.md:145-147 makes the review succeed ONLY if it finds and confirms a same-class defect the human missed — a 17-A, zero-finding run FAILS its own contract; the instrument is built to find, and its yield has been ~5.8 findings/lens across three runs regardless of platform state; (c) an 'identical' re-run is not reproducible on a live experiment — Day 0 of a reset was the surface that produced 6 of 7 P1s, and a Day-6 re-run cannot observe it; (d) the graders and the builders are the same agent estate reading the same rubric — 'teach to the test' is one prompt away, and there is no negative control (planted defect, planted false finding) to tell an honest 17-A from a blunted instrument (refutation fell 50%→10% with no calibration). Set 'all A' as the target and you will get it, and it will mean nothing. (4) 'Over-engineering = materially increases running cost' uses the wrong unit. The four analysts propose ~35 instruments and call ~30 of them FREE. This platform is not short of dollars ($215 ceiling, tier 0); it is short of ATTENTION: 597 gates, 538 unproven, 403 memory files, a 285-row residue ledger, 84 open review issues, a 5-hour session window. Every 'FREE' gate, ledger and residue entry is rent in the currency that actually binds, and the review just demonstrated that instruments added faster than they are proven become next month's findings (37 of 99 findings were defects IN an instrument).
framing_critique.what_to_add: (1) The owner's number: TIME-TO-DETECTION. For each of the 99, a birth date (the introducing commit or the reset that minted it — the review text already carries 'for 49 days', 'since #151', 'since 2026-06-24') and a detection date; report median and p90 silent window per class. That is what 'why silent' measures, and it is the metric the workflow changes should move (the P1 cluster's window was ~10h; INT-1's was 49 days). (2) A negative control for the review itself (M4): planted false findings per verifier batch, withheld known issues for grader recall, anchors frozen in a versioned rubric file and extended only by PR between runs. (3) An instrument budget with a per-entrant ratchet: a gate enters the census only proven (gate_census_mutations.py), and a registry of residue ledgers with expiry + consumer per entry — the 'one in, one out' the CHARTER's ratchet primitive implies but never applied to the gate estate. (4) The reset cadence as a first-class owner decision (M1): 12 resets in 55 days is the largest single cause in the input and no analyst put it to the owner. (5) A ranking rule for the ~35 proposals: findings-closed per instrument added, with the P1 cluster's three one-function fixes (wipe voids drafts; stamp derives from date; archive keyed on cycle) at the top and any proposal that adds a heuristic detector or a residue ledger at the bottom. (6) Time-separated closure (M2): the next wrap grades the last session's Outcome sentences; the closing session never grades its own.
framing_critique.what_to_drop: (1) 'All A on an identical re-run' as the goal. Replace with two observable bars: zero P1 on BOTH Day 0 and Day 6 of the next two cycles (the two surfaces the reviews have now sampled), and median silent-window for a confirmed defect under 7 days with the p90 under 30 — numbers a nightly instrument can report and a review can only sample. (2) The 84 per-lens path-to-A stories as the unit of work — they are the symptoms the owner said he did not want; ~20 of them are closed by six class fixes and the rest should be re-parented under the classes, not paid down one lane at a time (Session V measured the paydown: 'most review findings genuinely need code', batches are pairs, the census chain is a 2-hour tail). (3) The forced 'prevention AND detection per class' shape. For arithmetic (K6) there is no detection — a contract test IS the detector; for operate/reset classes there is no prevention at merge — a dead-man IS the fix. Forcing both produced the rent proposals (MetricFilters, nightly legs, NewInteriorGapCount). Let each class name its ONE missing primitive, which is what the CHARTER asks. (4) The dollar-only over-engineering test — replace with 'instruments added vs instruments proven' as the cost, with dollars as a secondary column. (5) The in-run anchor extension clause as currently worded — extension stays sanctioned, but as a rubric PR before a run, never inside the run that grades against it.

redteam.the_70_answer: One review found seventy things because it was the first instrument in weeks that asked the only question that matters — does this work live, today, after a reset — and asked it everywhere at once, on the worst possible day. Nothing in your workflow asks that question: a direct push meets no test (half of main lands that way, and the PR template literally asks for 'targeted pytest'), a merge closes the issue before anything runs in production (the closure contract is in warn mode and has never been armed), a fail-soft write logs 'non-fatal' and no alarm can see it, a citation is matched by its name not its cause, a gate counts as a gate whether or not it can fail (50 proven of 597), and the weekly delta carried ten lenses' grades forward for five weeks because it only re-graded what the diff touched — while the defects here come from scheduled writers, resets and the calendar, not from diffs. Roughly a third of the findings are defects IN your instruments, and the honest reading is that you have been adding instruments faster than you prove them. Two of the seventy are not workflow at all but you: you reset the experiment twelve times in fifty-five days on machinery priced for 'a few times a quarter', and six of the seven P1s are the ten-hour window between a reset and its first cron. And the thirteen dropped grades overstate the decay — every grader raised its own bar in the same run, so some of the drop is the bar. The fix is not seventy stories or thirty-five new gates; it is five workflow changes (test the landing path, close on first live output not on merge, guard sets not instances, derive reader-bound copy, contract-test the arithmetic), one owner decision (how often you reset), and one number to watch instead of a letter grade: how long a live defect stays silent.
redteam.path_to_A_reality_check: FREE and honestly reachable with the anchors AS EXTENDED: dataviz (five contract fixtures + the survival/calibration function changes — pure computation, no wire beyond the four named endpoints); qs (pure function changes in calibration_core/stats_core/build_predictions, EXCEPT clause (2) 'served season ledger mirrors the sealed artifact' which needs the attended cycle-16 prereg publish — an owner act still owed per the Session V memory); devex (mostly landed: #3529/31/34 mirror derivations, #3530 rollup reader; DEVEX-5 value rule and DEVEX-7 are S); a11y (CSS token lifts + composite pairs + the `issue` field + a 2-3 minute deterministic light-context axe pass per deploy — free CI minutes, no Bedrock); designer (CSS + gates, but 'MEASURED on all 89 pages' means lifting 19 tokens.css rules and measuring the registry clean first — M effort, and DES-1's fix is one JS condition); data-architect (all tests and derivations FREE; the DA-9 reconcile of 26 rows is an AWS write the owner authorises once); integrations (IAM-parity role family FREE; INT-5 is an owner decision on the #746 channel set); cost (COST-01..04 are code/test changes; #2883 is a dated owner check-in); aiq (deterministic rules in the existing freshness class + derivations from registry facets). NEED RENT, small and with stated demotes: cto (daily canary cadence ≈ $0.09/mo Bedrock, a DLQ or OnFailure destination on telegram-coach-worker ≈ $0 SQS, routing READER_AUDIENCE_ALARMS to the urgent topic $0); observability (choose the $0 expected-absence marker over NewInteriorGapCount; the ERROR-line dead-man should be the qa-smoke Logs Insights query, not filters+alarms). NEED AN OWNER ACT before A is even observable: principal (its EXTENDED A requires 'every landing path meets the pre-merge lane' — that is ADR-148's bypass-actor decision and the #2198 personal-repo constraint, not code); security (SEC-1 prefix move needs a role grant + DATA_GOVERNANCE row, SEC-4 is hand-applied IAM JSON the owner applies per the no-hand-twin rule); growth (G-4 is a product decision — which weekday, one send or three — before any derivation test can pin the copy; G-9 is SES identity verification + three DNS records; the base A anchor also requires 'commercial option value real and measured', a market outcome no code state reaches); cost (#3373 kill switch in flight, owner-gated). INCOHERENT for an identical re-run, say so plainly: narrative — its A anchor is still worded 'one coherent cycle-6 story' and its 09-04 extension requires that 'the story the reset tells at reset time is STILL the story every scheduled writer tells at the first cron after it', a property observable ONLY by running a reset and waiting for the crons; a re-run on any non-reset day cannot grade it, and a re-run ON a reset day is the event that manufactures the P1 class. CPO and reader — their A clauses are pinned to 'Day 4 of a fresh reset' and 'a Day-0 countdown reads as a deliberate premiere'; the surface a re-run sees depends on the calendar, so 'identical' is impossible on a live experiment by construction. cto and observability — their A anchors still cite the historical '$85/mo envelope' (the artifact says so in its own extension_note), so the anchor text is stale before any code moves. What 'an identical re-run hits all A' would ACTUALLY require, in order: (1) freeze the 17 anchors in a versioned rubric file and forbid in-run extension (today SKILL.md:84-87 sanctions it and every lens used it); (2) rewrite full.md's bar (2) — as written, a run that confirms zero new same-class defects has failed, so 'all A' and 'a valid review' are mutually exclusive; (3) pick the day of cycle and accept that Day 0 and Day 6 are different platforms — run both, or stop calling it identical; (4) add M4's negative controls so a 17-A result can be distinguished from a blunted instrument (without them, given a constant ~5.8 findings/lens yield across three runs, a zero-finding run is more likely the instrument than the platform); (5) land the six class fixes and ~84 stories, ~20 of which collapse into the class fixes; (6) the owner acts on ADR-148, SES, the IAM JSON, the prereg publish, the send cadence, and the reset frequency — six decisions no session can take; (7) then expect the re-run to extend anchors again anyway, because a rubric that stops moving is a checklist, and this platform's whole thesis (ADR-104/105, the CHARTER's 'prove it can fail') is that a green checklist is the failure mode. The coherent target is not a letter: it is 'no P1 on Day 0 and Day 6 of the next two cycles, median silent-window under 7 days, instruments proven ≥ instruments added' — three numbers a nightly run can report and a review can only sample.

redteam.persona: ADR-104/105 rigor lead — N=1 statistician and honesty auditor. Test applied to every proposal: does the READER see something truer, or does a dashboard go green? A guard that passes while the published surface still lies is worth nothing.

class_verdicts.class_name: SDLC-A. The ungated landing path (direct pushes, reset pipeline, wrap commit meet only the format hook)
class_verdicts.reason: Real and verified: .git/hooks holds commit-msg + pre-commit only, deploy/agent_commit.sh has 0 pytest references, the PR template still says 'Targeted pytest for what I touched'. But from the honesty lens this class lies to the OPERATOR, not the reader — the one reader-facing member is principal-02 (the regenerated public prereg reds its own readers). Keep it as the merge target for ORACLE-4 and EM-1. Two modifications: (1) the hook must carry its own positive control — an uninstalled or --no-verify'd hook passes silently, the exact vacuous shape the review found 37 times; a test that asserts the hook is installed AND a fixture push with a planted premerge red is refused; (2) do not run 155s on every push (see over-engineering flag 2).
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Path-scoped hook: derived doc leg (docs_ci_gate_commands(), seconds) for docs-only commits; the premerge lane only when the diff touches lambdas/deploy/scripts/cdk/tests/site. Structural fix underneath: code goes through PRs where the lane already runs; direct push is reserved for docs/wrap. Negative control: a planted premerge red on a code diff is refused; a docs-only commit that breaks sync_doc_metadata --check is refused; a green tree pushes in <3 min.

class_verdicts.class_name: SDLC-B. Point-in-time verification of a surface scheduled writers keep rewriting (the reset verifies at t0, 104 schedules write at t+N)
class_verdicts.reason: This is THE P1 class (CPO-1, NARR-1, NARR-2, R1, G-1, G-2, QS-1 — six of seven P1s) and the correct merge target for EM-5, DA-C1, DA-C2 and ORACLE-4's time dimension. Three corrections from the honesty lens: (1) the served-surface contract must read the CDN-SERVED bytes, not S3 or DDB — restart_verify proved the manifest in S3 at t0 and the reader still got cycle 15; a check on the store is a check on a copy of the claim. (2) The proposed assertion 'newest posts.json/moments entry date >= genesis while day_n >= 0' is WRONG as written: pre-genesis 'Prologue · Part N' installments are sanctioned by design (card_engine.py:353, subscriber_onboarding_lambda.py:89 — CPO-5 is a bug precisely because the email drops that label), so the check would red the honest prologue and get waived (ORACLE-5's class). Correct form: every served pre-genesis entry carries the Prologue/prior-cycle label AND maps to a visible, non-tombstoned record. (3) The nightly leg's red routes into qa-smoke-failures, an alarm the citation gate keys by NAME (OBS-2/CTO-3 — lit since 09-03 under a citation for a different cause) — land CTO-3's `cause` dimension before the family grows or the new check becomes another muted red.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Same nightly qa_smoke leg (≈$0) but fetched through CloudFront, asserting labels not absence, emitting its check id as the failing dimension. Writer-side prevention stays FREE: wipe voids the drafts it tombstones (status→voided), _find_stale_drafts routes through the phase filter, CoOwned contract entries for chronicle/recap/habit_scores/RELATIONSHIP#state.

class_verdicts.class_name: SDLC-C. Instruments that cannot fail, closed on the merge (fail-soft paths, mocked transport, unreachable thresholds, closure contract that checks comment shape)
class_verdicts.reason: Correct class and the second-largest honesty leak: INT-1 (49 days), G-3 (28 days, public /api/status red '44d ago' while three chronicles shipped), OBS-1 (30+ days), CPO-2 (21 runs of kept=0) — each a public or operator surface reading false for weeks. Merge target for ORACLE-1, ORACLE-6, EM-2, EM-6. The modification: do NOT add requirements 7 and 8 to scripts/closure_contract.py while it is DEFAULT_MODE='warn' with a flip bar (10 clean wraps / 25 merges) that has never been met — more warn-mode findings is dashboard-greening, not honesty. Flip the ONE code `no-live-proof` to block now, with the #1480/#2254/#1956/#532 closing comments as its four positive controls (each must fail the rule today). The two FREE primitives that actually close the class are the IAM-parity SET test (module verbs/pk literals ⊆ role grants, generalised from tests/test_freshness_checker_iam_parity.py — INT-1 and G-3 must go red the day it lands) and ORACLE-1's per-entrant proof ratchet.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Detection without four MetricFilters: one Logs Insights query in the existing weekly drift sentinel over all /aws/lambda/life-platform-* groups for `AccessDenied|[Nn]on-fatal` in the trailing 7d, printed with function names (≈$0; Insights bills per GB scanned and the fleet logs KB–MB). Keep at most ONE runtime dead-man — CommitmentsDueCheckable>0 ∧ graded==0 — as a qa_smoke check line rather than a metric+alarm, because it measures the product criterion, not plumbing.

class_verdicts.class_name: SDLC-D. Guard the instance, not the set (scan set is a hand-picked subset, no positive control)
class_verdicts.reason: Verified and reader-relevant: DES-2 (type floor measured on 3 of 89 pages while the doc claims site-wide), DV-8 (radar plots the 50.0 placeholder as a vertex after #747 fixed four siblings), R2 (retired coaches on reader surfaces outside the cast guard's scan set), a11y-1/2 (contrast class fixed three times as instances). The two structural tests over tests/ (positive-control rule + scan-set-derives-from-a-registry rule) are the right primitive, and qa_manifest as the page denominator is the honest one. Merge target for ORACLE-3, EM-3, DA-C5. Keep EM-3's intake-stage `## Set` section in the issue-filer — it is the cheapest point in the workflow to force the denominator question. One caveat: the ~94-file allowlist is a residue ledger and is ORACLE-5's class unless it carries an owner and a burn-down (see over-engineering flag 3).

class_verdicts.class_name: SDLC-E. A second hand copy of a registry vocabulary / a literal restating a derived number on a reader-bound surface
class_verdicts.reason: The class conflates two audiences and only one of them is an honesty problem. READER-BOUND members (G-4 promise cadence, G-5 'Real CGM data' over a null feed, G-6 '19 sources' vs 20 vs 22, CPO-5 'Week 0', R5 '117-lb journey' vs 140, AIQ-4/6/8, COST-02/03/04, NARR-4 'as of 2026-08-02') are lies a stranger reads today; AGENT-BOUND members (DEVEX-5/7, CTO-4, INT-4, principal-03/07) mislead the next session. Split them: reader-bound gets the structural rule 'any n=<int>/<int> sources/<int>-lb/week label/date in a served string or template equals a numeric field in the same payload or a registry read' plus enrolment of email templates and OG cards in test_platform_stats_truth; agent-bound rides value-keyed (not phrase-keyed) check_doc_facts rules — DEVEX-5 is the fifth specimen of the #2959/#3003/#3199 phrase-keyed family. Merge ORACLE-7 and EM-4 here.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Priority order, not scope reduction: reader-bound first (served payload strings, templates, site copy, OG cards, config/*.json rendered publicly), agent-bound second. The G-6 fix requires an owner ruling on what 'curated 20' excludes — no guard can pick a semantic the platform never recorded.

class_verdicts.class_name: SDLC-F. Arithmetic no gate can see — shared chart builders and the statistics core ship with no contract test; ADR-105 is prose, not an emission contract
class_verdicts.reason: My home class and the analysts have it right, with DA-C4 merged in. Verified: survival() counts a censored 1–7-day cycle as a day-30 survivor (`cd is None`, :712) and serves a literal 'n=2' beside len(priors)=15 (:736/:741); brier_skill_score uses one pooled base rate (stats_core.py:822); calibration_core already refuses 'well-calibrated' without skill>0 (#1370) — so a label guard exists and reads a manufactured input, the purest form of 'the guard passes while the reader is lied to'; test_calibration_core_parity.py has zero strata fixtures; all 121 api_schemas pin TYPE, never that the method can produce the number. ADR-105 rule 1 has no executable owner in CONVENTIONS §9. Rename it 'the statistic and its caption have two authors'. Keep: the Node charts.js contract test, the method OBJECT built by the same function as the number, the all-censored fixture (p30 ≤ (reached+1)/(n+2)), the two-strata fixture, the claim-shape classifier ('approximately N on <date>' can never be directional), min_effect derived from trailing personal SD and written into the frozen artifact with n. Detection needs no rent — pure functions do not drift.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Enrol only the endpoints that serve a probability/skill/projection/composition (derived by grep over lambdas/web/site_api_*.py for p_*_pct|brier_skill|projected|confidence — ~6 endpoints), not all 121 schemas; everything else gets a literal-string lint on `"confidence":`/`"method":` keys (≥6 hand-typed confidence literals exist today in site_api_nutrition/sleep/rollups).

class_verdicts.class_name: ORACLE-1. Born unproven — a guard enters main with no synthetic must-fail case because the entry bar is an aggregate ceiling with headroom
class_verdicts.reason: The single best proposal across all four reports. BASELINE_UNPROVEN_GATES=541 against 536 live (#3536) means five guards can enter unproven for free; 37 of 99 findings are defects IN instruments; the review's own principal-05 was downgraded to PLAUSIBLE because this slack exists. Changing test_gate_census_lane_3000 from 'aggregate ≤ 541' to 'no gate id new since the committed baseline is unproven' honours owner decision #3329 (no retroactive programme) while closing the entrance. Its negative control is itself the vacuous-control lesson: today ONE new unproven id under the ceiling passes — that case must fail. FREE.

class_verdicts.class_name: ORACLE-2. Self-referential oracle — the guard's comparand is a copy of the claim (mock of the subject, threshold copied from another surface, hand-typed mirror of a workflow)
class_verdicts.reason: The diagnosis is right (INT-1's FakeDdbTable, CTO-2's threshold copied from slo-mcp-availability onto a surface seeing ~8 requests/week, COST-03's test pinning a false disclaimer, DEVEX-4's regex mirror of a YAML path filter). Keep the two proposals that put a REAL wire or a REAL distribution behind the oracle: IAM-parity as a set (every LeadingKeys role) and threshold-comparand derivation (every Errors alarm carries a derivation token or a dated exemption — the #3474 discipline applied to the set). Drop the AST 'mock-of-subject detector' to a census lead: it is a heuristic over legitimate test technique (mocking the transport is correct when the wire is contract-tested elsewhere) and will mint a residue ledger of false positives — its own class 5.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: The two parity tests plus COST-03's rule stated structurally: a test that asserts a disclaimer must assert the CONDITION the disclaimer claims (a sibling assertion that the EstimatedCostUSD{LambdaFunction} series does/does not exist), never the wording.

class_verdicts.class_name: ORACLE-3. Instance-scoped guard — the fix lands on the specimen and the set is enumerated by hand
class_verdicts.reason: Same class as SDLC-D with the same members (INT-3, a11y-1/2, DV-8, AIQ-1, SEC-1/2, R2, DES-2/4, OBS-8, CTO-5, DA-2). Its distinctive contribution — closure rule 7 `set-named` — is a closure-stage version of EM-3's intake-stage `## Set` section; intake is cheaper and earlier, and closure_contract is warn-mode anyway.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: EM-3's `## Set` section + check_backlog_hygiene lint at filing time.

class_verdicts.class_name: ORACLE-4. Subset-of-the-gate on the landing path; verification point-in-time while writers run later
class_verdicts.reason: Two classes stapled together: the stand-in-derives-from-the-workflow half (DEVEX-1/2/3, principal-01/02) belongs to SDLC-A; the 'restart_verify has no time dimension' half (G-1, NARR-1, R1, CPO-1) belongs to SDLC-B. Keep its concrete pieces: ci_gate_commands(workflow) generalised from docs_ci_gate_commands(), and the test that ENUMERATES every stand-in (any module under scripts/ or deploy/ that names a workflow job or calls git push) so a new stand-in is enrolled or red — that enumeration is the set-guard the #3477 sweep itself lacked (it was widened twice by hand, #3479 and #3531).

class_verdicts.class_name: ORACLE-5. A waiver outlives its condition — citations, exemptions, chronic warns and debt baselines checked for existence and date, never re-derived against the condition they claim
class_verdicts.reason: Deserves its own class and the SDLC and EM analysts were wrong to fold it into C/6. The acknowledgement layer is where reader-honesty dies quietly: the a11y ledger's stale-in-the-good-direction entries DISARM serious-rule gating on the pages that carry debt (a11y-3), a citation written 09-01 for a cured cause kept the wrap gate green over a NEW reader-truth failure lit 09-03 (CTO-3/OBS-2 — alarm_citations.json has 20 entries and no `cause` field, verified), chronic=True warns are a permanent waiver (OBS-1). And it is RECURSIVE: every allowlist and shrink-only residue ledger the other 25 proposals create (conformance_residue 35 entries, pair_seam_residue ~285 rows, the ~94-file positive-control allowlist) is this class the day it lands unless it carries an owner and an expiry. The rule for CONVENTIONS §9 — a waiver is a claim with a CONDITION and an EXPIRY, and the gate re-derives the condition — must apply to the new ledgers as a condition of landing them.

class_verdicts.class_name: ORACLE-6. Closed on merge, not on first real output
class_verdicts.reason: Identical members to SDLC-C's core (OBS-1, G-3, INT-1, CPO-2) plus fast-follows never ticketed (INT-3, a11y-3, DEVEX-8). Its charter-rule-4 amendment ('every scheduled thing AND every fail-soft path gets a dead-man at birth') is the right sentence; its STANDING_RENT detection (~$0.80/mo of filters + metrics + alarms) is the third analyst proposing the same rent — see the cheaper alternative under SDLC-C.

class_verdicts.class_name: ORACLE-7. Vocabulary copies outside the conformance guard's vocabularies and roots
class_verdicts.reason: Same class as SDLC-E with the same members (AIQ-4/6/8, CPO-5, G-4/6, R5, COST-02, DV-1). Two pieces survive on their own merit: the Decimal-coercion AST guard (DA-1 is an honesty defect — a nudge that was SENT has no record and its ledger row says 'attempting' forever, so the platform's own memory of what it told the owner is false), and the observation that /new-machinery is invoked for 'durable machinery', never for a template or endpoint that restates a fact — the paved road has no on-ramp for consumers.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Reader-bound surfaces first; tests/scripts/deploy hand-lists via SDLC-D's positive-control rule rather than a vocabulary sweep with a residue ledger.

class_verdicts.class_name: EM-1. The ungated landing path — agent sessions and the reset pipeline push straight to main
class_verdicts.reason: Same class as SDLC-A with the sharpest measurement (302 of 613 commits since 08-22 direct, 179 code-touching). Its detection — a wrap-battery gh read counting direct-push red Unit-Test runs — is the FREE version of the SDLC analyst's sentinel leg and is the one to keep.

class_verdicts.class_name: EM-2. Closure on merge, not on live effect — fail-soft instruments ship dead and read CLOSED
class_verdicts.reason: Same class as SDLC-C; this analyst's version is the one to implement: flip ONLY the `no-live-proof` code to block ('the one code whose false-positive cost is a reopened issue, never a lost fix'). Its measurement — 289 closed since 08-22, median 9.0h open→close, 186/229 inside 24h — explains why 'first real run' is structurally after the close. Its per-function MetricFilter rent (~$0.40/mo) is the fourth proposal of the same rent.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Same as SDLC-C.

class_verdicts.class_name: EM-3. Instance fixed, set never swept — the issue is scoped to the specimen and the implementer never enumerates the class
class_verdicts.reason: Same class as SDLC-D but at the INTAKE stage, which is the cheapest place to intervene: the `## Set` section (enumeration query + member count) in .claude/agents/issue-filer.md, the hygiene lint, and worktree-implementer step 6b (paste the member list into the PR body). Its ADR-099 observation (Effort in the denominator makes the 9-hour instance fix outrank the class sweep) is a real scoring defect the owner should hear.

class_verdicts.class_name: EM-4. Hand-typed mirrors of a fact the platform already owns — prose, comments, fixtures, local restatements of CI's step set
class_verdicts.reason: Same class as SDLC-E's agent-bound half plus ORACLE-4's stand-ins. Keep one piece verbatim: 'any number in the CLAUDE.md status block that a doc-facts rule owns is emitted by sync_doc_metadata --render-status and pasted, never typed' — the wrap is the platform's largest prose writer (83 direct docs commits in 14 days) and DEVEX-5 (MEMORY.md 'genesis 2026-09-04' against constants 09-05) is exactly a typed number.

class_verdicts.class_name: EM-5. Reset-time verification is a snapshot; scheduled writers re-populate what the reset emptied; provenance stamped from a constant
class_verdicts.reason: Same class as SDLC-B (with DA-C1/C2/C3 members). Its observation that every prior review ran on Day 1–6 and 09-05 was the FIRST ever on Day 0 — between the reset and its first scheduled writers — is the single most important sentence in the four reports for the '70' question. Its prevention list is SDLC-B's; its T+writers re-run as a new scheduled Actions workflow is over-engineering flag 6.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Fold the T+writers re-verify into the existing daily standalone visual-qa fire with a day_n ≤ 2 branch — no new schedule, no new cron-freshness registry row.

class_verdicts.class_name: EM-6. Instruments that report green without measuring — guards without a control, acknowledgement layers without a staleness rule
class_verdicts.reason: Two classes: the 'guards without a control' half is SDLC-C/ORACLE-1 (AIQ-2, OBS-1, CTO-2, CPO-2, DEVEX-1/6), the 'acknowledgement without staleness' half is ORACLE-5 (OBS-2, CTO-3, OBS-3, a11y-3/6). Keep its enforcement: the census's unproven / vacuous-empty / swallowed-exit counters (597 gates, 50 proven, 49 vacuous, 33 swallowed) as CI ratchets — 'the ONE place the six-session lesson becomes enforcement'. Its NewInteriorGapCount rent (~$0.20/mo) is acceptable ONLY with its stated demote trigger, and OBS-5's owner-writable expected-absence marker is the cheaper honest alternative.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: Expected-absence marker written via MCP (same DDB shape as the sick-day suppress), honoured by the checker: $0, and it makes the operator's acknowledgement part of the RECORD rather than a citation beside it.

class_verdicts.class_name: EM-7. Review cadence as intake — grades carried forward across resets, delta selects rows by diff instead of by event
class_verdicts.reason: The diagnosis is correct and statistically important: 8 of 17 lenses were last graded from scratch on 07-28/08-02; 'grades stand' for five weeks and ~600 commits; the 08-27 delta was held; and every one of the 17 anchors was EXTENDED on the day, so '13 dropped' is confounded by a raised bar on a never-observed surface. Keep: the 28-day carry-forward cap (a dead-man on the grade's age) and day-of-cycle stamping in the artifact. Modify: the 'run the 8 reset-touching rows on every delta that contains a reset' rule is rent — resets are weekly (12 in 55 days), so it makes every delta a near-full review, and the review's own cost lens found 63% of August's stamped AI spend was ci+dev. Also missing: the rubric decision that an 'identical re-run' FREEZES the anchors — without it the goal in the owner's framing is unmeasurable.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: One Day-0 sample of the 8 reset-touching rows per GENESIS (not per delta), the 28-day carry cap, and an explicit 'anchors frozen for the re-run' flag in full.md. If resets stay weekly the honest fix is fewer resets, not more reviews.

class_verdicts.class_name: DA-C1. Scheduled writers select by status/timestamp and never by the wipe's stamp (the reset→writer contract does not exist)
class_verdicts.reason: The writer-side prevention of SDLC-B and the best-evidenced version of it: with_phase_filter in 76 files vs experiment_stamp in 14 / tag_record in 15 of 112 writer files; #2119's guard scoped to COACH#/ENSEMBLE# put_item only; 31 writer seams on EXPERIMENT_SCOPED partitions parked in pair_seam_residue with no countdown. Keep all three fixes (taxonomy-derived writer set guard seeded from the residue as a shrink baseline; wipe voids drafts; CoOwned registry entries). Its nightly census (~40 key-bounded queries inside qa_smoke, ≈$0) is fine with its demote trigger, subject to SDLC-B's `cause`-dimension precondition.

class_verdicts.class_name: DA-C2. The reset verifies the READ side once, at T0, and defers the WRITE side to an attended runlist nobody is obliged to run
class_verdicts.reason: Merges into SDLC-B, but ELEVATE one proposal to a named primitive: the per-step WORK CONTRACT — every restart_* step reports {input_count, acted_count, skipped_count} and the pipeline reds when input>0 ∧ acted==0 without a named reason. archive_one reported html_files_total=29 / archived=0 / already_archived=29 and PASSED on 09-04 (NARR-5); that is a dead-man on a step's OUTPUT, the cheapest new primitive in all four reports and one the charter's rule 4 ('did the job run') never asked. Also correct PROPORTIONALITY row 86: the sweep 'runs once per RESET, which is a few times a quarter' — CYCLE_GENESES shows 12 resets in 55 days; a subsystem priced at the wrong cadence cannot have an honest demote trigger.

class_verdicts.class_name: DA-C3. Write-time provenance and rendered tense come from a constant/SSM, not the event's own date — the pre-start window is not a phase the registry knows
class_verdicts.reason: KEEP as a distinct class — it is the one place a missing REGISTRY VALUE (PRESTART, or date-derived pilot) closes ~10 findings at once (QS-1, DA-7, AIQ-3/6/8, NARR-3, CPO-3/4, DV-4/5); experiment_stamp() returns EXPERIMENT_PHASE_CURRENT unconditionally (phase_taxonomy.py:60-76, verified) and the reset bumps SSM before genesis. One ADR-105 correction: 'refuse gradeable PREDICTION# writes while pre_start' is fine for FUTURE writes, but rule 2 says every emitted bet is graded or explicitly VOIDED ON THE RECORD — the 10 of 24 unsealed cycle-16 rows served today must be visibly marked unsealed or voided with a reason, never quietly filtered; a season⊆frozen contract that hides the residue is a greener dashboard over a rewritten ledger.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: experiment_stamp(as_of=…) derives phase from as_of >= EXPERIMENT_START_DATE (one function, all writers) + a `sealed: bool` field on every served season row (the extension anchor's own wording) + the season⊆frozen contract in CI. All FREE.

class_verdicts.class_name: DA-C4. Served statistics whose caption/method/label is a second hand-typed writer beside the computation
class_verdicts.reason: Same class as SDLC-F, and this analyst names the mechanism I care most about: the reset FREQUENCY leaks into a statistic — seven re-anchored 1–7-day cycles counted as day-30 survivors, so the more the platform resets the more confident the 47% becomes. Its 'method OBJECT built by the same function as the number, captions render from the object' is the correct executable form of ADR-105 rule 1; its live-payload rule ('n=<int>' in a served string must equal a numeric field) is the FREE detector.

class_verdicts.class_name: DA-C5. The reset tools enumerate from hand-typed lists where the registry rules per row/prefix
class_verdicts.reason: A member of SDLC-D with the sharpest specimen: assert_registry_coverage and its CI twin compare two copies of the same hand list (OPERATIONAL_COACH_IDS), so COACH#nudge_ledger / COACH#outbound_ledger are wipeable on paper and survived three resets (DA-2), and 26 CROSS_PHASE rows still carry a cycle-12 tombstone with no reconcile (DA-9). Keep the census artifact (deploy/generated/pk_family_census.json from restart_pipeline step 0) as the derived denominator every reset tool and the SCHEMA.md rule read. The DA-9 reconcile is an OWNER ACT (a DDB write).

class_verdicts.class_name: DA-C6. Derived artifacts (S3 pages, share kits, OG cards, static catalogs, proof stamps) sit outside the taxonomy so the wipe cannot reach them
class_verdicts.reason: KEEP as a distinct registry gap — ADR-077 governs rows and G-1 shows the slug-keyed archive has archived nothing since cycle 4 (2026-07-10). But the proposed fix 'ALWAYS tombstone-overwrite + 301 any live week-NN absent from posts.json' collides with #3512, which already made prior-cycle permalinks carry archive notices — an honest, sanctioned state. Purge is not the only honest state; a labelled archive is honest too, and for a reader a 301 to nowhere is LESS informative than a page that says 'this is cycle 14's article'. The DERIVED_ARTIFACTS registry should decide per artifact (archive-with-notice vs purge) and the served assertion should verify the LABEL, not the absence.
class_verdicts.cheaper_alternative: archive_one keyed on (slug, cycle) + the work contract from DA-C2 (acted==0 on a cycle with published content is red) + a served check that every 200 under /journal/posts/week-NN/ is either in posts.json or carries the #3512 notice + evidence_as_of/evidence_cycle required on any digit-bearing catalog entry. All FREE.

missing_classes.name: M1. The honesty label is itself a literal — self-certifying disclaimers, confidence strings, method captions and 'verified' notes hand-typed beside the thing they describe
missing_classes.evidence: ADR-105 rule 1 permits an explicit 'descriptive only' tag in place of uncertainty+n; the platform used that escape as a fig leaf: survival() serves a 47% hero with method 'n=2 is narrative, not statistics' beside len(priors)=15 (site_api_rollups.py:736/:741) — the honesty marker is the wrong number. The same pattern is everywhere a label was supposed to make a number honest: ≥6 hand-typed `"confidence": "…"` literals in served endpoints (site_api_nutrition.py:179/:420, site_api_sleep.py:229/:429/:439, rollups:741); /api/receipts' disclaimer states a reason that was never true (COST-03); the prereg says 'grounded in the plan' over literal min_effect thresholds (QS-5); og-glucose asserts 'Real CGM data. Updated daily.' over a null feed (G-5); the visceral gauge's aria-label asserts a 0–3 scale for a 3.2 lb datum (DV-7); data_phase is a constant 'established' (AIQ-8); the coaching read tab says 'the coaches read only this run's data' while the next tab serves Day-0 reads (NARR-3); the intro card says 'no page jumps' on the page that jumps (DES-1); DESIGN_SYSTEM_V5 §10.5 claims the floor site-wide over a 3-page gate (DES-2); alarm_citations says 'CURED and PROVEN LIVE' about a different cause (CTO-3/OBS-2); PROPORTIONALITY row 153 says 'declined build, $0' about an instrument that was built and is dark (CPO-2). None of the four analysts names this: the platform's honesty apparatus (ADR-104/105 labels, disclaimers, citations, 'Verified' stamps) is prose, and prose was hand-typed, so in ~12 findings the honesty marker IS the lie. Missing primitive: derivation guard on the LABEL — a disclaimer/confidence/method string must be emitted by the same function that computes the number, and the contract test is 'mutate the input, the label must move' (DV-1's own positive control generalised); a structural lint that `"confidence":`/`"method":`/`as of`/`verified` values are never string literals in lambdas/web. Stage: implement. Cost: FREE. Negative control: the live 'n=2' string fails today; a computed label passes; a literal label anywhere in lambdas/web reds.

missing_classes.name: M2. Reset-induced censoring counted as an outcome — no statistic on the platform models right-censoring although the reset (12 in 55 days) is the modal terminator of every window
missing_classes.evidence: CYCLE_GENESES (site_api_data.py:103-125) records 12 resets between 2026-07-12 and 2026-09-05 — the median cycle is ~5 days — while PROPORTIONALITY row 86 prices the reset as 'a few times a quarter'. Every duration or completion statistic therefore has a censoring problem that nothing models: survival() counts a cycle re-anchored at day 3 as a day-30 survivor (`cd is None`, :712) so p30 RISES with reset frequency; CPO-2's corrected cause (b) says no live-metric commitment has EVER reached its 7–90-day due date because resets tombstone them first (cycles 13/14/15 lasted 15/15/3 days) — the behavior-change instrument cannot grade by construction under this cadence; QS-1's directional bets carry 14-day windows opening on Day 0 of a regime whose cycles last 1–7 days; DV-5 fabricates zeros in a genesis-clamped window; a11y-3's ledger reads /data/training/ as 'fixed' when the fix is Day-0 emptiness; G-8's pendings can never convert and contaminate the funnel ratio; QS-5's arm floor (5 lag-1 pairs) is unreachable at 14 weigh-ins in 65 days. The analysts treat these as instances of F/C4 (arithmetic) or B (reset); the class is an ADR-104 absence rule applied to TIME: a window that outlasts the median cycle is not gradeable and must say so at emission, and a censored observation is never a success. Missing primitive: REGISTRY — the cycle archive's window_days is already the censoring record; every duration/completion statistic must consume it (Kaplan–Meier or 'censored excluded, n stated'), and ADR-105 rule 4 gains the corollary 'no threshold or window longer than the trailing median cycle length without a declared censoring rule'. Stage: design. Cost: FREE. Negative control: an all-censored fixture must not raise p30 above the Laplace prior (fails today at 47%); a 14-day commitment emitted on a 5-day-median regime must be born 'ungradeable at this cadence', not 'pending'. This is also the class where no code reaches A: only the owner's reset cadence does.

missing_classes.name: M3. The integrity seal protects a falsehood — the frozen pre-registration is content-addressed (hash-verified) but never truth-verified at freeze
missing_classes.evidence: The platform's credibility moat is the sealed prereg, and the memory rule 'Frozen prereg is STAMPED — fix the test, not the seal' (#3483) makes its content permanent by design. Five findings show the seal freezing something wrong or incomplete with no gate BEFORE the hash: Prologue III presents 326.24 lb as the starting weight against baseline 324.64 on the third reset (CTO-3, the closed #1985 class recurring); 10 of 24 served cycle-16 predictions are not in the frozen artifact and nothing on the wire says so (QS-1); confirmation_criteria is served null and min_effect is a literal inside a 'grounded' artifact (QS-5); the seed's hand-typed COACHES seals a retired and a non-operational coach into cycle 16 (R2 — 'needed before the seal because a sealed prereg cannot be edited'); the regen reds its own reader tests at every reset because they run outside the regeneration's gate (principal-02). The analysts scatter these across C3, D and E; none names the mechanism: a hash gate is an integrity primitive and it was mistaken for a truth primitive, so the one artifact readers are told to trust most is the one whose content is checked least. Missing primitive: CONTRACT TEST at FREEZE time between the artifact's claims and their registries (baseline == constants, every coach_name ∈ persona_registry operational set, min_effect derived with {metric, sd, n}, season ids ⊆ artifact) — run before sealing and refusing to seal on red; a wrong seal already published gets a visible amendment record (ADR-105 rule 2 'on the record'), never an edit. Stage: reset. Cost: FREE. Negative control: a seed naming 'Dr. Sarah Chen' or a baseline ≠ EXPERIMENT_BASELINE must refuse to seal; today's cycle-16 artifact fails on two counts.

missing_classes.name: M4. A fail-closed gate downstream of a lossy transformation — the registry facet that would license the honest sentence is destroyed before the gate can read it
missing_classes.evidence: ADR-104's #3268 amendment is explicit ('a paused or stale source is not an absent one … sourced_availability deletes the unlicensed answer before a prompt is built — fail-closed') and the grounded-generation gate is armed on the coach surfaces — yet Garmin (paused, ADR-074) reaches the reader as 'isn't syncing to my dashboard yet' (R4, NARR-3, AIQ-4) because coach_brief_input_gate's build_inventory collapses paused/lag facets to a binary BEFORE the prompt, so the fail-closed rule sees 'not available' and licenses a story. INT-2 is the same shape in a classifier (restart_integration_check reads capture_channel, a proxy, instead of the `behavioral` facet that carries the meaning) and INT-5 in the facet enum (the Dropbox CSV path is not a capture_channel, so the honesty chip keyed on the facet skips the one manual source dark 72 days). The analysts file these under E/ORACLE-7 (vocabulary copy) and DA-C3, which misses the point that the gate EXISTS and is fail-closed and the lie ships anyway. Missing primitive: the derivation guard must sit at the LOSSY boundary (the prompt builder / classifier input), not at the output gate — a derivation test that every registry facet a downstream rule keys on (paused, stale_hours, behavioral, capture_channel) survives to the gate's input unchanged. Stage: implement. Cost: FREE. Negative control: a registry source with paused=True must render 'PAUSED (ADR-074) — cannot report; not a sync problem' in build_inventory output (fails today); the grounded gate must hard-fail 'not syncing yet' for a paused source (fails today — it passed at quality 92).

over_engineering_flags.proposal: Per-function CloudWatch Logs MetricFilters on level=ERROR for freshness-checker / chronicle-email-sender / coach-nudge / qa-smoke plus CommitmentsGraded + CommitmentsDueCheckable metrics and 2–3 alarms (proposed independently by all four analysts)
over_engineering_flags.why: Four reports converge on the same ~$0.40–0.80/mo, but dollars are not the rent that bites here: each new alarm is another entry the citation ledger must acknowledge by NAME, and the review just showed that layer is the weak one (OBS-2/CTO-3: a citation for a cured cause kept the gate green over a new failure; OBS-3: a needs-human line renewed 93×). Two of the four functions (INT-1, G-3) are closed at CI time by the IAM-parity set test, making the runtime filter redundant for the IAM-denial sub-class the day it lands — the SDLC analyst's own demote trigger says so.
over_engineering_flags.rent_if_kept: ~$0.40–0.80/mo CloudWatch + 4–6 new alarm names in docs/alarm_citations.json (attention rent, unpriced by any of the four)
over_engineering_flags.alternative: One Logs Insights query in the EXISTING weekly drift sentinel (GET-only) over all /aws/lambda/life-platform-* groups for `AccessDenied|[Nn]on-fatal` in the trailing 7d, printed with function names — ≈$0 (Insights bills ~$0.005/GB scanned; the fleet logs KB–MB), covers every function not four, no alarm name to cite. Keep exactly one runtime dead-man as a qa_smoke check line: CommitmentsDueCheckable>0 ∧ graded==0 — it measures the product criterion. Demote trigger inherited from the sentinel: retire the leg when the IAM-parity set test has been green for 90 days and the query returns 0 for 8 consecutive weeks.

over_engineering_flags.proposal: A pre-push hook running the full premerge lane (~155s) on every push whose upstream is main
over_engineering_flags.why: $0 in AWS but 146 non-bot direct pushes in 14 days × 155s ≈ 6.3 hours of session wall-clock per fortnight, on the platform's scarcest resource (Opus session time; PROPORTIONALITY's own 'mind' column). 83 of those 146 pushes were docs-only and need the doc leg, not pytest.
over_engineering_flags.rent_if_kept: ~6h/fortnight of session time; $0 AWS
over_engineering_flags.alternative: Path-scoped hook: derived doc leg (seconds) for docs-only diffs, the premerge lane only when the diff touches lambdas/deploy/scripts/cdk/tests/site (179 of 302 direct pushes), and the derived artifact-reader set only when deploy/generated/** changed. Underneath: code lands via PR (where the lane already runs); direct push is reserved for docs/wrap. The hook stays as a backstop with its own installed-and-can-refuse positive control.

over_engineering_flags.proposal: Extending tests/test_conformance_guard_2844.py's vocabularies (genesis/cycle/day literals, platform counts, cadences, roster, phase labels) and roots (config/, deploy/, site/assets/js/, email templates, tests/js, tests/, scripts/) with every pre-existing hit parked in a dated shrink-only residue ledger
over_engineering_flags.why: This is ORACLE-5's class applied to its own proposal: conformance_residue already holds 35 entries and pair_seam_residue ~285 rows with no countdown; a vocabulary sweep this wide will mint hundreds more, and a residue ledger without an owner and an expiry is the a11y ledger (a11y-3/6 — 'accepted debt indefinitely because nothing requires an entry to name an issue'). The reader is not made more honest by a bigger allowlist.
over_engineering_flags.rent_if_kept: $0 AWS; a residue ledger that becomes permanent debt and disarms the guard on exactly the surfaces that carry drift
over_engineering_flags.alternative: Reader-bound surfaces first and structurally (served payload strings, templates, site copy, OG cards, publicly rendered config/*.json) via the 'served literal equals a field in the same payload / a registry read' rule; agent-bound hand-lists in tests/scripts/deploy via SDLC-D's positive-control rule; every residue ledger ships with an `issue` field per entry and a burn-down date, or it is not a ratchet.

over_engineering_flags.proposal: Closure-contract requirements 7 (`set-named`) and 8 (`first-live-output`) added to scripts/closure_contract.py, flip 'measured per FLIP_BAR'
over_engineering_flags.why: closure_contract.py is DEFAULT_MODE='warn' (verified) with a flip bar of 10 consecutive clean wraps / 25 merges that has never been met; adding two more requirements to a contract nothing blocks on produces more findings nobody must act on — a greener-looking process over the same closures. #3477 closed 'realized' and its class recurred the same afternoon under the existing six rules.
over_engineering_flags.rent_if_kept: $0; more warn-mode noise that trains the reader to skip the closure sweep (the OBS-3 mechanism applied to /wrap)
over_engineering_flags.alternative: Flip ONE code — `no-live-proof` — to block now (EM-2's version), with the #1480/#2254/#1956/#532 closing comments as its four positive controls (each must fail today), and leave the other rules in warn. The set question moves to intake (EM-3's `## Set` section + hygiene lint), which is earlier and cheaper than closure.

over_engineering_flags.proposal: ADR-105 as an emission contract on EVERY served statistic object ({n, method, ci|uncertainty}) across the api_schemas contract (121 schemas)
over_engineering_flags.why: Right primitive, wrong scope: enrolling 121 shape schemas is a large PR that will land as a shape-only field (`method: string`) — exactly what api_calibration.json already does for brier_skill (type pinned, derivation never). The honesty gain is concentrated in the handful of endpoints that serve a probability, skill, projection or composition percentage.
over_engineering_flags.rent_if_kept: $0; schema sprawl and a large enrolment PR whose fields will be typed as strings
over_engineering_flags.alternative: Derive the enrolment set from code (grep lambdas/web/site_api_*.py for p_*_pct|brier_skill|projected|confidence — ~15 files, ~6 endpoints) and require the method OBJECT only there, built by the same function as the number; everywhere else a literal-string lint on `"confidence":`/`"method":` values (the M1 class rule). Negative control: mutate priors 2→3 and the served n must move (fails today).

over_engineering_flags.proposal: A new scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (restart-reverify.yml) that re-runs restart_verify's served checks at T+writers after every reset
over_engineering_flags.why: Free minutes on a public repo, but one more scheduled workflow is one more scheduled_workflow_registry row with a hand-set grace — the DEVEX-8 class ('a measured threshold whose basis is a snapshot') — and one more producer the cron-freshness check can rule 'late' on an ordinary GitHub scheduler delay (median gap 211 min, max 729 min measured).
